# Loui DS: full documentation

> Loui DS is a dark, minimal, functional React design system (React 19, React Aria Components, CSS Modules, DTCG tokens) for internal tools, dashboards and apps. It is built to be operated by humans and AI agents.

Rules for generated UI:

- Use only components, hooks and tokens exported by the package; never write raw colors, px sizes, z-indexes or inline styles.
- One primary action per screen (`Button variant="primary"`), top right. The accent blue is for focus, selection and links only.
- Hierarchy comes from surface plus border; shadows only on overlays.
- Color never carries meaning alone: pair it with text or an icon with a name.
- Every interactive element needs an accessible name; icon-only controls require a `label`.
- Microcopy: English, sentence case, buttons are verb + object, no exclamation marks, no emoji. See content-rules.json.
- No user-visible string literals in components: use the message catalog and `DSProvider`.
- Money is integer minor units plus an ISO 4217 code; format dates, numbers and money with the provided utilities.
- Do not use `experimental` or `deprecated` components in recipes or generated code unless the user asks.

---

## Getting started

Browse every component live in Storybook: <https://xrazai.github.io/loUI/>. AI tools can load <https://xrazai.github.io/loUI/llms.txt> (see [Using with AI](./using-with-ai.md)).

### Requirements

- React 19 and React DOM 19 (peer dependencies). React 18 is not supported.
- An evergreen browser. Node 24 or later for tooling.
- A bundler that handles CSS imports and `woff2` assets (Vite, Next.js, webpack, esbuild).

### Install

```sh
pnpm add loui-ds react react-dom
```

`npm install loui-ds` and `yarn add loui-ds` work too. To upgrade, run `pnpm update loui-ds` and read the [release notes](https://github.com/xrazai/loUI/releases) first: before 1.0 a minor version may break. Every release also attaches the package tarball, if you need to install a version by URL.

`react-aria-components`, `react-stately` and `lucide-react` are regular dependencies of the package; you do not install them yourself.

### 1. Load the stylesheet once

Import the stylesheet once, at the root of your app, before any component renders:

```tsx
import 'loui-ds/styles.css';
```

It contains, in this layer order, `reset`, `tokens`, `base`, `components` and `utilities`. Because everything sits in named cascade layers, your own unlayered CSS always wins over the design system without specificity tricks.

The stylesheet sets the dark theme on the page (`bg-canvas` on `html`, `bg` and `text` on `body`, the Geist font), so you normally do not need your own reset.

### 2. Wrap the app in `DSProvider`

```tsx
import { DSProvider } from 'loui-ds';

export function Root({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <DSProvider locale="en-US">{children}</DSProvider>;
}
```

| Prop       | Purpose                                                                                                          |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locale`   | BCP 47 tag. Drives messages, number and date formatting, sorting, and the direction (RTL) of React Aria widgets. |
| `messages` | Overrides keyed by component, e.g. `{ Alert: { dismiss: 'Close' } }`. Applied over the built-in catalogs.        |
| `navigate` | Client-side navigation for `Link` and link-like components (your router's `navigate`).                           |
| `useHref`  | Maps a router path to a real `href` (needed for basename routing).                                               |

Without a provider everything still works in `en-US`; it just does not follow the user's locale. English is the default and `pt-BR` ships with the library. See `docs/architecture/i18n.md` for how messages resolve.

Client-side routing, for example with React Router:

```tsx
import { useNavigate, useHref } from 'react-router';

function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  return (
    <DSProvider navigate={navigate} useHref={useHref}>
      {children}
    </DSProvider>
  );
}
```

### 3. Use components

```tsx
import { Alert, Button } from 'loui-ds';

export function Example() {
  return (
    <>
      <Alert tone="warning" title="Low stock">
        3 boxes of notebooks are left. Reorder to avoid delays.
      </Alert>
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={() => console.log('created')}>
        Create order
      </Button>
    </>
  );
}
```

Use `onPress`, not `onClick`: it is the React Aria press event and works for mouse, touch, keyboard and screen readers.

### Fonts

Geist (UI) and Geist Mono (data) are self-hosted and ship inside the package: `styles.css` references `./fonts/*.woff2` relative to itself, and the build copies them to `dist/fonts`. Nothing is fetched from Google Fonts or a CDN at runtime. Your bundler resolves the font files when it processes `loui-ds/styles.css`; there is nothing to configure. Both families load with `font-display: swap` and a metric-matched fallback so the layout does not shift.

### Theming

Dark is the only theme. The semantic token layer (`--ds-bg`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, ...) can be overridden in your own CSS if you must; component code only reads semantic tokens. A `[data-theme="paper"]` scope provides the light surface for receipt and PDF previews. Forced-colors and reduced-motion modes are handled by the components.

### Server-side rendering

- Components never touch `window` or `document` while rendering or at import time, so they render on the server.
- IDs come from React `useId`; React Aria needs no `SSRProvider` with React 19.
- `useMediaQuery` returns its `defaultValue` (`false`) on the server and corrects after hydration. Prefer CSS media queries for styling.
- Import `loui-ds/styles.css` in the root layout so the first paint is already styled.

### Framework notes

**Vite.** Import the stylesheet in `main.tsx`; nothing else is needed.

**Next.js (App Router).** See [SSR and Next.js](#ssr-and-nextjs) below.

### SSR and Next.js

The package ships a `"use client"` directive **per module**: every file that uses hooks, React context or React Aria has it, and the entry points (`index.js`) and pure helpers do not. So a React Server Component (the default in the Next.js App Router) can import the design system directly, with no wrapper file:

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx (Server Component)
import 'loui-ds/styles.css';
import { DSProvider, ToastRegion } from 'loui-ds';

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <DSProvider locale="en-US">
          {children}
          <ToastRegion />
        </DSProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/page.tsx (Server Component): components are client references and render on the server too
import { Button, DataTable } from 'loui-ds';
```

Rules that follow from the React Server Components model, not from the library:

- Props that cross from a Server to a Client Component must be serializable. **Functions cannot**: `onPress`, `onChange`, render props such as `DataTable` column `render` or `Dialog` `footer={({ close }) => ...}`, and component values such as an `icon` prop. Put those in a file that starts with `'use client'` (a small component per interaction, see `examples/next-app/app/CreateOrderButton.tsx`).
- `DSProvider` takes plain props (`locale`, `messages`) and works in a Server layout; `navigate` and `useHref` are functions, so wrap the provider in a client component when you use client-side routing.
- Hooks (`useHotkeys`, `useToast`, ...) and the `toast` API only work in Client Components.
- Import the stylesheet once in the root layout. `dist/styles.css` and the Geist fonts need no `transpilePackages` or other `next.config` settings.

`sideEffects` in `package.json` lists only `**/*.css`, so bundlers drop unused components (importing `Button` alone costs about 12 kB brotli, enforced by `pnpm size` and `pnpm test:treeshake`). The packaging is verified on every pull request by building `examples/vite-app` and `examples/next-app` (Next.js 16, App Router, Turbopack) against a packed tarball: `pnpm examples:verify`.

### Next steps

- Read the [Principles](./principles.md) and the [Content guidelines](./content-guidelines.md) before building a screen.
- Browse the components in Storybook; each page lists props, variants, states and accessibility notes.
- Agents: start from [Using with AI](./using-with-ai.md).

---

## Principles

These rules apply to every screen built with Loui DS. They are short on purpose. When a case is not covered, choose the option that keeps the user's attention on one thing.

### Three rules

1. **One accent.** The blue accent (`--ds-accent`) is only for focus, selection, links and "open" states. Never use it for buttons or large fills.
2. **Ink for action.** The primary button is light on dark (`--ds-primary-bg`). Use **one primary action per screen**.
3. **Borders first.** Hierarchy comes from surface plus border. Shadows only on overlays: menus, toasts, dialogs and sheets.

### Clarity and focus

The system is designed for use that needs no effort of attention (the first product's owner has ADHD). Every new screen follows these rules.

1. **One main action per screen,** always at the top right, with a keyboard shortcut.
2. **The most important thing comes first and is largest.** Everything else is secondary text (`--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`).
3. **Color only carries meaning, and is always accompanied by text.** Never signal status by color alone.
4. **Fixed positions.** The same element lives in the same place in every module, with no misalignments: a 4 px grid and fixed heights.
5. **Deleting always asks for confirmation** in a dialog: the title "Delete X?", the consequence in one sentence, a red button that names the action, and **initial focus on Cancel**. A toast with "Undo" follows. Reversible actions (mark, link, change status) never ask; they only offer "Undo".
6. **Lists are alphabetical by default** (locale-aware, accent-insensitive), including groups, columns and select options. Exceptions: tasks (by urgency) and dated records such as orders (newest first). Use `sortByText`.
7. **Visible progress.** Counters that go down, a day progress bar, a green check for done. Feedback is **subtle**: a 320 ms transition, no confetti.
8. **Save automatically** and show "Saved".
9. **Keyboard first.** `⌘K` for everything, and shortcuts on primary actions.

### Agents (AI features)

For products that put an AI agent in front of customers or money.

1. **Approve before sending.** Anything that goes to a customer or touches money goes through an approval queue. The default is to ask for approval.
2. **Autonomy per task,** never per whole agent. Low-star reviews (1 to 3 stars) always require approval.
3. **Undo, don't confirm.** Sending and discarding show a toast with Undo.
4. **The chat is for the owner,** not for the customer: to test, ask why and adjust. It reads the guidelines and the current data.
5. **Customer-facing replies** are short, factual, make no delivery-time or discount promises, and use no emoji.

### Visual foundations

The authoritative values are the design tokens (see the Tokens page). The summary:

- **Color.** A slightly warm neutral ramp from `#050506` to `#EDEDEA` (text is never pure white). Signals are pastel-bright so they keep contrast on dark: accent `#8AB4FF`, success `#5FD49A`, warning `#E9B65C`, danger `#F07A6E`. Soft backgrounds use `color-mix`.
- **Layers.** canvas, bg, surface, raised, hover. Move one layer at a time; do not skip layers.
- **Type.** Geist (400, 500, 600) for the interface, Geist Mono (400, 500) for data. Display and title use negative tracking.
- **Spacing.** A 4 px grid: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 64. Card padding is 20; gaps of 8 to 16 inside components and 24 to 32 between sections.
- **Controls.** Heights 32, 40 (default) and 48. Buttons and inputs share the same height.
- **Radius.** 4 for chips, menu items and checkboxes; 6 for buttons and inputs; 10 for cards, menus and dialogs; pill for badges and switches.
- **Lines.** 1 px always. Subtle for internal dividers, regular for cards, strong for controls and overlays. Dashed means disabled or a total row.
- **Elevation.** Only `--ds-shadow-overlay` and `--ds-shadow-dialog`. No inner shadows, no glow, no blur.
- **States.** Hover is one surface step lighter. There is no press animation. Focus is an accent border plus a 3 px ring. A selected row has a raised background and a 2 px inset ink bar; the active tab has a 2 px ink underline. Disabled controls use reduced opacity and, for inputs, a dashed border.
- **Motion.** Minimal: 150 ms, `cubic-bezier(.2, 0, 0, 1)`, only color, opacity and position. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Backgrounds.** Flat. No gradients, textures or illustrations. Photos appear only in avatars and thumbnails.

### Iconography

- The icon set is **Lucide**, 1.5 px stroke, `currentColor`, **bundled** (never fetched from a CDN at runtime). Import icons from `loui-ds` (`PlusIcon`, `SearchIcon`, ...), not from `lucide-react`.
- Icons are decorative unless given a label. Icon-only controls use `IconButton`, which requires a `label`.
- No emoji. No filled or colored icons. Unicode glyphs (`+`, `×`, `⌘`) only inside labelled icon buttons.
- Outside the sidebar the system is text-first: actions use a label.

---

## Content guidelines

How the interface talks. These rules apply to every string in the UI: labels, buttons, titles, toasts, errors, empty states and confirmations. They are also available as data in `docs/ai/content-rules.json`.

### Tone

- **Direct, calm, technical without jargon.**
- Speak to "you", usually implied: "Select an order", not "Please select an order".
- State what happened and what to do. Do not blame the user and do not dramatize.

### Casing

- **Sentence case everywhere:** titles, buttons, tabs, menu items. "New order", not "New Order" or "NEW ORDER".
- Uppercase appears only in mono group captions, and it is applied with CSS, never typed.

### Buttons

- **A verb plus an object:** "Create order", "Mark as shipped", "Retry charge".
- Never a bare "OK", "Send" or "Submit".
- Destructive buttons name the action: "Delete order".

### Confirmations

Deleting always asks. The dialog names the object and the consequence in one sentence, the red button names the action, and initial focus is on Cancel.

> **Delete "Northwind Web"?**
> "Northwind Web" and its 14 environments will be removed. This can't be undone.
> [Cancel] [Delete project]

Reversible actions (mark, link, change status) do not ask. They happen and offer "Undo" in a toast.

### Toasts

Short and in the past tense: what just happened.

- "Order #1051 created"
- "3 items archived"

Not "Creating order", not "Success!", not "Order was successfully created".

### Empty states

Say what happened, then what to do.

- "No orders found. Try another filter or search term."

### Errors

Say how to fix the problem.

- "Enter a complete email address."

Not "Invalid email!". Link the message to its field (`aria-describedby`); the `Field` components do this for you.

### Punctuation and symbols

- **No emoji, no exclamation marks, no decorative ellipses.**
- The ellipsis character appears only on menu items that open something that needs more input: "Move to…".
- No "Loading..." or "Saving...". Use a spinner or skeleton, and state the result when it is done.

### Numbers, codes and shortcuts

- Numbers, codes, amounts and shortcuts are set in the mono font (Geist Mono): `ORD-1048`, `$1,240.00`, `⌘K`.
- **Never build currency, dates or numbers by hand.** Format them with `Intl` for the active locale through the provided utilities: `formatCurrency`, `formatDate`, `formatNumber`, `formatPercent`, `formatRelativeDays`.
- Money is an integer in minor units plus an ISO 4217 currency code (ADR-0006). `formatCurrency(124000, 'USD', locale)` renders `$1,240.00`.

### Lists

Alphabetical by default (locale-aware, accent-insensitive), including groups, columns and select options. Use `sortByText`. Exceptions: tasks (by urgency) and dated records (newest first).

### What belongs to the product, not to the design system

Domain vocabulary (for example, an ERP rule that sold units are always called "Quantity") belongs to the product's own guidelines. The design system's built-in strings stay generic.

### Built-in strings and translation

Components contain no user-visible string literals. Every built-in label and ARIA string lives in the component's message catalog (`<Name>.messages.ts`), is written in English following the rules above, and can be overridden per instance or through `DSProvider`. `pt-BR` ships with the library and follows the same tone.

---

## Accessibility

Accessibility is part of the definition of done for every component. The target is **WCAG 2.2 Level AA**, using the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices patterns.

### Conformance target

- Real semantics first: native `<button>`, `<a>`, `<input>`, `<table>` where possible; ARIA only to fill gaps.
- Every interactive element has an accessible name. Icon-only controls require a `label` (enforced by the types).
- Errors, hints and descriptions are programmatically linked (`aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`).
- Visible focus on every focusable element, including in `forced-colors` mode. Focus is never hidden behind sticky UI and is restored when overlays close.
- Contrast: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for UI boundaries and graphics. Every foreground and surface pairing is listed in `tokens.json` with its measured ratio and checked by a unit test.
- Color is never the only carrier of meaning.
- Targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8); default controls are 40 px.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`, `forced-colors` and `prefers-contrast` are respected; 200% text zoom and 320 px reflow are supported.
- Time-limited actions (such as an Undo toast) can be paused by hover or focus and reached by keyboard.

### Keyboard model

React Aria Components provides the behavior; each row becomes contract tests.

| Pattern          | Keys                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Button, link     | `Enter`; button also `Space`                                                                                                                |
| Checkbox, switch | `Space` toggles                                                                                                                             |
| Radio group      | One tab stop (roving); arrow keys move and select, wrapping                                                                                 |
| Tabs             | Roving; `←` `→` move; `Home` `End`; `Tab` moves into the panel                                                                              |
| Menu             | Trigger opens with `Enter`, `Space` or `↓`; `↑` `↓`, `Home` `End`, typeahead; `Enter` or `Space` activates; `Esc` closes and restores focus |
| Combobox         | `↓` `↑` open and move; `Enter` selects; `Esc` closes, then clears                                                                           |
| Dialog, sheet    | Focus trapped; initial focus configurable (Cancel for destructive); `Esc` closes only the top layer; focus returns to trigger               |
| Popover, tooltip | `Esc` closes; tooltips show on focus and hover                                                                                              |
| Tag group        | One tab stop; arrow keys move; `Backspace` or `Delete` removes                                                                              |
| Toast, alert     | Announced through a live region; actions are focusable; auto-dismiss pauses on hover and focus                                              |

Application-level shortcuts use `useHotkey` (for example `Mod+K`); they ignore editable fields and IME composition so they never fight typing.

### How we test

Stories are the single source of states; the tests iterate over them.

| Layer             | Tool                                 | Guards                                                                |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Static            | `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` (strict)    | Role misuse, missing labels                                           |
| Component         | Vitest browser mode (Chromium)       | Props, states, events, controlled and uncontrolled, message overrides |
| Automated a11y    | axe-core through the Storybook addon | Structural WCAG violations on every story; a violation fails the test |
| Keyboard contract | Vitest and story `play` functions    | The keyboard table above                                              |
| Contrast          | Token unit test and browser checks   | Every token pair against its minimum ratio                            |
| Visual            | Screenshot baselines                 | Unintended appearance changes                                         |
| SSR               | Server render tests                  | No `window` access; hydration-safe                                    |
| Manual            | Screen reader checklist per release  | What automation cannot judge                                          |

Rules: a bug fix starts with a failing test; axe rules are never disabled globally; a scoped exception needs a comment with the reason and a task ID.

### Assistive technology

Automated checks cover structure and contrast. Manual screen reader testing (NVDA with Firefox and Chrome, VoiceOver with Safari, TalkBack) is planned per release against a checklist. No manual screen reader pass has been recorded yet, so treat that coverage as not yet performed.

### Known limitations

- Automated tests cannot judge reading order, announcement quality or whether labels make sense; those are reviewed by hand.
- jsdom cannot compute contrast or layout, so contrast and layout checks run in a real browser.
- Dark is the only theme. Contrast has been verified for it and for the `paper` scope; a new theme needs its own verification.

### Reporting an issue

Open an issue with the component, the browser and assistive technology, the steps, and what you expected. Accessibility bugs are treated as defects, not enhancements.

---

## Bundle size

How much JavaScript Loui DS adds to an app, where the rest comes from, and what to do about it.

### What a typical app ships

Measured on `examples/vite-app` (Vite 8, production build): an `AppShell` with `Sidebar`, `TopBar`, a `DataTable` with pagination, a `Dialog` with an `Input`, and toasts.

| Share of the bundle                                      | Before minification | Notes                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `react-dom` + `react` + `scheduler`                      | ~550 kB             | Fixed cost of React 19.                                                                                  |
| `react-aria` + `react-aria-components` + `react-stately` | ~620 kB             | Behavior layer (ADR-0001): focus, keyboard, overlays, i18n. Includes translated strings for 30+ locales. |
| `loui-ds` (components, i18n, utilities)                 | ~90 kB              | Only the components the app imports; the package is tree-shakable (`sideEffects` lists CSS only).        |
| `lucide-react`                                           | ~10 kB              | Only the curated icons that are used.                                                                    |

Minified output: **531 kB (163 kB gzip)** without optimization, **489 kB (150 kB gzip)** with the locale plugin below. The design system's own code is under a tenth of the total; the rest is React and React Aria, which every app built on this system needs anyway.

### 1. Strip unused React Aria locales (recommended)

React Aria bundles its built-in strings (for example "Next month", "Dismiss") for every locale it supports. `@react-aria/optimize-locales-plugin` keeps only the locales your app serves. Use the same list you pass to `DSProvider`.

Vite:

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import optimizeLocales from '@react-aria/optimize-locales-plugin';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [{ ...optimizeLocales.vite({ locales: ['en-US', 'pt-BR'] }), enforce: 'pre' }, react()],
});
```

Next.js (webpack):

```ts
// next.config.ts
import optimizeLocales from '@react-aria/optimize-locales-plugin';
import type { NextConfig } from 'next';

const config: NextConfig = {
  webpack(webpackConfig) {
    webpackConfig.plugins.push(optimizeLocales.webpack({ locales: ['en-US', 'pt-BR'] }));
    return webpackConfig;
  },
};

export default config;
```

Saving in the example: 42 kB minified (14 kB gzip). A locale that is stripped falls back to English strings inside React Aria; Loui DS's own messages are unaffected (they come from its catalogs).

### 2. Import from the package root

Always `import { Button } from 'loui-ds'`. Bundlers drop what you do not use. Do not import from `loui-ds/dist/...` paths: they are not part of the public API and can duplicate modules.

### 3. Split heavy screens, not components

Lazy-load whole routes or rarely opened surfaces with `React.lazy` and `Suspense`, for example a settings page, a report with charts, or the command palette's command list. Splitting individual small components costs more in requests than it saves.

```tsx
const Reports = lazy(() => import('./routes/Reports'));
```

Keep `DSProvider`, `AppShell` and the toast region in the main chunk: they are on every screen.

### 4. Check before you ship

- `vite build` prints the size of each chunk; add `rollup-plugin-visualizer` (or Next's `@next/bundle-analyzer`) when a chunk grows unexpectedly.
- The design system itself is guarded by `size-limit` in its CI (`pnpm size`), so its own growth is reviewed per change.

---

## Color

Color in Loui DS is dark, flat and quiet. Hierarchy comes from five surface layers and three line weights; color itself is reserved for meaning. Use semantic tokens only (`--ds-surface`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-danger`); the primitive palette exists to define them. Every value, description and contrast ratio is listed on the Tokens page.

### Layers

Five surfaces build depth, from the darkest to the lightest. **Move one step at a time** and never skip a layer: a card sits on `bg`, something that floats sits on the card.

| Token                    | Use                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ds-bg-canvas`         | The page behind the app shell (the `html` element). Darkest layer.          |
| `--ds-bg`                | App background: body, top bar, main area.                                   |
| `--ds-surface`           | Cards, panels, table bodies and inputs at rest.                             |
| `--ds-surface-raised`    | Menus, popovers, selected rows, anything floating above a surface.          |
| `--ds-surface-hover`     | Hover state of controls and list items: one step above the resting surface. |
| `--ds-surface-row-hover` | Hover for table and list rows only. Subtler, so dense data stays calm.      |

### Lines

Borders do the work that shadows do elsewhere. Lines are always 1px. A dashed line means disabled or a total row.

| Token               | Use it for                                                                                 |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--ds-line-subtle`  | Dividers inside a card or table (row separators). Decorative.                              |
| `--ds-line`         | The border of cards and containers.                                                        |
| `--ds-line-strong`  | The border of overlays: menus, popovers, dialogs.                                          |
| `--ds-line-control` | The boundary of form controls: input, select, textarea, checkbox, radio, combobox trigger. |

Form control boundaries must reach 3:1 against the surface (WCAG 1.4.11). `line` and `line-strong` do not, which is why controls have their own token.

### Text

| Token               | Use                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ds-text`         | Primary text and icons. A warm off-white, never pure white. Anything the user must read.       |
| `--ds-text-2`       | Supporting text: descriptions, helper copy, inactive labels.                                   |
| `--ds-text-3`       | Tertiary text: metadata, placeholders, hints. Never the only carrier of essential information. |
| `--ds-text-inverse` | Text and icons on solid light or signal fills (primary button, selected calendar day).         |

All three text tokens pass 4.5:1 on every surface up to `surface-hover` (see the table below). The rule for `text-3` is about hierarchy, not contrast: the most important thing is `text`, supporting detail is `text-2`, and only metadata steps down to `text-3`. Do not use `text-3` on tinted or filled backgrounds; there is no contrast guarantee there.

`--ds-text-inverse` is measured on the fills it sits on, not on surfaces:

### Signals

One accent and three status colors. Each signal has a solid value for text and icons, and a soft tint for backgrounds.

- **Accent** (`--ds-accent`): focus, selection, links and "open" states. This is the only accent. **Never a button fill or a large area.** The primary button is light ink on dark (`--ds-primary-bg`), and there is one primary action per screen.
- **Success** (`--ds-success`): done, saved, healthy.
- **Warning** (`--ds-warning`): attention needed, nothing broken.
- **Danger** (`--ds-danger`): errors, invalid fields and destructive actions.

Success, warning and danger **always come with text** (a label, a message, an icon with a name). Color is never the only carrier of meaning.

### Soft tints

Soft tokens are the signal color at low opacity (14%, danger 10%), composited over the surface beneath. Use them as the background of badges, banners, selected items and invalid fields, with the solid signal as the text color. The ratio of a signal on its own tint is checked in the test suite.

### Paper

Receipt and PDF previews are the only light surface in the system. Scope them with `[data-theme="paper"]` and use `--ds-paper-*` tokens. `--ds-paper-rule` is decorative (below 3:1) and must never be a control boundary.

Inside the scope, `--ds-success`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-danger` and `--ds-accent` are remapped to darker twins (`--ds-paper-success`, `--ds-paper-warning`, `--ds-paper-danger`, `--ds-paper-accent`), and their tints (`--ds-success-soft` and the others) are remapped with them, so badges, alerts and tinted buttons keep 4.5:1 on the paper. The `Components/Card` story `PaperReceipt` shows the scope.

### Contrast changes from the handoff

Three tokens were changed from the original design handoff so that every text and control pairing meets WCAG 2.2 AA (task TOK-004). The full record is in `docs/tokens/changes.md`.

| Token                             | Old           | New       | Why                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------- | ------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ds-text-3` (and `--ds-gray-7`) | `#7A7A82`     | `#86868E` | Was 3.86:1 on `surface-hover` and below 4.5:1 on `surface-raised`. Now 4.55:1 on `surface-hover`, so it passes on every surface up to there. |
| `--ds-line-control`               | did not exist | `#64646B` | Control boundaries need 3:1. `line-strong` is about 1.5:1. Now 3.35:1 on `bg`, 3.21:1 on `surface`, 3.02:1 on `surface-raised`.              |
| `--ds-paper-accent`               | `#B8603E`     | `#944A2D` | 5.7:1 on `paper`, 4.7:1 on its 14% tint (TOK-012); the original was below 4.5:1 for text.                                                    |

### Rules of thumb

- Use `text` for what must be read, `text-2` for support, `text-3` for metadata.
- Never use a raw hex value. If a color is missing, add a token.
- Backgrounds are flat: no gradients, textures or illustrations.
- A selected state combines a surface step with a non-color cue (an ink bar, a check), never color alone.

---

## Typography

Two typefaces, ten roles, one rule: nothing is smaller than 11.5px. Geist carries the interface; Geist Mono carries data. Both are self-hosted (no runtime fetch), with metric-matched fallback faces so text does not jump while fonts load.

### Typefaces

| Variable         | Face       | Weights       | Use                                                            |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ds-font-sans` | Geist      | 400, 500, 600 | Interface text: titles, body, labels, buttons.                 |
| `--ds-font-mono` | Geist Mono | 400, 500      | Data: numbers, codes, identifiers, dates, shortcuts, captions. |

Weight roles: **400** for body text, **500** for labels and mono captions (not for body paragraphs), **600** for display, title and heading. Do not add a heavier weight.

### The scale

Use a role, never a free size. The roles are the tokens `--ds-fs-*` (size), `--ds-lh-*` (line height) and `--ds-weight-*`. Sizes in px, line heights in px.

| Role    | Face     | Use it for                                                              |
| ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| display | sans 600 | One hero statement per view, at most.                                   |
| title   | sans 600 | Page and section titles.                                                |
| heading | sans 600 | Dialog titles, card headings.                                           |
| body    | sans 400 | Running text; the base size of the app.                                 |
| small   | sans 400 | Descriptions, helper text, table cells.                                 |
| label   | sans 500 | Field labels, chips, compact buttons.                                   |
| meta    | mono 400 | Dates, phone numbers, counts beside titles.                             |
| caption | mono 500 | Group captions. Uppercase by CSS, +8% tracking. The floor of the scale. |
| num     | mono 500 | Indicator figures (24px).                                               |
| num-lg  | mono 500 | Highlighted totals such as a balance (30px).                            |

### Tracking and case

- **Display** has -2% tracking (-0.68px) and **title** -1% (-0.22px). Tight tracking only works at large sizes: never apply it to body text.
- **Caption** has +8% tracking (0.92px) and is the only role set in uppercase. Uppercase is applied with CSS (`text-transform`), so write the source text in sentence case ("Order details", not "ORDER DETAILS"). Everywhere else, use sentence case too.
- Tracking tokens are in px because DTCG dimensions have no `em`. They are exact for the fixed size of each role.

### The 11.5px floor

`--ds-fs-caption` (11.5px) is the smallest font size in the system and it is enforced by a test. Do not use a smaller size, in CSS or in a chart, and do not scale text down with transforms. Use `meta` (12px) or `caption` for the smallest text; never invent an in-between.

### When to use mono

Use Geist Mono for anything that is data rather than prose, and turn on tabular figures so columns align.

- Numbers and amounts: `$1,240.00`, `3 / 12`.
- Codes and identifiers: `ORD-1048`, `SKU-0032`.
- Dates and phone numbers beside a title.
- Keyboard shortcuts: `Ctrl K`.
- Group captions.

Do not set sentences, labels or buttons in mono. Format amounts and dates with `Intl` (the `formatCurrency` helper), never by hand.

### Tabular numerals

`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` gives every digit the same width, so figures in a column line up and live counters do not jitter. The `mono` prop of `Text` turns it on; for custom elements use the `.ds-tabular-nums` utility class. Mono roles (`meta`, `num`, `num-lg`) should always have it on.

### Heading and Text

`Heading` separates the semantic level (`h1` to `h6`, the page outline) from the visual size (`display`, `title`, `heading`). Choose the level for structure and the size for design; keep levels sequential with one `h1` per page. `Text` sets size, line height, tone and an optional mono face, and the `as` prop picks the element.

Use `Heading` and `Text` instead of setting font properties by hand. Do not use a heading element only for its size.

---

## Spacing, sizing and radius

Everything sits on a 4px grid and has a fixed size, so the same element lives in the same place in every module. Use tokens, never raw pixels.

### Spacing scale

Nine steps. The unit is 4px; steps are named by their multiple (`--ds-space-3` is 3 x 4px = 12px).

| Variable        | Value | Use                                                      |
| --------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ds-space-1`  | 4px   | Icon-to-text gaps, tight padding.                        |
| `--ds-space-2`  | 8px   | Default gap between related elements inside a component. |
| `--ds-space-3`  | 12px  | Compact padding, gaps between form fields.               |
| `--ds-space-4`  | 16px  | Standard padding and gap between components.             |
| `--ds-space-5`  | 20px  | Card padding.                                            |
| `--ds-space-6`  | 24px  | Gap between sections of a page.                          |
| `--ds-space-8`  | 32px  | Large section separation.                                |
| `--ds-space-12` | 48px  | Page-level separation.                                   |
| `--ds-space-16` | 64px  | Hero and empty-state breathing room.                     |

Rules of thumb: card padding is 20px; gaps **inside** a component are 8 to 16px; gaps **between** sections are 24 to 32px. Do not mix steps in one group, and do not use values off the grid.

### Control heights

Controls come in three heights. The default is 40px. Pick one size per group of controls and do not mix them in a row.

| Token               | Value | Use                                    |
| ------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------- |
| `--ds-control-h-sm` | 32px  | Dense toolbars and table filters.      |
| `--ds-control-h-md` | 40px  | Default: buttons, inputs, selects.     |
| `--ds-control-h-lg` | 48px  | Primary actions and touch-first forms. |

### Fixed layout sizes

| Token              | Value | Use                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ds-item-h`      | 36px  | Menu items, navigation items, listbox options.                          |
| `--ds-row-h`       | 52px  | Table and list rows.                                                    |
| `--ds-row-h-dense` | 60px  | Rows with two lines of content. It is taller on purpose: it holds more. |
| `--ds-topbar-h`    | 64px  | The top bar.                                                            |
| `--ds-sidebar-w`   | 240px | The app sidebar.                                                        |

### Target size

No interactive element may be smaller than 24 x 24 CSS px (`--ds-target-min`, WCAG 2.5.8). Small visuals, such as the 18px checkbox box, reach the minimum through their label row or padding. Never shrink the clickable area to match a small icon.

### Radius

Radius follows the role of the element, so nested shapes look related.

| Token              | Value | Elements                                                       |
| ------------------ | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ds-radius-sm`   | 4px   | Chips, menu items, small marks.                                |
| `--ds-radius-md`   | 6px   | Buttons and inputs.                                            |
| `--ds-radius-lg`   | 10px  | Cards, menus, popovers, dialogs.                               |
| `--ds-radius-pill` | 999px | Badges and switches. Any very large value renders fully round. |

The checkbox box uses a component token (`--ds-checkbox-radius`, 5px). An inner element has a smaller radius than its container.

### Elevation

Hierarchy comes from surface plus border, not from shadow. There are **only two shadows, and only overlays use them**.

| Token                 | Use                                             |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `--ds-shadow-overlay` | Floating overlays: menus, popovers, toasts.     |
| `--ds-shadow-dialog`  | Dialogs and side sheets: the highest elevation. |

No inner shadows, no glow, no blur. Cards, panels and inline elements are flat. Dialogs use the `--ds-overlay` backdrop and sheets use the lighter `--ds-scrim`, both without blur.

---

## States and interaction

Every interactive element has the same small set of states, and they look the same everywhere. Feedback is subtle: no press animation, no bounce, no confetti.

### The states

| State    | What changes                                                                                                               | Notes                                                        |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Rest     | The base surface, a 1px line.                                                                                              |                                                              |
| Hover    | One surface step lighter (`surface` becomes `surface-hover`). The primary button dims to 88% brightness instead.           | Table rows use the subtler `surface-row-hover`.              |
| Focus    | Accent border plus a 3px ring (`--ds-focus-ring`).                                                                         | Shown for keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`). Always visible. |
| Pressed  | No visual change.                                                                                                          | There is no press animation by design.                       |
| Selected | Raised background plus a 2px ink bar on the left of a row; a 2px ink underline for the active tab; a check for checkboxes. | Never color alone.                                           |
| Disabled | Opacity 35% (`--ds-opacity-disabled`), no hover; inputs also get a dashed border.                                          | One value for every component.                               |
| Invalid  | Danger border and the danger ring (`--ds-focus-ring-danger`), with an error message in text.                               | The message says how to fix it.                              |
| Pending  | The label is replaced by a spinner at the same width. The control stays focusable.                                         | Not disabled: focus is never lost.                           |

States are CSS, not React state: components expose them as data attributes (`data-hovered`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-selected`, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`), and styles never use inline overrides.

### Fields

Inputs, selects and other fields move through rest, focus, invalid and disabled. Tab into a field to see the focus ring; the other states are set by props.

### Selection controls

### Tabs and rows

An active tab has a 2px ink underline. A selected table row has a raised background and a 2px ink bar on its inline-start edge. Both also work in forced-colors mode.

### Focus

Focus is always visible. Buttons, fields, tabs and panels show an accent border or a 3px ring; table rows, headers and cells show a 2px accent outline inset in the cell. A transparent outline is kept so the focus indicator also appears in forced-colors (high contrast) mode. Focus is never hidden behind sticky UI, and it is restored to the trigger when an overlay closes.

### Keyboard model

Keyboard first: everything is reachable and operable without a pointer, `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` walk the page in reading order, and `Ctrl K` (Command K on Apple) opens the command palette. Each row below is also a contract test.

| Pattern                                | Keys                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Button / link                          | `Enter`; button also `Space`                                                                                                                            |
| Checkbox / switch                      | `Space` toggles (switch also `Enter` optional)                                                                                                          |
| Radio group / segmented / choice tiles | One tab stop (roving); `Left/Up` previous, `Right/Down` next (radio groups wrap; segmented controls stop at the ends); `Space` selects                  |
| Tabs                                   | Roving; `Left/Right` move; `Home/End`; automatic or manual activation as documented; `Tab` moves into the panel                                         |
| Menu                                   | Trigger `Enter/Space/Down` opens and focuses the first item; `Up/Down`, `Home/End`, typeahead; `Enter/Space` activates; `Esc` closes and restores focus |
| Combobox                               | `Down/Up` open and move (`aria-activedescendant`), `Enter` selects, `Esc` closes then clears, `Home/End` in the list                                    |
| Dialog / sheet                         | Focus trapped; initial focus configurable (Cancel for destructive); `Esc` closes **only the top layer**; focus returns to the trigger                   |
| Popover                                | `Esc` closes and restores focus; focus moves in only if interactive                                                                                     |
| Tooltip                                | Shows on focus and hover; `Esc` dismisses; content is hoverable                                                                                         |
| Accordion / disclosure                 | `Enter/Space` toggles; optional `Up/Down/Home/End` between headers                                                                                      |
| Slider                                 | Arrow keys step; `PageUp/PageDown` large step; `Home/End` min/max                                                                                       |
| Number field (stepper)                 | Textbox with `aria-roledescription="Number field"`; `Up/Down` step; `PageUp/PageDown` step; `Home/End` min/max; typing allowed                          |
| Calendar grid                          | Arrows move by day/week; `PageUp/PageDown` month; `Shift+PageUp/PageDown` year; `Home/End` first/last day of the month; `Enter/Space` selects           |
| Data table                             | Header buttons sort (`aria-sort`); row action via a real button or link; selection checkboxes are labelled                                              |
| Toast / alert                          | Announced through a live region; actions focusable; auto-dismiss pauses on hover and focus                                                              |

Sources: the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices and React Aria. The same table is in the [accessibility guide](../guides/accessibility.md).

### Undo, or confirm

Two kinds of action, two behaviors. Do not mix them.

- **Undo for almost everything.** Change a status, pay, send, remove a row, link a color: do it at once and show a toast with "Undo" (short-lived, and paused while hovered or focused). It is faster and calmer than asking.
- **Confirm only when deleting a record.** Delete a product, customer, sale, order or entry: open a dialog. The title is "Delete X?", one sentence states the consequence, the red button names the action (`danger-solid`, "Delete order"), and **initial focus is on Cancel**. A toast with "Undo" follows when the data can be restored.

Anything that goes to a customer or touches money goes through an approval queue instead; see the [principles guide](../guides/principles.md).

### Wordmark

There is no logo. Until a brand exists, the product name is set in Geist 600 as plain text. Do not draw, trace or approximate a mark, and do not use an icon as a logo.

---

## Motion, layering and iconography

Motion is minimal, layers are strictly ordered, and icons come from one small curated set.

### Motion

Motion explains a change; it never decorates. Only `color`, `background-color`, `border-color`, `opacity` and position change, never size or layout.

| Token                    | Value                        | Use                                                                              |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ds-duration`          | 150ms                        | Standard transition: hover, focus and state changes.                             |
| `--ds-duration-done`     | 320ms                        | Completion feedback: a subtle check or fill when something is done. No confetti. |
| `--ds-duration-progress` | 300ms                        | Progress bar fill changes.                                                       |
| `--ds-ease`              | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | Easing for every transition: fast start, soft landing.                           |

Rules:

- Use the tokens; never write a raw duration or easing.
- No press animation, bounce, spring, parallax or looping decoration. The only continuous animation is a loading spinner.
- Feedback for a finished task is subtle and positive: a green check, a filled progress bar, a calm toast.

#### Reduced motion

When the user asks for less motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`), the base stylesheet cuts every transition and animation to an instant change, globally. Components must not depend on a transition to communicate state: the end state alone has to be clear. Do not add per-component motion that bypasses this rule.

### Layering

Overlays use a fixed stack of z-index tokens. Raw `z-index` values are not allowed.

| Layer    | Token             | Value | Why it sits here                                                                                |
| -------- | ----------------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sheet    | `--ds-z-sheet`    | 40    | Side panels with their scrim. The panel is the sheet value plus one. The lowest overlay.        |
| Dialog   | `--ds-z-dialog`   | 45    | Modals and their backdrop. Above sheets, so a dialog opened from a sheet stacks on top of it.   |
| Dropdown | `--ds-z-dropdown` | 50    | Selects, comboboxes, date pickers. Above dialogs and sheets because they open from inside them. |
| Popover  | `--ds-z-popover`  | 55    | Popovers and action menus. Above dropdowns, dialogs and sheets.                                 |
| Toast    | `--ds-z-toast`    | 58    | Confirmations and Undo. Above every overlay so they stay visible.                               |
| Tooltip  | `--ds-z-tooltip`  | 60    | The highest layer. It must never be hidden. Do not add layers above it.                         |

Order: **sheet < dialog < dropdown < popover < toast < tooltip**. `Esc` closes only the top layer. Overlays render through a shared portal, so they never depend on the stacking context of their trigger.

### Iconography

Icons are Lucide, bundled in the package (never fetched from a CDN at runtime), drawn with a 1.5px stroke in `currentColor`.

- **Curated set only.** Import from the design system (`SearchIcon`, `XIcon`), not from `lucide-react`. To add an icon, add it to the set with a documented use first.
- **Decorative unless labelled.** `Icon` hides itself from assistive technology by default; the text next to it names the control. Pass `label` only when the icon carries meaning on its own. An icon-only control is an `IconButton`, and its `label` is required.
- **Sizes** are tokens: `xs` 12px, `sm` 14px, `md` 18px (default), `lg` 20px.
- **Directional icons** (chevrons, arrows) take the `directional` prop so they mirror in right-to-left languages.
- **No emoji.** No filled or colored icons, with one exception: the filled star of `Rating`. Unicode glyphs appear only inside a labelled `IconButton`.
- Color comes from the surrounding text color. A status icon is paired with text; do not rely on its color.

#### Decorative and labelled

---

## Design tokens

431 tokens; the table lists the 417 semantic and core ones (primitives are listed in tokens.json). Use the CSS variable, never the value.

| CSS variable | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--ds-bg-canvas` | `#050506` | Page canvas behind the app shell (the html element). The darkest layer. Not for cards or controls. |
| `--ds-bg` | `#0B0B0C` | Default app background (body, top bar, main area). One step above the canvas. Not for cards; use surface. |
| `--ds-surface` | `#111113` | Cards, panels, table bodies and inputs at rest. Move one layer at a time: bg, surface, surface-raised, surface-hover. |
| `--ds-surface-raised` | `#18181B` | Menus, popovers, selected rows and anything floating above a surface. Not for page backgrounds. |
| `--ds-surface-hover` | `#1F1F23` | Hover state of controls and list items: one step lighter than the resting surface. Do not use at rest. |
| `--ds-surface-row-hover` | `#141416` | Hover background of table and list rows only; subtler than surface-hover so dense data stays calm. Not for buttons or menu items. |
| `--ds-line-subtle` | `#1E1E22` | Internal dividers inside a card or table (row separators). Decorative, so exempt from the 3:1 non-text contrast rule. Never use it as a control boundary. |
| `--ds-line` | `#26262B` | Default 1px border of cards and containers. Not for form control boundaries; use line-control. |
| `--ds-line-strong` | `#33333A` | Border of overlays, menus, popovers, dialogs and cards that must stand out. Not for form control boundaries (use line-control); it is below 3:1. |
| `--ds-line-control` | `#64646B` | Boundary of form controls: input, select, textarea, checkbox, radio and combobox triggers. At least 3:1 on bg, surface and surface-raised (WCAG 1.4.11). New in TOK-004. Not for decorative dividers. |
| `--ds-text` | `#EDEDEA` | Primary text and icons. Warm off-white, not pure white. Use for anything that must be read first. |
| `--ds-text-2` | `#A3A3A9` | Secondary text: descriptions, supporting copy, inactive labels. |
| `--ds-text-3` | `#86868E` | Tertiary text: metadata, placeholders, hints. Meets 4.5:1 on every surface up to surface-hover. Do not use on surfaces lighter than surface-hover or on colored fills. |
| `--ds-text-inverse` | `#0B0B0C` | Text and icons on solid light or signal fills (selected day in a calendar, solid badges). Not on dark surfaces. |
| `--ds-primary-bg` | `#EDEDEA` | Fill of the primary button and the tooltip: light ink on a dark UI. One primary action per screen. Hover is brightness .88, not a new token. |
| `--ds-primary-fg` | `#0B0B0C` | Text and icons on primary-bg. |
| `--ds-primary-fg-muted` | `#5A5A60` | Secondary text on primary-bg (for example the shortcut hint in a tooltip). Only valid on primary-bg. |
| `--ds-accent` | `#8AB4FF` | The single accent: focus, selection, links and open states. Never a button fill or a large area. Always pair with text or a shape, never color alone. |
| `--ds-success` | `#5FD49A` | Success signal: done, saved, healthy. Always accompanied by text or an icon. Not decorative. |
| `--ds-warning` | `#E9B65C` | Warning signal: attention needed, nothing broken. Always accompanied by text or an icon. |
| `--ds-danger` | `#F07A6E` | Error and destructive signal: errors, delete buttons, invalid fields. Always accompanied by text or an icon. |
| `--ds-accent-soft` | `rgba(138, 180, 255, 0.14)` | Tinted background for accent states (selected item, info). 14% accent over the surface beneath, resolved with color-mix so it adapts to the surface. Not for text. |
| `--ds-success-soft` | `rgba(95, 212, 154, 0.14)` | Tinted background for success states (badge, banner). 14% success over the surface beneath. Not for text. |
| `--ds-warning-soft` | `rgba(233, 182, 92, 0.14)` | Tinted background for warning states (badge, banner). 14% warning over the surface beneath. Not for text. |
| `--ds-danger-soft` | `rgba(240, 122, 110, 0.1)` | Tinted background for error states (badge, banner, invalid field). 10% danger over the surface beneath. Not for text. |
| `--ds-danger-soft-hover` | `rgba(240, 122, 110, 0.18)` | Hover state of danger-soft surfaces such as the ghost-danger button. 18% danger over the surface beneath. |
| `--ds-danger-line` | `rgba(240, 122, 110, 0.35)` | Border of danger-tinted surfaces (error banner, destructive confirmation). 35% danger over the surface beneath. Not a form control boundary; invalid fields use danger. |
| `--ds-overlay` | `rgba(5, 5, 6, 0.72)` | Backdrop behind dialogs. Flat, no blur. Not for side sheets; use scrim. |
| `--ds-scrim` | `rgba(5, 5, 6, 0.55)` | Backdrop behind side sheets. Lighter than overlay so the page stays visible. Not for dialogs. |
| `--ds-swatch-ring` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12)` | Inset 1px ring drawn inside color swatches and avatars so dark swatches stay visible on dark surfaces. Not a general border. |
| `--ds-paper` | `#F4F2EC` | Paper surface of printed-document previews (receipt, PDF). The only light surface in the system; use inside [data-theme="paper"] only. |
| `--ds-paper-ink` | `#151515` | Primary text on paper. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-ink-2` | `#3A3A3A` | Secondary text on paper. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-muted` | `#6B6B6B` | Tertiary text and control boundaries on paper (above 4.5:1 on paper). Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-rule` | `#9A968C` | Decorative rules and dividers on paper (table lines, totals). Below 3:1, so never a control boundary or text. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-accent` | `#944A2D` | Accent on paper: links and highlighted figures (5.7:1 on paper, 4.7:1 on paper-accent-soft). Darkened from #B8603E in TOK-004 and again from #A95839 in TOK-012 so accent text passes on its own tint. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-success` | `#17683D` | Success signal on paper: text, icons and borders (6.1:1 on paper, 4.9:1 on paper-success-soft). Remaps success inside [data-theme="paper"] only (TOK-012). |
| `--ds-paper-warning` | `#7F5200` | Warning signal on paper: text, icons and borders (6.0:1 on paper, 4.9:1 on paper-warning-soft). Remaps warning inside [data-theme="paper"] only (TOK-012). |
| `--ds-paper-danger` | `#A8231B` | Error and destructive signal on paper (6.4:1 on paper, 4.8:1 on paper-danger-soft-hover). Remaps danger inside [data-theme="paper"] only (TOK-012). |
| `--ds-paper-success-soft` | `rgba(23, 104, 61, 0.14)` | Tinted background for success states on paper. 14% paper-success over the paper. Not for text. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-warning-soft` | `rgba(127, 82, 0, 0.14)` | Tinted background for warning states on paper. 14% paper-warning over the paper. Not for text. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-danger-soft` | `rgba(168, 35, 27, 0.1)` | Tinted background for error states on paper. 10% paper-danger over the paper. Not for text. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-danger-soft-hover` | `rgba(168, 35, 27, 0.18)` | Hover state of paper-danger-soft surfaces. 18% paper-danger over the paper. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-danger-line` | `rgba(168, 35, 27, 0.35)` | Border of danger-tinted surfaces on paper. 35% paper-danger over the paper. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-accent-soft` | `rgba(148, 74, 45, 0.14)` | Tinted background for accent states on paper (selected item, info badge). 14% paper-accent over the paper. Not for text. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-focus-ring` | `0px 0px 0px 3px rgba(138, 180, 255, 0.25)` | Focus halo: 3px ring, 25% accent over the surface beneath, used as box-shadow next to an accent border. base.css adds a transparent outline so focus stays visible in forced-colors mode. Not a hover or selected style. |
| `--ds-focus-ring-danger` | `0px 0px 0px 3px rgba(240, 122, 110, 0.25)` | Focus halo for invalid fields: 3px ring, 25% danger over the surface beneath. Use instead of focus-ring when the control is in an error state. Not a general error style. |
| `--ds-font-sans` | `Geist, "Geist Fallback", system-ui, sans-serif` | UI font stack: self-hosted Geist, then a metric-matched Arial fallback face, then the system font. Use for all interface text. Not for numbers, codes or data (use font.mono). |
| `--ds-font-mono` | `"Geist Mono", "Geist Mono Fallback", ui-monospace, monospace` | Data font stack: self-hosted Geist Mono with a metric-matched fallback. Use for numbers, codes, amounts, shortcuts and uppercase group captions. Pair with tabular-nums. Not for running text. |

| `--ds-fs-label` | `13px` | Label font size (13px, line 18px, medium). Field labels, chips and compact buttons. Minimum font size in the system is 11.5px (caption); never go below it. |

| `--ds-fs-caption` | `11.5px` | Caption font size (11.5px, line 16px, mono medium, uppercase, +8% tracking). FLOOR of the type scale: no token or component may use a smaller size. Group captions and table headers. |

| `--ds-fs-num-lg` | `30px` | Number font size for highlighted totals such as a balance (30px, line 36px, mono medium). Use with tabular-nums. Minimum font size in the system is 11.5px (caption); never go below it. |
| `--ds-fs-icon` | `20px` | Font size of text glyphs inside icon-only buttons (for example the multiplication sign and chevrons), 20px. Not for SVG icons; use size.icon-*. |
