### Pairings that fail contrast

- `--ds-line-control` fails 3:1 on color.surface-hover (2.8:1).

---

## Components

### Accordion

> A stack of sections that expand and collapse. Each header is a heading that wraps a real
button (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`), so it appears in the page outline and works with
`Enter` and `Space`. Built on React Aria `DisclosureGroup`.

Use it to shorten a long page of related, optional content (FAQs, settings groups). Do not
hide content people need to finish their task.

A stack of sections that expand and collapse. Each header is a heading that wraps a real button. Built on React Aria `DisclosureGroup`, `Disclosure` and `DisclosurePanel`.

- Handoff source: `components/layout/Accordion.jsx` (TODO `CMP-LAY-04`).

- Import: `import { Accordion } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Accordion/Accordion.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Accordion`): Default, Plain, InitiallyExpanded, KeyboardSingle, Multiple, DisabledItem, HeadingLevel2, Controlled, LongText, RightToLeft, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly AccordionItem[]` | yes |  | The sections, in order. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Allow several sections open at once. By default opening one section closes the others (single expansion). |
| `value` | `readonly string[]` |  |  | Values of the expanded items (controlled). |
| `defaultValue` | `readonly string[]` |  | `[]` | Values of the items expanded at first (uncontrolled). |
| `onChange` | `(value: string[]) => void` |  |  | Called with the values of all expanded items after the user toggles one. |
| `variant` | `'bordered' \| 'plain'` |  | `'bordered'` | `bordered` (default) draws a card around the sections; `plain` only draws dividers. |
| `headingLevel` | `'2' \| '3' \| '4' \| '5' \| '6'` |  | `'3'` | Level of the heading that wraps each trigger, `3` by default. Use the level that follows the heading above the accordion in the page outline. |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Disables every section. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the root element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `variant`: `bordered`, `plain`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-accordion-padding-inline`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-icon-sm`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-line-subtle`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-row-h`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-surface-row-hover`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`, `--ds-weight-regular`

#### When to use

- FAQs, grouped settings, long optional detail on a record.
- To shorten a page whose sections people read one at a time.

#### When not to use

- For content people must see to finish the task.
- For switching between views: use `Tabs`.
- For a single show/hide of one block: a plain disclosure is enough.

#### Accessibility

- Each header is `h3` (configurable) containing a `button` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the panel is a `group` labelled by the button. Headings appear in the page outline and in screen reader heading lists.
- Keys: `Tab` moves between triggers; `Enter` and `Space` toggle. Optional arrow-key movement between headers (APG) is not added: each trigger is a tab stop.
- Collapsed panels are hidden (`hidden="until-found"`), so find-in-page can open them, and they take no space.
- The chevron rotates 180 degrees to show the state; the state itself is `aria-expanded`, not the icon. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the rotation is instant.
- The focus indicator is an inset accent outline because the group clips overflow. Forced colors use `Highlight`.
- Disabled items are not focusable.
- Meta text is read after the title; keep it short.

#### Content rules

- Titles are short phrases or questions in sentence case, and say what is inside.
- Do not put the only copy of important information in a collapsed panel.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Accordion
  headingLevel={2}
  items={[
    { value: 'shipping', title: 'How long does shipping take?', content: 'Two to five days.' },
    { value: 'returns', title: 'Can I return an order?', meta: '30 days', content: '…' },
  ]}
/>

<Accordion multiple variant="plain" value={open} onChange={setOpen} items={items} />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Tabs: For switching between views: use `Tabs`.
- Renders: Icon

### ActionList

> A vertical list of records, each with a title, optional description, a mono meta value and a
"more actions" menu. Built on React Aria `GridList`: rows are reached with the arrow keys
(one tab stop for the list), `Enter` runs `onAction`, and `Tab` or the right arrow moves
from a row to its menu button.

A vertical list of records. Each row has an optional leading node, a title, an optional description, a mono meta value and an optional "more actions" menu. Built on React Aria `GridList`, so rows are reachable with the arrow keys and can run an action.

- Import: `import { ActionList } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/ActionList/ActionList.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/ActionList`): Default, Actionable, KeyboardNavigation, RowMenu, Borderless, WithLeadingAndLongText, DisabledRow, Empty, CustomEmpty, PortugueseBrazil

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly ActionListItem[]` | yes |  | The rows, in the order given. The list never sorts: lists are alphabetical by default in this design system, so sort with `sortByText` before passing them (tasks by urgency and dated records newest first are the exceptions). |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the list root. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the list root element. |
| `onAction` | `(item: ActionListItem) => void` |  |  | Called when the user activates a row (click, or Enter on the focused row). Makes the whole row a press target with hover and pointer cursor. The menu button does not trigger it. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Draws the border, surface and radius around the list. Turn off inside a `Card`. Default `true`. |
| `emptyState` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Content when `items` is empty. Default: an `EmptyState` with built-in text. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ moreActions: (title: string) => string; emptyTitle: string; emptyDescription: string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name of the list. Required unless `aria-labelledby` is set. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the list (a visible heading). |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaGridListProps` (react-aria): `escapeKeyBehavior`, `keyboardNavigationBehavior`
- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `GridListProps` (react-aria): `autoFocus`, `disabledBehavior`, `shouldSelectOnPressUp`
- From `GridListProps` (react-aria-components): `disallowTypeAhead`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ ActionList: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `moreActions(title: string)` | `More actions for {title}` | Accessible name of the row actions button. `title` is the text of the row ("More actions for Price list"). |
| `emptyTitle` | `No items found` | Title of the default empty state. |
| `emptyDescription` | `Try another filter or search term.` | Description of the default empty state. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-line-subtle`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-row-h`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-surface-row-hover`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- Short lists of things with a few actions each: files, saved filters, members, recent items.
- One main line of text per record, with secondary detail.

#### When not to use

- Many comparable columns, sorting or selection: use `DataTable`.
- Navigation between pages: use `NavItem` or `Tabs`.
- Choosing options in a form: use `RadioGroup`, `CheckboxGroup` or `Select`.

#### Anatomy

```
div[role=grid]            named by aria-label / aria-labelledby
  div[role=row]           one tab stop for the whole list; arrow keys move between rows
    span  leading         optional (Avatar, Icon)
    span  title / description
    span  meta            mono, text-2
    MoreActionsMenu       IconButton "More actions for {title}" + Menu (optional)
```

#### Props (key ones)

| Prop         | Type                | Default | Notes                                                                                 |
| ------------ | ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`      | `ActionListItem[]`  | -       | `id`, `title`, `textValue`, `description`, `meta`, `leading`, `actions`, `isDisabled` |
| `aria-label` | `string`            | -       | Required (or `aria-labelledby`)                                                       |
| `onAction`   | `(item) => void`    |         | Row click or Enter. Makes the row a press target                                      |
| `bordered`   | `boolean`           | `true`  | Border, surface and radius. Turn off inside a `Card`                                  |
| `emptyState` | `ReactNode`         |         | Default: compact `EmptyState` with built-in text                                      |
| `messages`   | `Partial<messages>` |         | `moreActions(title)`, `emptyTitle`, `emptyDescription`                                |

`actions` is a node: `MenuItem`, `MenuSection` and `MenuSeparator` elements from `Menu`. Put the handler on the item (`<MenuItem onAction={...}>`). Destructive items use `tone="danger"` and still ask for confirmation in a dialog.

The list renders `items` in the order given. Lists are alphabetical by default in this design system: pass them through `sortByText` first (exceptions: tasks by urgency, dated records newest first).

#### Accessibility

- `GridList` gives `role="grid"` with `row` and `gridcell` roles; rows are not a `list`/`listitem` pair because they are focusable and actionable.
- Keyboard: `Tab` enters the list on one row (one tab stop); Arrow Up/Down, Home and End move between rows; Arrow Right moves from the row to its menu button (Arrow Left back); `Enter` on a row runs `onAction`; the menu button follows the Menu contract (`Enter`/`Space`/`Arrow Down` opens, `Escape` closes and focus returns to the button).
- Every menu button has its own name ("More actions for Price list 2026") so a screen reader user can tell them apart.
- Row actions never rely on color; the meta value is text. Disabled rows are dimmed and skipped.
- Known quirk: React Aria moves focus to the row after an overlay inside a row closes. The component hands focus back to the button that was pressed.

#### Content rules

- Titles are the record name, not a sentence. Descriptions say who or when ("Updated by Ana").
- Menu items are verb + object ("Download file", "Delete file").

#### Examples

```tsx
<ActionList
  aria-label="Files"
  items={sortByText(files, (f) => f.name, locale).map((file) => ({
    id: file.id,
    title: file.name,
    description: `Updated by ${file.author}`,
    meta: formatBytes(file.size),
    actions: (
      <>
        <MenuItem onAction={() => download(file)}>Download file</MenuItem>
        <MenuSeparator />
        <MenuItem tone="danger" onAction={() => askToDelete(file)}>
          Delete file
        </MenuItem>
      </>
    ),
  }))}
  onAction={(item) => openFile(item.id)}
/>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see DataTable: Many comparable columns, sorting or selection: use `DataTable`.
- Instead, see NavItem: Navigation between pages: use `NavItem` or `Tabs`.
- Instead, see Tabs: Navigation between pages: use `NavItem` or `Tabs`.
- Instead, see RadioGroup: Choosing options in a form: use `RadioGroup`, `CheckboxGroup` or `Select`.
- Instead, see CheckboxGroup: Choosing options in a form: use `RadioGroup`, `CheckboxGroup` or `Select`.
- Instead, see Select: Choosing options in a form: use `RadioGroup`, `CheckboxGroup` or `Select`.
- Renders: EmptyState, MoreActionsMenu

### AgentCard

> A card for one agent: icon, name, status, description and a footer with the last activity
and the number of items waiting for approval.

The whole card is clickable through the "stretched link" pattern: the agent name inside the
heading is the only link (or button), and a pseudo-element extends its hit area over the
card. The accessible name is just the agent name; status, description and footer are the
description. There is no nested interactive element and no `role="button"` on a `div`.

A card that represents one AI agent: icon, name, status, description and a footer with the last activity and the number of items waiting for approval. The whole card opens the agent. Import it from `loui-ds/patterns`.

- Handoff source: `components/agents/AgentCard` (TODO `CMP-AGT-01`).

- Import: `import { AgentCard } from 'loui-ds/patterns';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/patterns/AgentCard/AgentCard.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Patterns/AgentCard`): Default, Testing, Paused, ComingSoon, AsLink, NothingPending, LongText, WithoutIcon, Grid, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | Name of the agent. It is the accessible name of the card's single link or button. |
| `area` | `string` |  |  | Short caption under the name (the area the agent works in). |
| `icon` | `LucideIcon` |  |  | Icon of the agent: any icon of the curated set (for example `SearchIcon`) or another Lucide icon. Decorative. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | One or two sentences about what the agent does. Part of the accessible description. |
| `status` | `'testing' \| 'active' \| 'paused' \| 'soon'` |  | `'active'` | Lifecycle of the agent. `testing`, `active` and `paused` are available. `soon` is not interactive: dashed border, no link, no pending count. Default `active`. |
| `pending` | `number` |  | `0` | Number of items waiting for approval. Shown (accent number plus text) only when above zero and the agent is available. |
| `lastActivity` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Text about the last activity ("Last reply sent at 08:40"). Shown in the footer. |
| `href` | `string` |  |  | Destination of the card. Renders a real link (router-aware through `DSProvider`). |
| `onOpen` | `() => void` |  |  | Called when the card is activated. Without `href` it renders a real button. |
| `headingLevel` | `'1' \| '2' \| '3' \| '4' \| '5' \| '6'` |  | `'3'` | Heading level of the agent name (`h1` to `h6`). Default `3`. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ statusTesting: string; statusActive: string; statusPaused: string; statusSoon: string; notConfigured: string; pending: (n: number) => string; }>` |  |  | Override the built-in messages for this instance. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ AgentCard: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `statusTesting` | `In testing` | Status badge text. |
| `statusActive` | `Active` |  |
| `statusPaused` | `Paused` |  |
| `statusSoon` | `Coming soon` |  |
| `notConfigured` | `Not set up yet` | Footer text of a card that is not available yet and has no last-activity text. |
| `pending(n: number)` | `to approve` | Text after the (separately styled) pending number: "4 to approve". |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-agent-card-gap`, `--ds-agent-card-icon-box-size`, `--ds-agent-card-min-height`, `--ds-agent-card-padding`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-body`, `--ds-fs-heading`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-lh-body`, `--ds-lh-heading`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-meta`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-line-subtle`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- A grid of agents (or automations) on an overview page, each leading to its own screen.
- To make "what needs me" visible: the accent number is the only call for attention on the card.

#### When not to use

- A generic clickable card of any other content: build it with `Card` and the same stretched-link technique.
- Several actions per card: this card has exactly one (open). Put other actions on the agent's own screen.

#### Pattern decision: stretched link

The card needs to be fully clickable, show a status badge and still have a clean accessible name. Three options were weighed:

1. Wrap the card in a link or button: the accessible name becomes the concatenation of every text inside (name, caption, status, description, footer), and block content inside a `<button>` is invalid HTML.
2. `div role="button"` (the handoff): no native semantics, and a badge nested in a button.
3. **Stretched link (chosen)**: the agent name, inside the heading, is the only real link or button. A `::after` pseudo-element on it covers the card, so a click anywhere activates it. The accessible name is just the agent name; the status, description and footer are the accessible description (`aria-describedby`). No nested interactive elements.

The focus ring is drawn around the whole card (`:has()` on the focused link), hover brightens the card border.

#### Anatomy

```
div (card, data-status)
  header
    icon box (decorative)
    h{headingLevel} > a | button   <- the only interactive element, stretched over the card
    area caption
    Badge (status)
  p description
  footer
    last activity text
    pending: accent number + "to approve"
```

#### Accessibility

- One tab stop per available card; `Enter` activates a link or button, `Space` also a button.
- The status is text in a `Badge` (color and dot only reinforce it) and is part of the description, so it is read after the name.
- A `soon` card has no link or button and no tab stop; the heading and the "Coming soon" badge say why.
- Count: "4 to approve" is real text in reading order (the number is just styled), pluralized and number-formatted through messages and `Intl`.
- Contrast: the caption and last-activity text use `--ds-text-3` on the surface (passes 4.5:1 there; do not move the card onto a raised surface). Forced colors: the ring becomes a `Highlight` outline.

#### Content rules

- Name: the agent's job in two or three words. Description: what it does and that you approve, in one or two sentences.
- Last activity in the past tense with a time: "Last reply sent at 08:40". Do not add decorative metrics.

#### Examples

```tsx
<AgentCard
  name="Marketplace agent"
  area="Marketplace"
  icon={ShoppingBag}
  status="active"
  pending={4}
  description="Answers buyer questions and reviews. You approve before it sends."
  lastActivity="Last reply sent at 08:40"
  href="/agents/marketplace"
/>
<AgentCard name="Chat agent" status="soon" description="Will draft orders from the conversation." />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Card: A generic clickable card of any other content: build it with `Card` and the same stretched-link technique.
- Renders: Badge, Icon

### Alert

> An inline message with a tone, an icon, an optional title, an action and a dismiss button.
The icon is decorative and a visually hidden prefix names the tone for screen readers.

An inline message with a tone, an icon, an optional title, one action and an optional dismiss button.

- Import: `import { Alert } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Alert/Alert.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Alert`): Default, Success, Warning, Danger, Urgent, StaticNotice, TitleOnly, TextOnly, WithAction, Dismissible, LongText, AllTones, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | `'info'` | Kind of message: `info` (neutral, default), `success`, `warning` or `danger`. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Short heading of the alert, in one line: what happened. Plain text, not a document heading. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  | The detail: why it happened and what to do. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  |  | A single action next to the text, usually a link or a small `Button` ("Update card"). |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` |  |  | Shows a dismiss button that calls this. The alert is removed by the parent. |
| `urgent` | `boolean` |  | `false` | The message interrupts the user's task and must be announced immediately (`role="alert"`, assertive). Use it only for failures the user must know about right now. |
| `announce` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Whether the alert is a live region (`role="status"`, polite). Default `true`, because most alerts appear after something the user did. Set `false` for a static notice that is part of the page content from the start: it then has no role and is read in page order. Ignored when `urgent`. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ dismiss: string; info: string; success: string; warning: string; danger: string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `tone`: `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Alert: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dismiss` | `Dismiss alert` | Name of the dismiss button. |
| `info` | `Information` | Visually hidden prefix that tells screen reader users the kind of alert; color and icon alone cannot. |
| `success` | `Success` |  |
| `warning` | `Warning` |  |
| `danger` | `Error` |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-alert-danger-bg`, `--ds-alert-danger-border`, `--ds-alert-success-bg`, `--ds-alert-success-border`, `--ds-alert-warning-bg`, `--ds-alert-warning-border`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- Explain a state that affects the page or a form: a declined payment, a scheduled maintenance, a failed import.
- Tell the user what to do about it, next to the thing it is about.

#### When not to use

- Feedback about an action that just finished ("Order #1051 created"): use `Toast`.
- A confirmation that needs a decision: use `Dialog`.
- A field error: use the field's error message.
- A status of a record (Shipped, Failed): use `Badge`.

#### Anatomy

```
div[role=status | alert | none]  (tinted surface, 1px tinted border, radius lg)
  Icon (decorative)  info | success | warning (triangle) | danger
  content
    VisuallyHidden   "Information" | "Success" | "Warning" | "Error"
    title            optional, 14/22, weight 500
    children         13/18, text-2
  actions            action slot · dismiss IconButton
```

#### Accessibility: role decisions

- **Default `role="status"` (polite).** Most alerts appear after something the user did (submit, import). A status region is announced politely, without stealing focus or interrupting speech. The handoff used `role="alert"` for every `danger` alert, which interrupts for things that are not urgent; urgency is now an explicit `urgent` prop, not a function of the tone.
- **`urgent` gives `role="alert"` (assertive).** Use it for a failure the user must know right now (lost connection, session expired). Avoid more than one at a time.
- **`announce={false}` gives no role.** A notice that is part of the page when it loads (a permanent banner, a form-level note) does not need a live region; screen readers read it in page order. A live region that never changes is noise, and many `status` regions on one page are worse.
- Live regions announce **changes**: for the announcement to work, render the Alert when the event happens and keep the region mounted; do not render it hidden and unhide it.
- **The tone is not only color and icon.** The icon is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden prefix ("Error", "Warning", "Success", "Information", from messages) names the kind of alert for screen readers.
- The **dismiss button** is an `IconButton` named "Dismiss alert" (messages), reachable by Tab and operated with Enter or Space. After dismissing, the parent should move focus somewhere sensible if the alert held it.
- Text contrast on the tinted backgrounds is at least 4.5:1 (checked in the browser test with the real computed colors). The 6% and 30% tints are component tokens (`--ds-alert-*`).
- Forced colors: the browser repaints border and icon with system colors; the icon and the hidden tone prefix still name the tone.

#### Content rules

- Title: what happened, sentence case, no exclamation marks ("Payment declined").
- Text: why and what to do ("The card ending in 4242 was declined. Use another card.").
- The action is a verb plus object ("Update card"), not "Click here".

#### Examples

```tsx
<Alert title="Scheduled maintenance">Sunday, 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" title="Payment declined" action={<Link href="/billing">Update card</Link>}>
  The card ending in 4242 was declined.
</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" urgent title="Connection lost" onDismiss={() => setOffline(false)}>
  Changes are not being saved.
</Alert>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Dialog: A confirmation that needs a decision: use `Dialog`.
- Instead, see Badge: A status of a record (Shipped, Failed): use `Badge`.
- Renders: Icon, IconButton, VisuallyHidden

### ApprovalCard

> A reply waiting for approval: the original message, an editable draft written by an agent
and two actions, send and discard.

It is an `article` named by its heading ("Review buyer_sp"). Send and discard are secondary
and ghost buttons on purpose: a screen has many of these cards and only one primary action.
They act immediately; the consumer shows an Undo toast instead of asking for confirmation.

A reply waiting for approval: the original message, an editable draft written by an agent, an optional warning and two actions, send and discard. Import it from `loui-ds/patterns`.

- Handoff source: `components/agents/ApprovalCard` (TODO `CMP-AGT-02`).

- Import: `import { ApprovalCard } from 'loui-ds/patterns';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/patterns/ApprovalCard/ApprovalCard.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Patterns/ApprovalCard`): Default, Review, LowRatingWithFlag, Minimal, LongText, RightToLeft, SendWithUndo

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The original message the draft answers. Plain text or nodes. |
| `kind` | `'question' \| 'review'` |  | `'question'` | What is being answered: a `question` or a `review`. Shown as a text badge. Default `question`. |
| `author` | `string` |  |  | Who wrote it (a username or code). Shown in mono and part of the card's accessible name. |
| `itemName` | `string` |  |  | Reference to the item the message is about (a product or order name). |
| `itemColor` | `string` |  |  | Hex color (`#rgb` or `#rrggbb`) shown as a dot before `itemName`. Decorative: `itemName` must name it. |
| `when` | `ReactNode` |  |  | When it was written, as display text ("today, 10:40"). |
| `whenDateTime` | `string` |  |  | Machine-readable date for `when` (an ISO string). Renders a `<time>`. |
| `rating` | `number` |  |  | Star rating of a `review` (0 to 5, halves allowed). Shown only for reviews. |
| `draft` | `string` |  |  | Controlled value of the draft reply. |
| `defaultDraft` | `string` |  |  | Initial value of the draft when uncontrolled. |
| `onDraftChange` | `(draft: string) => void` |  |  | Called with the new text whenever the draft is edited. |
| `flag` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Warning shown above the actions (for example "2-star review: read it carefully before sending"). Linked to the card as its description. Reviews of 1 to 3 stars should always have one. |
| `onSend` | `() => void` |  |  | Called when the send button is pressed. Do it now and offer Undo with a toast; do not ask to confirm. |
| `onDiscard` | `() => void` |  |  | Called when the discard button is pressed. Do it now and offer Undo with a toast. |
| `headingLevel` | `'1' \| '2' \| '3' \| '4' \| '5' \| '6'` |  | `'3'` | Heading level of the card heading (`h1` to `h6`). Default `3`. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ kindQuestion: string; kindReview: string; messageLabel: string; draftLabel: string; draftHint: string; send: string; discard: string; }>` |  |  | Override the built-in messages for this instance. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ ApprovalCard: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kindQuestion` | `Question` | Kind badge and the first word of the accessible name. |
| `kindReview` | `Review` |  |
| `messageLabel` | `Customer message` | Visually hidden label before the original message. |
| `draftLabel` | `Agent reply` | Label and hint of the editable draft. |
| `draftHint` | `You can edit before sending` |  |
| `send` | `Send reply` | Verb plus object buttons. The card's heading describes which card they belong to. |
| `discard` | `Discard reply` |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-approval-card-body-padding-block`, `--ds-approval-card-gap`, `--ds-approval-card-header-min-height`, `--ds-approval-card-header-padding-block`, `--ds-approval-card-padding`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-meta`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-line-subtle`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- An approval queue: replies, messages or changes an agent prepared that go to a customer or touch money.
- Any "review the draft, edit it, send or discard it" step with many items on one screen.

#### When not to use

- A single decision with a consequence you cannot take back: use a `Dialog` with a confirmation.
- Free chat with an agent: use `ChatPanel`.

#### Principles

**Approve before sending.** Anything an agent writes to a customer goes through this card first. The draft is editable ("You can edit before sending"). Reviews of 1 to 3 stars always carry a `flag`.

**Undo, don't confirm.** Send and discard act immediately. Do not open a confirmation dialog; show a toast with **Undo** (see the recipe below). A confirmation for every card would train people to click through it.

**Secondary buttons, on purpose.** A screen has many cards and only one primary action (AGENTS.md section 5). Send is `secondary`, Discard is `ghost`. The button text is verb plus object ("Send reply", "Discard reply"), not a bare "Send".

#### Anatomy

```
article (named by the heading)
  header
    h{headingLevel}    Badge (Question | Review) + author in mono   <- the accessible name
    Rating             reviews only
    item               optional Swatch dot + item name
    time               when
  body
    message            original text, visually hidden label "Customer message:"
    Textarea           label "Agent reply", aside "You can edit before sending"
    flag               optional warning (icon + text), the card's description
    actions            Discard (ghost)                 Send (secondary)
```

#### Undo recipe

```tsx
function Queue() {
  const toast = useToast();
  function send(reply: Reply) {
    const previous = reply.state; // save what you need to reverse
    markSent(reply.id); // 1. do it now
    toast.success('Reply sent', {
      // 2. say so, past tense
      action: { label: 'Undo', onPress: () => restore(reply.id, previous) }, // 3. reverse it
    });
  }
  return replies.map((reply) => (
    <ApprovalCard
      key={reply.id}
      {...reply}
      onSend={() => send(reply)}
      onDiscard={() => discard(reply)}
    />
  ));
}
```

The real side effect (actually sending to the customer) should be held for the undo window, or undone by a compensating action; see the Toast documentation. After send or discard, remove the card from the queue and move focus to the next card's heading or to the list, so keyboard focus is not lost.

#### Accessibility

- `article` named by its heading through `aria-labelledby` ("Review buyer_sp"); with several cards, screen reader users can jump by heading or article.
- The two buttons are described by the heading (`aria-describedby`), so "Send reply, Review buyer_sp" is spoken without making every button name unique.
- The kind is a text badge, the rating is an image with a text alternative, the flag is text with a decorative icon: nothing relies on color alone. The flag uses `--ds-warning` on the surface (4.5:1 or better).
- Tab order follows reading order: draft, Discard, Send. The draft is a real labelled `Textarea` (its hint is the field description).
- The original message is announced after a hidden "Customer message:" label.

#### Content rules

- The draft is a customer-facing reply: short, factual, no promises about delivery time or discounts, no emoji (AGENTS.md section 5). That is the agent's job; the card only makes it visible and editable.
- `flag` explains the risk and what to do: "2-star review: read it carefully before sending."

#### Related components

- Instead, see Dialog: A single decision with a consequence you cannot take back: use a `Dialog` with a confirmation.
- Instead, see ChatPanel: Free chat with an agent: use `ChatPanel`.
- Renders: Badge, Button, Icon, Rating, Swatch, Textarea, VisuallyHidden

### AppShell

> The application layout: a sidebar, and a main column with a top bar above a scrollable
content region. The sidebar and the content scroll independently; the page itself does not.

Landmarks: the sidebar (`aside`, from `Sidebar`), the top bar (`header`), one `main`
(`id="main"`), and the optional detail `aside`. A skip link to `main` comes first.

Responsive contract (TOK-010): the shell measures its own width (a container query, so it
also works inside a frame). From `--ds-breakpoint-md` (768px) up the sidebar sits in the flow.
Below it the sidebar leaves the flow and opens as an off-canvas panel over the content,
controlled by `isNavOpen` and `AppShellNavToggle`; while it is open the rest of the page is
inert, `Escape` and the scrim close it, and focus returns to the toggle. The shell works from
320px. It fills its parent: give the parent a height, or it takes the viewport height.

The application layout: a sidebar, and a main column with a top bar above a scrollable content region. It includes the skip link and the landmarks.

- Import: `import { AppShell } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/AppShell/AppShell.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Layout/AppShell`): Default, WithDetail, WithoutSidebar, Unpadded, LongContent, NarrowClosed, NarrowOpen, Narrow320, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sidebar` | `ReactNode` |  |  | The app sidebar: a `Sidebar` element. Below the md breakpoint it becomes an off-canvas panel. |
| `topBar` | `ReactNode` |  |  | The page header: a `TopBar` element. Put an `AppShellNavToggle` in its `children` so narrow screens can open the sidebar. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  | The page content. It is rendered inside the one `main` landmark. |
| `detail` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Optional detail pane at the inline end, `--ds-app-shell-detail-w` (360px) wide, for the record selected in the main content. It is an `aside` landmark with its own scroll. Below the md breakpoint it moves under the main content. |
| `detailLabel` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name of the detail aside. Default "Details" from the message catalog. |
| `mainId` | `string` |  | `main` | `id` of the `main` element, and the target of the skip link. Default `main`. |
| `padded` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Pads the main content with `--ds-app-shell-main-padding`. Turn it off when the content brings its own padding (a `Container` has a gutter). Default `true`. |
| `skipLink` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Renders the skip link as the first focusable element. Default `true`; turn it off only if the app has its own. |
| `isNavOpen` | `boolean` |  |  | Controlled state of the off-canvas sidebar (narrow screens only). Pair with `onNavOpenChange`. |
| `defaultNavOpen` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Initial state of the off-canvas sidebar when uncontrolled. Default `false`. |
| `onNavOpenChange` | `(isOpen: boolean) => void` |  |  | Called when the off-canvas sidebar opens or closes (toggle, `Escape`, scrim, close button). |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ navToggle: string; navClose: string; detail: string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ AppShell: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `navToggle` | `Menu` | Text of the button that opens the navigation panel on narrow screens. |
| `navClose` | `Close menu` | Text of the button that closes the navigation panel on narrow screens. |
| `detail` | `Details` | Accessible name of the detail aside landmark. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-app-shell-detail-w`, `--ds-app-shell-main-padding`, `--ds-app-shell-nav-z-index`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-line-subtle`, `--ds-scrim`, `--ds-shadow-dialog`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-12`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-toast-clearance`

#### When to use

- The frame of every screen of an app: `Sidebar` + `TopBar` + content (+ optional detail pane).

#### When not to use

- A marketing page or a single-column document: use `Container` and let the page scroll.
- Inside another AppShell.

#### Anatomy

```
div.root  (container, fills the parent, no page scroll)
  SkipLink                       first focusable element
  div.nav                        wraps the Sidebar (aside); off-canvas below md
  div.scrim                      only when the panel is open
  div.column
    TopBar                       header
    div.body
      main#main                  scrolls on its own
      aside "Details"            optional, 360px, scrolls on its own
```

#### Responsive decision (TOK-010)

**The DS guarantees every component works from 320px wide, and AppShell collapses its sidebar into an off-canvas panel below `--ds-breakpoint-md` (768px).**

Why built in rather than left to apps: a sidebar hidden by an app without a way back strands keyboard and touch users, and every product would build the same panel. It is kept simple: it reuses the same `Sidebar` element (no second copy, no lost state) and CSS does the layout.

- The shell measures **its own width** with a container query, so it behaves the same in a frame, a preview or a test. The 768px in the CSS is `--ds-breakpoint-md`; CSS cannot read variables inside a query, so `AppShell.test.tsx` asserts the two agree at 767/768px.
- From md up the sidebar sits in the flow. Below, it leaves the flow; `AppShellNavToggle` (visible only below md) opens it as a panel over a scrim.
- While open: focus moves into the panel, the rest of the page is `inert`, `Escape`, the scrim or the "Close menu" button close it, and focus returns to the toggle. It is not a `Dialog`: it keeps the sidebar's own landmarks.
- The detail pane moves **under** the main content (half the height at most, own scroll) below md.
- Breakpoint tokens: `--ds-breakpoint-sm|md|lg|xl` (480 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 px); content: `--ds-content-max`, `--ds-content-gutter`; `--ds-container-sm|md|lg`.

#### Accessibility

- Landmarks: `aside` (Sidebar, "Sidebar"), `header` (TopBar), **one** `main`, optional `aside` ("Details"). Each `nav` in the sidebar is named by its caption.
- The skip link is the first stop and moves focus to `main`.
- `main` and the detail aside scroll independently. While they overflow they become keyboard stops (`tabindex="0"`) so the arrow keys scroll them; with nothing to scroll there is no extra tab stop.
- The closed panel is `visibility: hidden` and `inert`, so it is out of the tab order and the accessibility tree.
- The panel slide respects `prefers-reduced-motion`; the layout mirrors in RTL.
- `AppShellNavToggle` reports `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. It is an `IconButton` (menu icon) named "Menu" (`pt-BR` "Menu"; pass a string child to rename it); the close button is an `IconButton` (x icon) named "Close menu" / "Fechar menu", which sits on the scrim beside the panel and never wraps.

#### Content rules

- One `h1` per page: `TopBar` renders it from `title`.
- One primary action per screen, at the end of the top bar.

#### Examples

```tsx
<AppShell
  sidebar={<Sidebar workspace={workspace} sections={sections} value={route} onChange={go} />}
  topBar={
    <TopBar title="Orders" actions={<Button variant="primary">New order</Button>}>
      <AppShellNavToggle />
    </TopBar>
  }
  detail={selected ? <OrderDetail order={selected} /> : undefined}
>
  <OrdersTable />
</AppShell>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Container: A marketing page or a single-column document: use `Container` and let the page scroll.
- Renders: IconButton, SkipLink

### AppShellNavToggle

> The icon button (menu icon) that opens the off-canvas sidebar. Put it in the `TopBar` (as its `children`).
It is only visible below the md breakpoint, and reports `aria-expanded`. It must be rendered
inside `AppShell`.

The application layout: a sidebar, and a main column with a top bar above a scrollable content region. It includes the skip link and the landmarks.

- Import: `import { AppShellNavToggle } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/AppShell/AppShell.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Layout/AppShell`): Default, WithDetail, WithoutSidebar, Unpadded, LongContent, NarrowClosed, NarrowOpen, Narrow320, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name of the icon button. Default "Menu" from the message catalog. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the wrapper. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-app-shell-detail-w`, `--ds-app-shell-main-padding`, `--ds-app-shell-nav-z-index`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-line-subtle`, `--ds-scrim`, `--ds-shadow-dialog`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-12`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-toast-clearance`

#### When to use
