| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`                                                           | One is required.                                                                                                                |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange`                                                                | ISO string or `null`.                                                                                                           |
| `min`, `max`                                                                                         | ISO strings. Outside days are disabled in the grid; typed dates outside are invalid. "Today" is disabled when today is outside. |
| `description`, `errorMessage`, `size`, `name`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly` | As in `Select`.                                                                                                                 |
| `messages`                                                                                           | `today`, `clear`, `openCalendar`, `previousMonth`, `nextMonth`, `requiredMark`.                                                 |

`Calendar` takes `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange(iso)`, `min`, `max`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`, `autoFocus`, `messages`, and requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

#### Locale

Segment order and separators, placeholders (`dd/mm/aaaa`), month names, weekday letters and the first day of the week come from the `DSProvider` locale through React Aria; there are no hard-coded names. Only the button texts are in the message catalog (`Calendar` key for the month buttons, `DatePicker` for the rest).

#### Accessibility and keyboard

| Key (calendar grid)               | Behavior                                                      |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Arrows                            | Previous / next day, previous / next week                     |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown`             | Previous / next month                                         |
| `Shift+PageUp` / `Shift+PageDown` | Previous / next year                                          |
| `Home` / `End`                    | First / last day of the **month** (React Aria; APG says week) |
| `Enter` / `Space`                 | Select the focused day                                        |
| `Escape`                          | Close the popover, focus returns to the button                |

In the field: digits fill the segment and move to the next; arrows change a segment's value; `Backspace` clears a segment; `Tab` moves between segments. Each day is named with its full date ("Wednesday, October 28, 2026", "Today, ..."), so the grid is usable without sight. Today has a ring (`--ds-text-3`), the selected day an accent fill with `--ds-text-inverse`; disabled days are dimmed and `aria-disabled`.

#### Content rules

Label with the date's role ("Delivery date"). Errors say how to fix: "Choose a date after today."

#### Example

```tsx
<DatePicker
  label="Delivery date"
  name="delivery"
  min="2026-10-30"
  value={date}
  onChange={setDate}
/>
```

#### Dependency note

The component imports `@internationalized/date`, which React Aria already depends on. It is not a direct dependency of this package yet, so under pnpm's strict layout it must be added to `package.json` (`pnpm add @internationalized/date@^3.12.4`, already in the lockfile as a transitive dependency).

#### Related components

- Renders: Button, FieldMessages, Icon, Label

### Description

> Helper text under a field (the handoff `hint`). Linked to the control with
`aria-describedby` by the surrounding React Aria field. It stays visible when an error shows.

Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

- Import: `import { Description } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Field/Field.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Field`): Anatomy, ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt, RealtimeValidation

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### Exports

| Export                                 | What it is                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Label`                                | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker.                                                         |
| `Description`                          | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`.                                                     |
| `FieldError`                           | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. |
| `FieldMessages`                        | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box.                                                                                  |
| `RequiredMark`                         | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`.                                                                                                       |
| `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel`      | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel<P>` helps type stories.                                       |
| `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result).                                                                               |

#### Anatomy and spacing

```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

#### One state model (ARCH-009)

| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

#### Required marker

`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

#### Validation behavior: native (default), and why

React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language. A static `errorMessage` replaces only that browser text: a message the app supplied (a `validate` rule or `validationErrors` on a `Form`) is shown instead (GAP-009).
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

#### Accessibility

- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

#### Related components

- Used by: FileUpload, Radio, RadioGroup

### Dialog

> A modal dialog built on React Aria `DialogTrigger`, `ModalOverlay`, `Modal` and `Dialog`.

React Aria traps focus, restores it to the trigger on close, locks page scroll, hides the
rest of the page from assistive technology and closes only the top-most layer on `Escape`
(a Dialog opened from a Sheet closes first). Initial focus goes to the dialog itself unless
a child has `autoFocus`; for destructive confirmations use `ConfirmDialog`, which focuses
Cancel.

A modal dialog, and `ConfirmDialog` for destructive confirmations. Built on React Aria `DialogTrigger`, `ModalOverlay`, `Modal` and `Dialog`.

- Handoff source: `components/feedback/Dialog` (CMP-FBK-03). Overlay management: ARCH-005.

- Import: `import { Dialog } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Dialog/Dialog.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/ConfirmDialog`): Default, ConfirmByKeyboard, EscapeCancels, ConfirmFlow, Open, Neutral, Pending, WithDetails, Default, Open, Medium, Large, WithoutBody, LongContent, LongTitle, InsideSheet, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Heading of the dialog and its accessible name. A question for a confirmation ("Delete order #1048?"), otherwise a noun phrase or a verb plus object ("Edit customer"). |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | One or two sentences under the title. It is linked to the dialog with `aria-describedby`, so screen readers read it right after the title. |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| ((options: DialogRenderOptions) => ReactNode)` |  |  | Body of the dialog. A function receives `close`. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode \| ((options: DialogRenderOptions) => ReactNode)` |  |  | Actions, aligned to the end of the footer. Cancel (secondary) before the confirming action; one primary action at most. A function receives `close`. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'sm'` | Maximum width: `sm` 420px (default), `md` 540px, `lg` 680px. Narrower on small screens. |
| `role` | `'dialog' \| 'alertdialog'` |  | `'dialog'` | `dialog` (default), or `alertdialog` for a message that needs an answer before the user continues, such as a destructive confirmation. `ConfirmDialog` uses `alertdialog`. |
| `trigger` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  |  | The element that opens the dialog (a `Button`). Optional: omit it and control the dialog with `isOpen`. Focus returns to the element that was focused when the dialog opened. |
| `isOpen` | `boolean` |  |  | Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  |  | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(isOpen: boolean) => void` |  |  | Called when the dialog opens or closes. |
| `isDismissable` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Whether pressing the overlay closes the dialog. Default `true`; `ConfirmDialog` sets `false`. |
| `isKeyboardDismissDisabled` | `boolean` |  |  | Disables closing with `Escape`. Use it only while a request is running. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the dialog panel. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  | Ref to the dialog panel. |

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cancel` | `Cancel` | Label of the button that dismisses a `ConfirmDialog` without doing anything. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-dialog-gutter`, `--ds-dialog-padding`, `--ds-dialog-width-lg`, `--ds-dialog-width-md`, `--ds-dialog-width-sm`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-heading`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-heading`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-overlay`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-shadow-dialog`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- A short task or decision that blocks the page: edit a record in a small form, confirm a deletion.
- `ConfirmDialog`: every deletion. "Deleting always asks for confirmation" (AGENTS.md section 5).

#### When not to use

- Reversible actions (mark, link, change status): do them and offer **Undo** in a `Toast`. Do not confirm.
- Viewing or editing a record next to its list: use `Sheet`.
- Interactive content anchored to a control: use `Popover`.
- A message about the page: use `Alert`.
- Nesting dialogs more than two deep.

#### Anatomy

```
DialogTrigger
  trigger            Button                                (optional when controlled)
  ModalOverlay       --ds-overlay, z dialog
    Modal            raised surface, strong line, radius lg, dialog shadow, width sm | md | lg
      Dialog         role=dialog | alertdialog, aria-labelledby = title, aria-describedby = description
        header       h2 title (17/24, 600) · description (14/22, text-2)
        body         scrolls
        footer       actions aligned to the end; divider when there is a body
```

#### Accessibility

- Focus is **trapped** while open, **restored** to the element that opened it, the page behind is `inert`/`aria-hidden` and does not scroll (all React Aria).
- **Initial focus.** Plain `Dialog`: the dialog itself, or the child with `autoFocus` (put it on the first field). `ConfirmDialog`: **Cancel**, so pressing Enter or Space as soon as it opens never confirms. The handoff focused nothing.
- `Escape` closes **only the top-most layer**. A `Dialog` opened from a `Sheet` closes first and the Sheet stays (tested). Every overlay uses React Aria's shared layer stack instead of its own window listener (ARCH-005).
- Named by the title (`aria-labelledby`, from the `h2`) and described by the description (`aria-describedby`; not linked in the handoff).
- `ConfirmDialog` uses `alertdialog`, which screen readers announce with its description. A press outside does not dismiss it.
- Reduced motion: the 150 ms fade and 8 px rise are removed. Forced colors: border in `CanvasText`.
- 320 px reflow: the dialog shrinks to the viewport less the 24 px gutter and the body scrolls.

##### Layers

Overlays are portaled to `body`, each with its own layer: sheet (40) < dialog (45) < dropdown (50) < popover (55) < toast (58) < tooltip (60). A `Select`, `Menu`, `Popover` or `Combobox` opened from inside a Dialog or Sheet therefore renders **above** it. This is safe because a modal blocks page-level popovers while it is open. Tests assert the order.

#### Content rules

- Title: a question for confirmations that names the object ("Delete order #1048?"), otherwise verb plus object or a noun phrase ("Edit customer"). Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
- Description: the consequence in one sentence ("The order and its 14 lines will be removed. This can't be undone.").
- Buttons: Cancel (secondary) then the action, verb plus object ("Save customer", "Delete order"). Never "OK" or "Yes". One primary action.
- After a confirmed delete show a `Toast` with **Undo** when the data can come back.

#### Examples

```tsx
<ConfirmDialog
  trigger={<Button variant="danger">Delete order</Button>}
  title="Delete order #1048?"
  description="The order and its 14 lines will be removed. This can't be undone."
  confirmLabel="Delete order"
  onConfirm={() => deleteOrder(1048)}
/>

<Dialog
  trigger={<Button>Edit customer</Button>}
  title="Edit customer"
  footer={({ close }) => (
    <>
      <Button onPress={close}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={save}>Save customer</Button>
    </>
  )}
>
  <Input label="Name" autoFocus />
</Dialog>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Sheet: Viewing or editing a record next to its list: use `Sheet`.
- Instead, see Popover: Interactive content anchored to a control: use `Popover`.
- Instead, see Alert: A message about the page: use `Alert`.
- Used by: ShortcutsHelp

### Divider

> A 1px line that separates groups of content, built on React Aria `Separator`
(`<hr>`, or `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation` when vertical). Prefer spacing to
separate related things; use a divider where the content changes topic.

A 1px line that separates groups of content. Built on React Aria `Separator`.

- Import: `import { Divider } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Divider/Divider.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Layout/Divider`): Default, Subtle, Strong, Vertical, Weights

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` |  | `'horizontal'` | `horizontal` (default) separates stacked content; `vertical` separates items in a row and needs a parent with a height. |
| `variant` | `'subtle' \| 'default' \| 'strong'` |  | `'default'` | Line weight by token: `subtle` (`--ds-line-subtle`, internal dividers), `default` (`--ds-line`, between cards and sections) or `strong` (`--ds-line-strong`, around controls and overlays). Default `default`. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  | Ref to the separator element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `SeparatorProps` (react-aria): `elementType`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `variant`: `subtle`, `default`, `strong`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-line`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-line-subtle`

#### When to use

- Between sections of a panel or a menu-like list where the topic changes.
- Vertically, between inline groups in a toolbar.

#### When not to use

- To separate closely related items: use spacing.
- Around every field or row: borders-first hierarchy comes from surfaces, not a line between everything.
- To wrap a Card in a Card: use a divider inside one card instead.

#### Anatomy

```
hr (1px line)          horizontal
div[role=separator]    vertical, with aria-orientation
```

#### Accessibility

- Rendered by React Aria: a horizontal divider is an `<hr>`; a vertical one has `role="separator"` and `aria-orientation="vertical"`.
- It is a thematic break for assistive technology, so do not use it as a pure visual rule between unrelated things.
- Line colors are borders, not text; `forced-colors` paints them with `CanvasText`.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Stack gap={4}>
  <Section />
  <Divider />
  <Section />
</Stack>

<Inline>
  <Button>Bold</Button>
  <Divider orientation="vertical" />
  <Button>Link</Button>
</Inline>
```

### DonutMeter

> A circular meter for one proportion: how much of a whole is used, done or filled (storage
used, goal reached, stock level). The percentage is printed in the center, formatted with
`Intl` for the active locale. Built on React Aria `Meter` (`role="meter"` with
`aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext`).

It needs an accessible name: a visible `label` (printed under the ring), `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby`. For a task that makes progress use `Progress`; for a bar use `Meter`;
for one proportion among several use `ProportionBar`.

A circular meter for one proportion: how much of a whole is used, done or filled (storage used, goal reached, stock level). The percentage is printed in the center, formatted with `Intl` for the active locale. Built on React Aria `Meter` (`role="meter"`). It is a separate component from `Progress`/`Meter`, in its own folder, and does not change them.

- TODO `GAP-007`.

- Import: `import { DonutMeter } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/DonutMeter/DonutMeter.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/DonutMeter`): Default, Small, Large, Neutral, Success, Warning, Danger, Empty, Full, CustomRange, CustomCenter, WithoutCenterValue, AriaLabelOnly, LongLabel, Portuguese, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | `'accent'` | Color of the ring: `accent` (default), `neutral`, `success`, `warning` or `danger`. Color is never the only signal: the percentage is printed in the center and the label says what it is. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | Diameter token: `sm` 48px, `md` 72px (default), `lg` 96px. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Prints the percentage in the center. On by default. Turn it off when the center is empty on purpose. |
| `centerLabel` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Replaces the percentage in the center ("12" over "days"). Visual only: screen readers get `valueLabel` (or the percentage) as the value of the meter. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the meter element. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `ProgressBarBaseProps` (react-aria): `formatOptions`, `maxValue`, `minValue`, `value`, `valueLabel`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`
- `tone`: `neutral`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-donut-meter-color`, `--ds-donut-meter-size-lg`, `--ds-donut-meter-size-md`, `--ds-donut-meter-size-sm`, `--ds-donut-meter-stroke-w`, `--ds-donut-meter-value`, `--ds-duration-progress`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-heading`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-fs-num`, `--ds-lh-heading`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-meta`, `--ds-lh-num`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- One share of a known total, as a compact visual in a card or a table cell.
- When the center number is the main message and the ring supports it.

#### When not to use

- Progress of a task that is running: use `Progress`.
- A bar in a column or a row: use `Meter` (`Progress` module).
- Several parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.
- A trend over time: use `Sparkline` or `Chart`.

#### Anatomy

```
div[role=meter] aria-valuenow/min/max/valuetext
  div.ring
    svg[aria-hidden]   (track circle + filled circle)
    span.center        (percentage or centerLabel)
  label                (optional, under the ring)
```

#### Accessibility

- `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` from React Aria. An accessible name is required (types and a development warning). The drawing is hidden from assistive technology; the center text is covered by `aria-valuetext`.
- Color is never the only signal: the percentage is printed in the center. The ring and track keep 3:1 against the surface in every tone.
- Motion: the ring animates 300ms; none under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Forced colors: track `GrayText`, ring `CanvasText`.
- Not interactive and not focusable.

#### Content rules

- Label: what is measured, in sentence case ("Storage used"). The unit and total belong in `valueLabel` ("6.2 of 10 GB").
- Pair a tone change with text that says why ("Almost full").

#### Examples

```tsx
<DonutMeter label="Storage used" value={62} />

<DonutMeter
  label="Storage"
  value={6.2}
  maxValue={10}
  valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB"
  tone="warning"
  size="lg"
/>

<DonutMeter aria-label="Trial" value={40} centerLabel="12 d" valueLabel="12 days left" />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Progress: Progress of a task that is running: use `Progress`.
- Instead, see Meter: A bar in a column or a row: use `Meter` (`Progress` module).
- Instead, see ProportionBar: Several parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.
- Instead, see Sparkline: A trend over time: use `Sparkline` or `Chart`.
- Instead, see Chart: A trend over time: use `Sparkline` or `Chart`.

### Drawer

> A non-modal side panel for filters, inspectors and secondary navigation. It sits next to the
content in the page flow: there is no scrim, the page stays interactive, focus is not trapped
and the page is not made inert. Place it as a sibling of the main content inside a flex or grid
container; it renders nothing while closed.

Use `Sheet` instead when the panel is a task that must be finished or dismissed first
(editing one record): that one is modal.

`Escape` closes the drawer while focus is inside it and returns focus to the trigger.

A non-modal side panel that sits next to the content, for filters, inspectors and secondary navigation. There is no scrim, the page stays interactive and focus is not trapped. Generic: it lives in the core entry point.

- Import: `import { Drawer } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Drawer/Drawer.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Drawer`): Default, AtStart, Small, Large, Region, Unpadded, LongContent, Rtl, OpenAndCloseWithKeyboard

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Heading of the drawer and its accessible name. |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| ((options: DrawerRenderOptions) => ReactNode)` |  |  | Body of the drawer; it scrolls when it is taller than the drawer. A function receives `close`. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode \| ((options: DrawerRenderOptions) => ReactNode)` |  |  | Footer actions, aligned to the end. A function receives `close`. |
| `placement` | `'start' \| 'end'` |  | `'end'` | Edge the drawer sits against: `end` (default) or `start`. Both follow the writing direction. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | Width: `sm` 280px, `md` 320px (default), `lg` 400px. It never exceeds its container. |
| `padded` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Pads the body. Turn it off for a table or a full-bleed list. Default `true`. |
| `isOpen` | `boolean` |  |  | Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(isOpen: boolean) => void` |  |  | Called when the drawer opens or closes through the user (close button or `Escape`). |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Moves focus into the drawer when it opens after the first render. A drawer that is open on first render never takes focus. Default `true`; turn it off for a panel that should stay beside the page without interrupting what the user is doing. |
| `role` | `'complementary' \| 'region'` |  | `'complementary'` | Landmark role. `complementary` (default) for content that supports the page (filters, inspectors); `region` for a section the user may want to find in the landmark list. |
| `headingLevel` | `'1' \| '2' \| '3' \| '4' \| '5' \| '6'` |  | `'2'` | Level of the title heading. Default `2`. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ close: string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the drawer panel. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  | Ref to the drawer panel. |

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Drawer: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `close` | `Close panel` | Name of the close button in the Drawer header. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-drawer-from`, `--ds-drawer-padding`, `--ds-drawer-shift`, `--ds-drawer-width`, `--ds-drawer-width-lg`, `--ds-drawer-width-md`, `--ds-drawer-width-sm`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-heading`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-heading`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-line-subtle`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-topbar-h`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### Drawer or Sheet

|          | Drawer                                                                   | Sheet                                                      |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Modality | Non-modal: page stays usable                                             | Modal: page is `inert`, scroll locked                      |
| Layout   | In the page flow, beside the content                                     | Overlay above the page, with a scrim                       |
| Focus    | Not trapped; Tab leaves the drawer                                       | Trapped and restored                                       |
| Use for  | Filters, inspector for the current selection, secondary navigation, help | Viewing or editing one record, a task to finish or dismiss |

Rule of thumb: if the user should keep working in the page while the panel is open, use a `Drawer`. If the panel is a task that needs a decision before going back, use a `Sheet`.

#### When not to use

- A short confirmation or form: `Dialog`.
- A few controls anchored to a button: `Popover`.
- Top-level navigation: `Sidebar`.

#### Anatomy

```
aside (role complementary | region, aria-labelledby = title)
  header     --ds-topbar-h tall: heading + close IconButton
  body       scrolls; padded or not
  footer     optional, end-aligned actions
```

Place the drawer as a sibling of the main content in a flex or grid container. It renders nothing while closed and does not animate out.

#### Accessibility

- A named landmark (`complementary` by default, `region` on request) labelled by its title.
- Not modal: nothing is hidden from assistive technology and Tab moves freely between the drawer and the page.
- When the drawer opens after first render, focus moves to the panel (it is programmatically focusable, `tabIndex=-1`), so the next Tab reaches its first control. A drawer that is open on first render never takes focus; set `autoFocus={false}` to keep focus where it is.
- `Escape` closes the drawer when focus is inside it (and when no inner overlay handled it) and focus returns to the element that had it before the drawer opened, normally the trigger. Closing from the close button does the same.
- If the consumer closes a controlled drawer from outside (for example a toolbar toggle), focus is left where the user put it.
- Slide-in is a short fade plus 16 px move (`--ds-drawer-shift`); it is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion` and mirrors in right-to-left layouts (`:dir(rtl)`). Borders and padding use logical properties.
- The width is capped by its container (`max-inline-size: 100%`), so on narrow containers it fills the width instead of overflowing.

#### Content rules

- Title: the purpose in sentence case ("Filters", "Order details").
- Footer buttons are verb plus object ("Apply filters", "Clear filters"). Use one primary action.

#### Examples

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<div style={{ display: 'flex' }}>
  <main>
    <Button onPress={() => setOpen(true)}>Open filters</Button>
  </main>
  <Drawer
    title="Filters"
    isOpen={open}
    onOpenChange={setOpen}
    footer={({ close }) => (
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={close}>
        Apply filters
      </Button>
    )}
  >
    <Input label="Customer" />
  </Drawer>
</div>;
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Dialog: A short confirmation or form: `Dialog`.
- Instead, see Popover: A few controls anchored to a button: `Popover`.
- Instead, see Sidebar: Top-level navigation: `Sidebar`.
- Renders: IconButton

### DueIndicator

> A due date with a status in words: "Mar 9  Overdue by 3 days", "Due today", "Due in 5 days",
"Paid". A dot and the text color follow the tone (`danger` overdue, `warning` within a week,
`neutral` later, `success` paid), but the status is always text, never color alone.

The urgency comes from `dueStatus`, the wording from messages and `Intl` (`formatRelativeDays`),
the date from `formatDate`. Day arithmetic is calendar-based, so daylight-saving changes never
shift the count.

A due date with a status in words and a tone dot: "Mar 9 Overdue by 3 days", "Due today", "Due in 5 days", "Paid". Color reinforces the status; the text always states it.

- Handoff source: `components/erp/DueIndicator.jsx` (TODO `CMP-PAT-07`).

- Import: `import { DueIndicator } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/DueIndicator/DueIndicator.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/DueIndicator`): Default, Overdue, DueToday, DueTomorrow, Later, Paid, WithoutDate, LongDate, AcrossDaylightSaving, AllTones, Portuguese, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | `string` | yes |  | The due date as `YYYY-MM-DD` (`ISODate`). Invalid values throw in development. |
| `today` | `string` |  |  | The current day as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to the user's local day at render time. Pass it to make output deterministic (tests, stories, server rendering with a known day). |
| `paid` | `boolean` |  | `false` | The item is settled: shows "Paid" in the success tone, whatever the date. |
| `showDate` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Shows the formatted date before the status. Default `true`. |
| `dateStyle` | `'short' \| 'medium' \| 'long' \| 'full' \| 'monthDay' \| 'monthYear'` |  | `'monthDay'` | Format of the date (`formatDate` styles). Default `monthDay` ("Mar 9"). |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ overdue: (days: number) => string; due: (relative: string) => string; paid: string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ DueIndicator: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `overdue(days: number)` | `Overdue by 2 days` | Status of a date in the past. `days` is a positive whole number. |
| `due(relative: string)` | `Due {relative}` | Status of a date today or later. `relative` is the locale's relative time from `formatRelativeDays` ("today", "tomorrow", "in 3 days"). |
| `paid` | `Paid` | Status of a settled item: the due date no longer matters. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-danger`, `--ds-due-indicator-dot-size`, `--ds-due-indicator-gap`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- A deadline in a list row, a card or a detail header (invoice due, task due, renewal).
- When urgency should be readable at a glance without relying on color.

#### When not to use

- A timestamp of something that already happened: format it with `formatDate` / `formatRelativeDays`.
- A workflow status that is not date-driven: use `Badge`.

#### Anatomy

```
span[data-tone=danger|warning|neutral|success]
  span.dot          (aria-hidden)
  time[datetime]    formatDate(date, locale, dateStyle)     (showDate)
  span.status       "Overdue by 3 days" | "Due today" | "Due in 5 days" | "Paid"
```

#### Accessibility

- The status is text (`Overdue by 3 days`), so color is never the only signal; the dot is `aria-hidden`.
- The date is a `<time datetime>` element.
- Contrast: the status uses `--ds-danger`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-success` or `--ds-text-2` on the page background, all above 4.5:1.
- Forced colors: the dot and the text fall back to `CanvasText`.

#### Content rules

- "Overdue by 3 days", "Due today", "Due tomorrow", "Due in 5 days", "Paid". Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
- Dates and relative wording come from `Intl` for the active locale; never build them by hand.

#### Examples

```tsx
<DueIndicator date={invoice.dueISO} paid={invoice.paid} />

// Deterministic output
<DueIndicator date="2026-03-14" today="2026-03-10" dateStyle="long" />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Badge: A workflow status that is not date-driven: use `Badge`.

### EmptyState

> Tells the user that there is nothing to show, why, and what to do next. The copy follows
"what happened + what to do".

A typographic placeholder for a list, table or panel that has nothing to show. It says what happened and what the user can do about it.

- Import: `import { EmptyState } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/EmptyState/EmptyState.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/EmptyState`): Default, WithActions, Compact, WithoutBorder, WithIcon, TitleOnly, LongText, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | What happened, in one short sentence: "No orders found". Rendered as a heading (see `headingLevel`). |
| `headingLevel` | `'1' \| '2' \| '3' \| '4' \| '5' \| '6'` |  | `'2'` | Heading level of the title (`h1` to `h6`). Pick the level that fits the page outline. Default `2`. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | What the user can do about it: "Try another filter or search term." |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Optional icon above the title. Decorative: it is hidden from assistive technology. No illustrations. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  |  | The primary action, usually a `Button`. Rendered after the secondary action. |
| `secondaryAction` | `ReactNode` |  |  | A second, lower-emphasis action. |
| `compact` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Less padding and a smaller title, for use inside a card, a panel or a table. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Dashed border. Set to `false` when the empty state already sits inside a bordered container. Default `true`. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-empty-state-compact-padding-block`, `--ds-empty-state-compact-padding-inline`, `--ds-empty-state-description-max-w`, `--ds-empty-state-padding-block`, `--ds-empty-state-padding-inline`, `--ds-fs-heading`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-heading`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- A list, table or search has no results.
- A feature has no data yet and the user can create some.

#### When not to use

- While data is loading: use `Skeleton`.
- When loading failed: use `Alert` with a retry action.
- For a short inline note inside a field: use the field's description.

#### Anatomy

```
div.root (dashed border, centered)
  span[aria-hidden]  icon (optional)
  h{headingLevel}    title
  p                  description (optional)
  div                secondaryAction, action
```

#### Copy: what happened + what to do

Title: say what is missing, in sentence case, without apologies or exclamation marks. Description: tell the user the next step, in one sentence.

| Situation        | Title             | Description                                              | Action        |
| ---------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Filtered to zero | No orders found   | Try another filter or search term.                       | Clear filters |
| First use        | No orders yet     | Orders created here or in the store appear in this list. | Create order  |
| Cleared inbox    | Nothing to review | New approvals appear here as they arrive.                | (none)        |

Avoid "Oops", "Sorry", blame ("You have no orders") and filler ("There is nothing to show here at the moment").

#### Accessibility

- The title is a real heading: choose `headingLevel` so the outline stays sequential. The heading lets screen reader users find the empty region by navigating headings.
- The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the text carries the meaning.
- The component does not announce itself. If the empty state replaces content after a user action (for example a search), announce the result count in your own live region.
- Actions are ordinary buttons or links with their own names; order in the DOM is secondary then primary, matching the visual order.

#### Examples

```tsx
<EmptyState
  title="No orders found"
  description="Try another filter or search term."
  action={<Button>Clear filters</Button>}
/>

<EmptyState compact bordered={false} headingLevel={3} title="No comments" />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Skeleton: While data is loading: use `Skeleton`.
- Instead, see Alert: When loading failed: use `Alert` with a retry action.
- Used by: ActionList, DataTable

### FieldError

> Error text of a field. Renders only while the field is invalid and the error is *displayed*:
with the default `validationBehavior="native"` that is after a submit attempt (see Field.md).
The message sits in a `role="alert"` element so it is announced when it appears; on submit focus also
moves to the first invalid field, which reads it again through `aria-describedby`.

Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

- Import: `import { FieldError } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Field/Field.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Field`): Anatomy, ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt, RealtimeValidation

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  | The message. A function receives the validation result and decides everything. A static message replaces only the browser's own constraint text; an error the app supplied (a `validate` rule, or `validationErrors` on a `Form`) is shown instead of it. Without children, the validation errors are shown (the browser's message for native constraints). |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### Exports

| Export                                 | What it is                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Label`                                | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker.                                                         |
| `Description`                          | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`.                                                     |
| `FieldError`                           | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. |
| `FieldMessages`                        | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box.                                                                                  |
| `RequiredMark`                         | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`.                                                                                                       |
| `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel`      | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel<P>` helps type stories.                                       |
| `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result).                                                                               |

#### Anatomy and spacing

```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

#### One state model (ARCH-009)

| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

#### Required marker

`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

#### Validation behavior: native (default), and why

React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language. A static `errorMessage` replaces only that browser text: a message the app supplied (a `validate` rule or `validationErrors` on a `Form`) is shown instead (GAP-009).
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

#### Accessibility

- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

### FieldMessages

> Description followed by the error: the footer every field renders under its control.

Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

- Import: `import { FieldMessages } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Field/Field.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Field`): Anatomy, ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt, RealtimeValidation

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |  |
| `errorMessage` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`

### FieldSet

> Groups related fields under a caption: a real `fieldset` with a `legend`, an optional
description, and disabled propagation. Use it for a set of fields that answer one question
(an address, notification channels), not for every section of a form.

A group of related fields under a caption: a real `fieldset` with a `legend`, an optional description and disabled propagation.

- Import: `import { FieldSet } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/FieldSet/FieldSet.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/FieldSet`): Default, WithDescription, Disabled, WithRadioGroup, LongText, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `legend` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Caption of the group, required. It is the `legend`: screen readers announce it before each field in the group ("Billing address, Street"). Write it in sentence case; CSS makes it a mono caption. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Optional help for the whole group, linked to the fieldset with `aria-describedby`. |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Disables every native control inside (inputs, selects, textareas, buttons), the way `<fieldset disabled>` does: they cannot be focused or submitted and dim together. Controls that are not native elements (menus, custom widgets) are not affected: disable those individually. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-field-set-gap`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-tracking-caption`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- A set of fields that answer one question: an address, a date range, notification channels.
- A group that should be disabled together.

#### When not to use

- For every section of a form: a heading is enough to organize a long form.
- For a single `RadioGroup` or `CheckboxGroup`: they already render a labelled group.

#### Anatomy

```
fieldset
  legend        mono caption, uppercase by CSS
  p             description (optional)
  div           the fields, stacked with --ds-field-set-gap
```

#### Accessibility

- A `fieldset` + `legend` is announced as a named group; screen readers read the legend before each field ("Billing address, Street").
- `isDisabled` uses the native attribute, so inputs, selects, textareas and buttons inside cannot be focused or submitted, and are skipped by constraint validation. Controls that are not native elements (menus, custom widgets) are **not** affected: disable those yourself.
- The legend uses `--ds-text-2` (the faint `--ds-text-3` is too low-contrast for a name).

#### Content rules

- Legends are short nouns in sentence case ("Billing address"); CSS uppercases them. Descriptions say what the group is for, not how to fill each field.

#### Examples

```tsx
<FieldSet legend="Billing address" description="Shown on every invoice.">
  <Input label="Street" name="street" />
  <Input label="City" name="city" />
</FieldSet>

<FieldSet legend="Shipping address" isDisabled>…</FieldSet>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see RadioGroup: For a single `RadioGroup` or `CheckboxGroup`: they already render a labelled group.
- Instead, see CheckboxGroup: For a single `RadioGroup` or `CheckboxGroup`: they already render a labelled group.

### FileUpload

> A drop zone with a "Choose files" button and the list of added files (React Aria `DropZone`
and `FileTrigger`). Dragging is a pointer shortcut; the button is the keyboard and click way
in. Files are validated (type, size, count) as they arrive and the errors are shown under the
zone; added, removed and rejected files are announced politely. The component keeps no upload
state: pass `progress` to show a bar per file.

A drop zone with a "Choose files" button and the list of added files. Built on React Aria `DropZone` and `FileTrigger`; progress bars use [Progress](../Progress/Progress.md). The component validates and lists files; it uploads nothing. Task: CMP-INP-03.

- Import: `import { FileUpload } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/FileUpload/FileUpload.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/FileUpload`): Default, WithFiles, Validation, SingleFile, WithProgress, Disabled, LongFileName

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Helper text under the drop zone, for the rules: "PNG, JPG or PDF up to 10 MB". Linked to the zone. |
| `accept` | `readonly string[]` |  |  | Accepted types: MIME types (`image/png`), wildcards (`image/*`) or extensions (`.pdf`). Files of other types are rejected with an error message. Also filters the file dialog. |
| `maxSize` | `number` |  |  | Largest file in bytes. Larger files are rejected with an error message. |
| `maxFiles` | `number` |  |  | Most files in the list. `1` switches to single-file mode: choosing or dropping a file replaces the current one. Default: no limit. |
| `value` | `readonly File[]` |  |  | The files, when controlled. Pair with `onChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `readonly File[]` |  |  | The initial files when uncontrolled. |
| `onChange` | `((files: File[]) => void)` |  |  | Called with the full list after files are added or removed. |
| `onReject` | `((rejections: FileRejection[]) => void)` |  |  | Called with the files that were not added and why (wrong type, too large, too many). |
| `progress` | `ReadonlyMap<File, number>` |  |  | Upload progress per file, 0 to 100, supplied by you (the component uploads nothing and never invents progress). A file with a value under 100 shows a progress bar; 100 shows "Done"; a file without an entry shows only its size. |
| `name` | `string` |  |  | Name for form submission: the selected files are submitted as `File` entries under this name (multiple entries when several files). |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Disables choosing, dropping and removing. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the root. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ dropZone: string; dropLabel: (multiple: boolean) => string; choose: (multiple: boolean) => string; listLabel: string; remove: (name: string) => string; uploading: (name: string) => string; ... 9 more ...; removed: (name: string) => string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the root `<div>`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ FileUpload: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dropZone` | `Drop zone` | Accessible name of the drop target itself (React Aria adds a keyboard stop on it that accepts pasted files). |
| `dropLabel(multiple: boolean)` | `Drop a file here` | Text of the drop target, which names it for assistive technology. |
| `choose(multiple: boolean)` | `Choose a file` | The button that opens the file dialog (the keyboard and click alternative to dragging). |
| `listLabel` | `Added files` | Accessible name of the list of added files. |
| `remove(name: string)` | `Remove {name}` | Accessible name of the remove button of a file. |
| `uploading(name: string)` | `Uploading {name}` | Accessible name of the progress bar of a file that is uploading. |
| `done` | `Done` | Status text of a file whose progress reached 100. |
| `unitB` | `B` | Size units shown after the number. |
| `unitKB` | `KB` |  |
| `unitMB` | `MB` |  |
| `unitGB` | `GB` |  |
| `wrongType(name: string)` | `"{name}" is not an accepted file type.` | Error: the file type is not accepted. |
| `tooLarge(name: string, max: string)` | `"{name}" is larger than {max}.` | Error: the file is larger than the limit (already formatted, e.g. "10 MB"). |
| `tooMany(max: number, skipped: number)` | `Only 2 files can be added. 2 not added.` | Error: files over the count limit were not added. |
| `added(n: number)` | `2 files added` | Live announcement after files were added. |
| `removed(name: string)` | `Removed {name}` | Live announcement after a file was removed. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-accent-soft`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-file-upload-dropzone-padding-block`, `--ds-file-upload-dropzone-padding-inline`, `--ds-file-upload-item-padding-block`, `--ds-file-upload-item-padding-inline`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- Attaching one or several files to a record or form.

#### When not to use

- Image galleries, cropping or previews: a product pattern.
- A hidden uploader inside a button: use `FileTrigger` from React Aria directly.

#### Props (key ones)

| Prop                                         | Notes                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`   | One is required. The root is a `group` named by it.                                                                                                         |
| `description`                                | The rules in words ("PNG, JPG or PDF up to 10 MB"), linked to the zone.                                                                                     |
| `accept`                                     | MIME types, wildcards (`image/*`) or extensions (`.pdf`). Also filters the file dialog.                                                                     |
| `maxSize`                                    | Bytes. Larger files are rejected.                                                                                                                           |
| `maxFiles`                                   | Count. `1` is single-file mode: a new file replaces the current one.                                                                                        |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(files)` | The full `File[]` after every add or remove.                                                                                                                |
| `onReject(rejections)`                       | `{ file, reason: 'type' \| 'size' \| 'count' }[]` for files not added.                                                                                      |
| `progress`                                   | `Map<File, number>` (0 to 100), yours. Under 100 shows a bar, 100 shows "Done", no entry shows only the size.                                               |
| `name`                                       | Submits the files with the form (`FormData.getAll(name)` returns `File`s) through a hidden file input.                                                      |
| `isDisabled`, `className`, `ref`, `messages` | `messages`: `dropZone`, `dropLabel`, `choose`, `listLabel`, `remove`, `uploading`, `done`, `unit*`, `wrongType`, `tooLarge`, `tooMany`, `added`, `removed`. |

#### Behavior

- Errors are listed under the zone and replaced on the next add or removal. Sizes are formatted with `formatNumber` for the locale and unit messages (`1.5 MB`, pt-BR `1,5 MB`; steps of 1024).
- Polite live region (`role="status"`) announces "2 files added" (with the error texts), "Removed name.pdf". Pluralized per locale.
- Each file row: name (truncated), size or "Done · size", and a ghost button "Remove {name}".
- `progress` is never simulated by the component. The handoff's random progress exists only in the "WithProgress" story, driven by a timer.

#### Accessibility and keyboard

| Key                         | Behavior                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                       | Zone (React Aria's own stop: `Ctrl/Cmd+V` pastes files there), Choose button, Remove buttons |
| `Enter` / `Space` on Choose | Opens the file dialog: the keyboard and click alternative to dragging                        |
| `Enter` / `Space` on Remove | Removes the file                                                                             |

Dragging is only a pointer shortcut; nothing depends on it. While files are dragged over it the zone gets an accent border and soft fill (also an outline in forced colors). The list is a `ul` named "Added files".

#### Content rules

`description` states the limits in one sentence. Error texts name the file and the limit and are produced from messages ("\"big.pdf\" is larger than 1 MB.").

#### Example

```tsx
<FileUpload
  label="Attachments"
  description="PDF up to 10 MB."
  accept={['.pdf']}
  maxSize={10 * 1024 * 1024}
  name="attachments"
  value={files}
  onChange={setFiles}
  progress={progress}
/>
```

#### Manual verification

Dropping files is automated: `FileUpload.test.tsx` performs a native drag of real files through the Chrome DevTools Protocol (`commands.dropFiles`, defined in `tests/browser-commands`), because React Aria rejects synthetic `DragEvent`s. Pasting is not automatable, so check it by hand before a release that touches this component (TEST-017):

1. Copy a file in the operating system file manager (Explorer, Finder), or copy an image.
2. Tab to the drop zone (the first stop, named "Drop zone") so it has focus.
3. Press `Ctrl+V` (`Cmd+V` on macOS). The file should be added to the list and announced ("1 file added.").
4. Repeat with Chrome, Firefox and Safari. Record any browser where the file is not added.

Why it cannot be automated: the paste handler of React Aria reads each item through `webkitGetAsEntry()`, which returns `null` for a synthetic `DataTransfer` and for an image written to the clipboard by a script (verified in Chromium: `kind: file`, `type: image/png`, entry `null`), so the item is skipped. Only a file copied by the operating system can be tested, and no browser API can put one on the clipboard.

#### Related components

- Renders: Button, Description, IconButton, Progress, VisuallyHidden

### Form

> A form built on React Aria `Form`: native validation by default, server errors through
`validationErrors`, a vertical rhythm of `--ds-form-gap` between its children, and an
optional error summary. Fields inside inherit the form's `validationBehavior`.

Put exactly one primary action in it, at the end ("Save changes"), and keep submit enabled:
a disabled submit gives no way to learn what is wrong.

A form built on React Aria `Form`: native validation by default, server errors, a consistent vertical rhythm and an optional error summary.

- Import: `import { Form } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Form/Form.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Form`): Default, WithErrorSummary, ServerErrors, ServerRoundTrip, WithFieldSets, AriaValidation, LongText, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `validationBehavior` | `'native' \| 'aria'` |  | `'native'` | Native validation (default) uses the browser's constraint validation: a failed submit focuses the first invalid field. `aria` marks fields invalid with ARIA only and never blocks the submit; use it when the server is the only validator. |
| `validationErrors` | `ValidationErrors` |  |  | Errors from the server, keyed by the field `name`. The matching fields become invalid and show the message; the first one takes focus (or the summary does, with `errorSummary`). Clear them (pass `undefined`) when the user edits the field or submits again. |
| `errorSummary` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Shows a `FormErrorSummary` at the top of the form. After a failed submit it takes focus and lists the invalid fields as links. Default `false`. To place the summary elsewhere, leave this off and render `FormErrorSummary` inside the form yourself. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  | The fields and actions of the form. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ summaryTitle: (count: number) => string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLFormElement>` |  |  | Ref to the `<form>` element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `FormProps` (@react-types/shared): `action`, `autoCapitalize`, `autoComplete`, `encType`, `method`, `onInvalid`, `onReset`, `onSubmit`, `role`, `target`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Form: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `summaryTitle(count: number)` | `Fix 2 fields before saving` | Title of the error summary shown after a failed submit. `count` is the number of invalid fields. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-danger`, `--ds-danger-line`, `--ds-danger-soft`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-form-gap`, `--ds-form-summary-gap`, `--ds-form-summary-padding`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-space-5`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- Any set of fields submitted together: create or edit a record, settings, sign-in.
- When you want a failed submit to move focus to the first problem and to list all problems.

#### When not to use

- A single search box or an auto-saving inline edit: use the field alone.
- A filter bar that updates as you type: no submit, no form.

#### Anatomy

```
form (flex column, gap --ds-form-gap)
  FormErrorSummary   (errorSummary prop, or placed by hand)
  children           fields, FieldSets, actions
```

#### Validation flow

1. The user presses the submit button. With native validation the browser blocks an invalid submit and fires `invalid` on each invalid field.
2. React Aria displays the errors (`FieldError`) and focuses the **first invalid field**, whose error is read through `aria-describedby`.
3. With `errorSummary`, focus goes to the **summary** instead: a `role="alert"` box, "Fix 2 fields before saving", listing each invalid field as a link that focuses it.
4. Fixing a field (on blur, when React Aria commits the edit) updates the summary; it disappears when nothing is left.
5. Server errors: set `validationErrors` after the request; the matching fields show their message and the summary (if on) lists them and takes focus. Clear them on the next submit or edit.

Keep the submit button enabled: a disabled submit gives no way to learn what is wrong.

#### Accessibility

- The summary is `role="alert"` with `tabindex="-1"`, so it is announced and can take focus programmatically. The links use the field label (the required marker is excluded) and the field's error text.
- Radio and checkbox groups count once, under the group's label.
- Give the form a name (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`) when it should be a landmark.

#### Content rules

- The summary title is "Fix {n} fields before saving" (pluralized; "Fix 1 field before saving"). `pt-BR` has "Corrija {n} campos antes de salvar".
- Field messages say how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). A static `errorMessage` text replaces only the browser's own constraint text ("Please fill out this field"); a server error from `validationErrors` (or a `validate` message) is shown instead of it. Use the function form when you need full control: `errorMessage={(v) => v.validationDetails.valueMissing ? 'Enter a name.' : v.validationErrors.join(' ')}`.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Form aria-label="Profile" errorSummary onSubmit={save} validationErrors={errors}>
  <Input label="Full name" name="name" isRequired />
  <FieldSet legend="Contact">
    <Input label="Email" name="email" type="email" isRequired />
  </FieldSet>
  <Button type="submit" variant="primary">
    Save changes
  </Button>
</Form>
```

### FormErrorSummary

> The error summary of a `Form`: after a failed submit (or new server errors) it takes focus,
is announced (`role="alert"`), says how many fields need fixing, and lists them as links that
move focus to the field. It renders nothing while the form is valid. Place it inside a
`Form`, or turn it on with the form's `errorSummary` prop.

A form built on React Aria `Form`: native validation by default, server errors, a consistent vertical rhythm and an optional error summary.

- Import: `import { FormErrorSummary } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Form/Form.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Form`): Default, WithErrorSummary, ServerErrors, ServerRoundTrip, WithFieldSets, AriaValidation, LongText, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the summary. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-danger`, `--ds-danger-line`, `--ds-danger-soft`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-form-gap`, `--ds-form-summary-gap`, `--ds-form-summary-padding`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-space-5`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- Any set of fields submitted together: create or edit a record, settings, sign-in.
- When you want a failed submit to move focus to the first problem and to list all problems.

#### When not to use

- A single search box or an auto-saving inline edit: use the field alone.
- A filter bar that updates as you type: no submit, no form.

#### Anatomy

