### NavItem

> One entry of a navigation list. A real link when it has an `href`, a button when it only has
`onPress`. The active item is marked with `aria-current="page"`, a raised background and a
2px ink bar at the start edge.

One entry of a navigation list: a real link (or a button) with an optional icon and count. Built on React Aria `Link` and `Button`.

- Handoff source: `components/navigation/NavItem.jsx` (TODO `CMP-NAV-03`).

- Import: `import { NavItem } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/NavItem/NavItem.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/NavItem`): Default, Active, AsButton, WithoutIcon, WithCount, CountTones, ZeroCountHidden, Disabled, LongLabel, RouterNavigation, PortugueseCount, RightToLeft, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Label: a noun in sentence case ("Orders"). Truncated with an ellipsis when it does not fit. |
| `href` | `string` |  |  | Destination. With `href` the item is a real link (`<a>`) and navigates through the router set on `DSProvider`. Without it the item is a `<button>` that runs `onPress`. |
| `icon` | `LucideIcon` |  |  | Icon from the curated set, drawn at 18px before the label. Decorative. |
| `isActive` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Marks the item for the page or view being shown: sets `aria-current="page"`, the raised background and the 2px ink bar. Exactly one item of a navigation should be active. |
| `count` | `string \| number` |  |  | A count shown in a pill at the end of the item. `0` shows no pill. Numbers are formatted for the active locale. |
| `countLabel` | `string` |  |  | The text a screen reader hears instead of the bare number, with what is being counted ("3 pending", "12 unread"). Always set it together with `count`; without it a generic "Count: 3" from the message catalog is used. |
| `countTone` | `'neutral' \| 'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | `'neutral'` | Tone of the count pill. Color never carries the meaning alone: `countLabel` does. Default `neutral`. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ count: (value: string) => string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  | Ref to the underlying `<a>` (with `href`) or `<button>` element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`
- From `AriaLinkOptions` (react-aria): `isDisabled`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `HoverEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onHoverChange`, `onHoverEnd`, `onHoverStart`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `LinkDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `download`, `hrefLang`, `ping`, `referrerPolicy`, `rel`, `routerOptions`, `target`
- From `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `PressEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onClick`, `onPress`, `onPressChange`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressStart`, `onPressUp`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ NavItem: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count(value: string)` | `Count: {value}` | Spoken text for a count when the consumer gives no `countLabel`. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-accent-soft`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-danger-soft`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-item-h`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-nav-item-count-padding-inline`, `--ds-nav-item-count-size`, `--ds-nav-item-icon-opacity`, `--ds-nav-item-indicator-width`, `--ds-nav-item-padding-inline`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-success-soft`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-warning-soft`, `--ds-weight-medium`, `--ds-weight-regular`

#### When to use

- Inside the `Sidebar`, or any vertical navigation list.
- To go to a page or view (with `href`), or to run a navigation-like command such as "Log out" (with `onPress`).

#### When not to use

- For actions inside a page: use `Button`.
- For switching panels on a page: use `Tabs`.
- For a link inside text: use `Link`.

#### Anatomy

```
a | button .root           (36px high, --ds-item-h)
  Icon                     (18px, optional, 0.7 opacity when inactive)
  label                    (truncates with an ellipsis)
  count                    (optional pill with tone)
    "3"                    (aria-hidden)
    "3 pending"            (visually hidden text alternative)
```

#### States

| State    | Look                                                                          | Semantics             |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Rest     | transparent, `--ds-text-2`                                                    | link or button        |
| Hover    | raised background (`--ds-surface-raised`), ink text                           | none                  |
| Active   | raised background, ink text, 2px ink bar at the start edge, full-opacity icon | `aria-current="page"` |
| Focus    | accent ring                                                                   |                       |
| Disabled | `--ds-opacity-disabled`                                                       | `aria-disabled`       |

#### Accessibility

- Real `<a href>` (or `<button>`), so opening in a new tab, copying the URL and screen reader link lists work. The handoff used `div role="link"` with no `href`.
- `aria-current="page"` on the active item, on links and on buttons.
- The count pill is not enough on its own: a screen reader hears the label then the text alternative ("Orders 3 pending"). Color (tone) is only reinforcement.
- Keys: `Tab` to focus; `Enter` follows a link; `Enter` and `Space` press a button.
- Contrast: label `--ds-text-2` on `--ds-bg`, ink on the raised surface. The pill text meets 4.5:1 on its soft background.
- Forced colors: the active bar and the pill border use system colors.

#### Content rules

- Labels are nouns in sentence case: "Orders", "Customers". Long labels are truncated.
- `countLabel` states what is counted and its state: "3 pending", "12 unread".

#### Examples

```tsx
<nav aria-label="Main">
  <NavItem
    href="/orders"
    icon={StarIcon}
    isActive
    count={3}
    countLabel="3 pending"
    countTone="warning"
  >
    Orders
  </NavItem>
  <NavItem href="/customers" icon={SearchIcon}>
    Customers
  </NavItem>
  <NavItem onPress={signOut}>Log out</NavItem>
</nav>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Button: For actions inside a page: use `Button`.
- Instead, see Tabs: For switching panels on a page: use `Tabs`.
- Instead, see Link: For a link inside text: use `Link`.
- Renders: Icon, VisuallyHidden
- Used by: Sidebar

### NumberField

> A number field with minus and plus steppers (the handoff `Stepper`), built on React Aria
`NumberField`: a text `<input>` with `aria-roledescription="Number field"` (React Aria
deliberately drops `role="spinbutton"`: VoiceOver cannot focus a spin button with typed
text). You can type a value or step it: `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` by `step`,
`PageUp` / `PageDown` like the arrows (React Aria has no larger step), `Home` / `End` to the
limits (when `minValue` / `maxValue` are set), the mouse wheel while focused, and press and hold on a button repeats.
The typed text is parsed with the locale of `DSProvider` (`1.234,5` in pt-BR) and committed on
blur or `Enter`; values are clamped to the limits and snapped to `step`.

`onChange` receives a number, `NaN` while the field is empty. For money use `CurrencyInput`.

A number input with minus and plus steppers; the successor of the handoff `Stepper`. Built on React Aria `NumberField` (`Group`, `Input`, two `Button`s in the `decrement` / `increment` slots), styled like [Input](../Input/Input.md). Task: CMP-PAT-06.

- Import: `import { NumberField } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/NumberField/NumberField.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/NumberField`): Default, KeyboardContract, TypingClampsToLimits, WithSuffix, FormattedUnit, WithDescription, Required, Invalid, Disabled, ReadOnly, AtLimit, Sizes, Controlled

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Helper text under the control, linked with `aria-describedby`. |
| `errorMessage` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  | Error text, shown while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. See `Input`. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  | Text shown while the field is empty. Never a substitute for the label. |
| `suffix` | `ReactNode` |  |  | A unit shown after the number inside the box ("m", "kg", "pcs"). Visual only: for a spoken unit use `formatOptions={{ style: 'unit', unit: 'meter' }}`, which also formats the number. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | Height of the box and of both stepper buttons: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the field root. |
| `inputClassName` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the `<input>` element. |
| `inputRef` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` |  |  | Ref to the `<input>` element. The `ref` prop points at the field root. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ decrease: string; increase: string; } & { requiredMark: string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance: `decrease`, `increase`, `requiredMark`. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the field root `<div>`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `AriaNumberFieldProps` (react-aria): `decrementAriaLabel`, `incrementAriaLabel`, `isWheelDisabled`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `InputBase` (@react-types/shared): `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`
- From `InputDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `form`, `name`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `NumberFieldProps` (react-stately): `commitBehavior`, `formatOptions`
- From `RACValidation` (react-aria-components): `validationBehavior`
- From `RangeInputBase` (@react-types/shared): `maxValue`, `minValue`, `step`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- From `TextInputDOMEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBeforeInput`, `onCompositionEnd`, `onCompositionStart`, `onCompositionUpdate`, `onCopy`, `onCut`, `onInput`, `onPaste`, `onSelect`
- From `Validation` (@react-types/shared): `isInvalid`, `isRequired`, `validate`
- From `ValueBase` (@react-types/shared): `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `value`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ NumberField: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `decrease` | `Decrease` | Accessible name of the "minus" stepper button. |
| `increase` | `Increase` | Accessible name of the "plus" stepper button. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-field-control-padding-inline`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-number-field-value-min-width`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-text-3`

#### When to use

- A bounded or unbounded count or measure that users type or nudge: quantity, length, number of copies.

#### When not to use

- Money: `CurrencyInput` (integer minor units, currency formatting).
- An approximate value on a range: `Slider`.
- Digits that are an identifier (postal code, phone): `Input` with `mono`.

#### Anatomy

`[ - ] [ value + suffix ] [ + ]`: three boxes of the same height (`sm` 32 / `md` 40 / `lg` 48). The middle box is the `Input` look (`--ds-line-control` border, focus ring, mono, centered); the steppers are `IconButton`s.

#### Props (key ones)

| Prop                                                          | Notes                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`                    | One is required.                                                                                     |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`                  | RAC naming. `onChange` receives a `number`, `NaN` while the field is empty.                          |
| `minValue`, `maxValue`, `step`                                | Typed and stepped values are clamped and snapped to `step`.                                          |
| `formatOptions`                                               | `Intl.NumberFormat` options (`{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilogram' }`, `{ maximumFractionDigits: 2 }`). |
| `suffix`                                                      | A visual unit after the number ("m", "pcs"). For a spoken unit use `formatOptions`.                  |
| `size`                                                        | `sm` / `md` (default) / `lg`; the steppers follow.                                                   |
| `description`, `errorMessage`                                 | As in `Input`.                                                                                       |
| `name`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly` | Standard. `name` submits the raw number (`1234.5`), not the formatted text.                          |
| `messages`                                                    | `decrease`, `increase`, `requiredMark`.                                                              |

#### Accessibility and keyboard

| Key                       | Behavior                                                                  |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown`   | Step up / down                                                            |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown`     | Same as the arrows (React Aria has no larger step)                        |
| `Home` / `End`            | `minValue` / `maxValue` (only when set)                                   |
| Typing                    | Parsed with the locale (`1.234,5` in pt-BR), committed on `Enter` or blur |
| Press and hold a stepper  | Repeats (React Aria)                                                      |
| Mouse wheel while focused | Steps                                                                     |

The input is a text input with `aria-roledescription="Number field"`: React Aria deliberately does not use `role="spinbutton"` because VoiceOver cannot focus a spin button that accepts typed text. The stepper buttons are named "Decrease" / "Increase" from messages and, through `aria-labelledby`, followed by the field label ("Increase Quantity"); they are out of the tab order (the input handles the keys) and disabled at the limits. The value is not a live region (RAC announces changes).

#### Content rules

Label with the noun ("Quantity"). Put the unit in `suffix` or `formatOptions`, not in the label. Error text says how to fix: "Enter a quantity between 0 and 10."

#### Example

```tsx
<NumberField label="Quantity" name="quantity" defaultValue={1} minValue={1} maxValue={99} />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see CurrencyInput: Money: `CurrencyInput` (integer minor units, currency formatting).
- Instead, see Slider: An approximate value on a range: `Slider`.
- Instead, see Input: Digits that are an identifier (postal code, phone): `Input` with `mono`.
- Renders: FieldMessages, IconButton, Label

### Pagination

> Previous and next buttons, numbered page buttons with ellipses, and a text that says where
you are ("11–20 of 42", or "Page 2 of 5" when only the page count is known).

The text is a polite live region, so a screen reader announces the new range when the page
changes. The current page button has `aria-current="page"`. The buttons that cannot be used
(previous on page 1) are disabled; when pressing a button disables it, focus moves to the
current page button so it is never lost.

Previous and next buttons, numbered page buttons with ellipses and a text that says where you are ("11–20 of 42"). The list logic is a tested pure function, `getPageItems`.

- Handoff source: `components/data/Pagination.jsx` (TODO `CMP-DAT-02`).

- Import: `import { Pagination } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Pagination/Pagination.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Pagination`): Default, WithRange, MiddlePage, LastPage, FewPages, SinglePage, NoResults, KeyboardNavigation, FocusStaysAfterLastPage, Controlled, Portuguese, NarrowContainer, RightToLeft, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | `number` |  |  | Current page, 1-based (controlled). |
| `defaultPage` | `number` |  | `1` | Page shown first (uncontrolled). Default `1`. |
| `onChange` | `(page: number) => void` |  |  | Called with the new page when the user picks one. |
| `pageCount` | `number` |  |  | Number of pages. Optional when `total` and `pageSize` are given (then it is derived from them). Default `1`. |
| `total` | `number` |  |  | Total number of items. With `pageSize` it enables the "1–10 of 42" range text. |
| `pageSize` | `number` |  |  | Items per page. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ navLabel: string; previous: string; next: string; page: (page: string) => string; range: (from: string, to: string, total: string) => string; empty: string; pageOf: (page: string, count: string) => string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Pagination: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `navLabel` | `Pagination` | Accessible name of the pagination navigation landmark. |
| `previous` | `Previous page` |  |
| `next` | `Next page` |  |
| `page(page: string)` | `Page {page}` | Accessible name of a page button; the button shows only the number. |
| `range(from: string, to: string, total: string)` | `{from}–{to} of {total}` | Visible and announced range of items. All arguments are already formatted for the locale. |
| `empty` | `No results` | Visible and announced text when `total` is 0. |
| `pageOf(page: string, count: string)` | `Page {page} of {count}` | Visible and announced text when only the page count is known. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-5`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`

#### When to use

- Below a table or list that is split into pages on the server or the client.

#### When not to use

- For endless feeds: use a "Load more" `Button`.
- For a handful of items that fit on one screen.
- For moving through steps: use a stepper.

#### Anatomy

```
div.root
  span[role=status, aria-live=polite]   "11–20 of 42"  or  "Page 2 of 5"
  nav[aria-label="Pagination"]
    ul
      li  IconButton  Previous page
      li  button      1    (aria-label "Page 1", aria-current="page" on the current one)
      li  …                (aria-hidden)
      li  IconButton  Next page
```

#### Page list algorithm

Up to 7 pages every page is shown. Beyond that: the first page, the last page, the current page and its two neighbours; each gap becomes an ellipsis. A gap that would hide exactly one page shows that page instead (the handoff showed an ellipsis for it, which is wider than the page it hides). The page list never exceeds 7 slots.

#### Accessibility

- `nav` named "Pagination" (from the catalog). Page buttons have `aria-label="Page 3"` and show only the number; the current one has `aria-current="page"`.
- The summary is a polite live region: when the page changes, a screen reader announces the new range ("11–20 of 42"). It is not announced on first render.
- Previous and next are disabled at the ends. When pressing one disables it, focus moves to the current page button, so focus is never lost to the page body.
- Ellipses are `aria-hidden` list items. In right-to-left locales the previous and next chevrons swap direction.
- Targets are 32px; page numbers are mono with tabular figures. Numbers are formatted for the locale ("1.248" in pt-BR).
- Keys: `Tab` to move; `Enter` and `Space` press.

#### Content rules

- Do not repeat the total elsewhere. Keep the labels from the catalog unless your product uses another word for the items ("rows", "orders").

#### Examples

```tsx
<Pagination total={42} pageSize={10} page={page} onChange={setPage} />

<Pagination pageCount={8} defaultPage={3} />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Button: For endless feeds: use a "Load more" `Button`.
- Renders: IconButton
- Used by: DataTable

### Popover

> A floating surface for interactive content (filters, a small form, a color picker), built on
React Aria `DialogTrigger`, `Popover` and `Dialog`.

It is not for lists of commands (use `Menu`), for choosing one option (use `Select`) or for
plain hints (use `Tooltip`). `Escape` and an outside press close it and focus returns to the
trigger; when the content has focusable elements, `Tab` stays inside until it is closed.

A floating surface that opens from a trigger and holds interactive content. Built on React Aria `DialogTrigger`, `Popover` and `Dialog`.

- Handoff source: `components/navigation/Popover` (CMP-NAV-04).

- Import: `import { Popover } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Popover/Popover.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Popover`): Default, Open, WithArrow, AboveTrigger, AlignedToEnd, KeyboardOpenAndRestoreFocus, CloseFromInside

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` | yes |  | The element that opens the popover: a `Button`, `IconButton` or any React Aria pressable. It receives `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="dialog"`. |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | Accessible name of the popover (for example "Filters"). The popover is a `dialog`, so it needs a name; a visible heading inside it can be linked with `aria-labelledby` instead. |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| ((options: { close: () => void; }) => ReactNode)` | yes |  | Interactive content. A function receives `close` to dismiss the popover from inside. |
| `placement` | `'bottom' \| 'bottom left' \| 'bottom right' \| 'bottom start' \| 'bottom end' \| 'top' \| 'top left' \| 'top right' \| 'top start' \| 'top end' \| 'left' \| 'left top' \| 'left bottom' \| 'start' \| 'start top' \| 'start bottom' \| 'right' \| 'right top' \| 'right bottom' \| 'end' \| 'end top' \| 'end bottom'` |  | `'bottom start'` | Side and alignment relative to the trigger. Default `bottom start`. Flips on collision. |
| `showArrow` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Draws an arrow that points at the trigger. |
| `isNonModal` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Keeps the page outside the popover available to assistive technology and does not hide it. Leave it off unless the popover is a long-lived tool the user returns to; React Aria's guidance is that most popovers should stay modal for screen readers. |
| `isOpen` | `boolean` |  |  | Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  |  | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(isOpen: boolean) => void` |  |  | Called when the popover opens or closes. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the popover surface. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  | Ref to the popover surface. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-popover-arrow-size`, `--ds-popover-min-width`, `--ds-popover-padding`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`

#### When to use

- Filters, a small form, a date range, a color picker: content the user operates and then dismisses.

#### When not to use

- A list of commands: use `Menu`.
- Choosing one option from a list: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
- A hint on hover or focus: use `Tooltip`.
- A decision that blocks the task: use `Dialog`.

#### Anatomy

```
DialogTrigger
  trigger            Button | IconButton            aria-haspopup=dialog, aria-expanded, aria-controls
  Popover            raised surface, strong line, radius lg, overlay shadow, z popover
    OverlayArrow     optional
    Dialog           role=dialog, aria-label = label
      children
```

#### Accessibility

- The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The handoff used a `span` with a click handler and no ARIA.
- The surface is a `dialog` named by `label`. A menu is **not** a dialog: use `Menu` for commands.
- Keys: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens it and moves focus inside; `Tab` moves through the content; `Esc` closes it and focus returns to the trigger.
- Outside press closes it. React Aria hides the rest of the page from assistive technology while it is open (`isNonModal` turns that off; React Aria recommends it only for long-lived tool popovers).
- Focus is restored to the trigger on close.
- Placement is collision-aware. Forced colors: the arrow uses `CanvasText`/`Canvas`.
- Layer: `--ds-z-popover`. A popover opened from inside a `Dialog` or `Sheet` sits **below** them in the current z-index scale (see the Dialog doc, "Layers").

#### Content rules

- `label` is a noun phrase: "Filters", "Date range".
- Put the confirming action inside the content ("Apply filters"); verb plus object.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Popover trigger={<Button>Filters</Button>} label="Filters" placement="bottom end">
  {({ close }) => (
    <>
      <Input label="Customer" />
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={close}>
        Apply filters
      </Button>
    </>
  )}
</Popover>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Menu: A list of commands: use `Menu`.
- Instead, see Select: Choosing one option from a list: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
- Instead, see Combobox: Choosing one option from a list: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
- Instead, see Tooltip: A hint on hover or focus: use `Tooltip`.
- Instead, see Dialog: A decision that blocks the task: use `Dialog`.

### Progress

> A thin bar for a task that makes progress: determinate with a `value`, or indeterminate
when the amount is unknown. Built on React Aria `ProgressBar` (`role="progressbar"`).
For a measured quantity that is not a task (disk used, quota) use `Meter`.

A thin bar (4 px) with a label and a value in mono type. `Progress` shows the progress of a task, determinate or indeterminate (React Aria `ProgressBar`, `role="progressbar"`). `Meter` shows a quantity within a range (React Aria `Meter`, `role="meter"`) and shares the same look.

- Import: `import { Progress } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Progress/Progress.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Progress`): Default, WithoutLabel, ShowValue, Empty, Complete, Warning, Danger, Indeterminate, AllTones, AsMeter, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label, wired to the bar with `aria-labelledby`. Required unless you set `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`: a bar without a name is an accessibility bug (React Aria warns in development). |
| `meta` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Text on the right of the label, in mono type: "6.2 / 10 GB". It is visual only. If it says more than the percentage, also pass `valueLabel` so screen readers hear the same thing. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` |  |  | Shows the formatted percentage (`62%`, from `Intl` with the active locale) as `meta` when `meta` is not given. |
| `tone` | `'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | `'accent'` | Color of the fill. Color is never the only signal: pair it with a label or `meta`. Default `accent`. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  |  |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `ProgressBarBaseProps` (react-aria): `formatOptions`, `maxValue`, `minValue`, `value`, `valueLabel`
- From `ProgressBarProps` (react-aria): `isIndeterminate`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `tone`: `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration-progress`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-progress-height`, `--ds-progress-indeterminate-duration`, `--ds-progress-indeterminate-width`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-warning`

#### When to use

- `Progress`: an upload, an import, a multi-step job. Use indeterminate when the amount is unknown.
- `Meter`: disk used, quota consumed, a score. The value is a measurement, not a task that will finish.

#### When not to use

- Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.
- Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.

#### Anatomy

```
div[role=progressbar|meter]
  div.header      Label (left) · meta (right, mono)
  div.track       4px, pill
    div.fill      width = percentage (or a sweeping segment when indeterminate)
```

#### Accessibility

- The bar is named by the visible label (`aria-labelledby`) or `aria-label`; React Aria warns in development when a bar has neither.
- `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are set, and `aria-valuetext` is the percentage formatted with `Intl` for the active locale ("62%", "62,5%" in pt-BR). If you show "6.2 / 10 GB", set `valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB"` so screen readers hear the same thing.
- An indeterminate bar has no `aria-valuenow`, so assistive technology reports it as busy without a number.
- Progress does not announce changes by itself. For long tasks, announce milestones and completion in a live region (for example with a `Toast`).
- Color is not the only signal: the label and the value text carry the meaning. The fill is 4 px high but the track and fill are a graphic that keeps at least 3:1 against the surface; the track is a neutral surface step.
- **Reduced motion:** the width change has no transition and the indeterminate sweep becomes a static segment centered in the track. **Forced colors:** the track gets a border and the fill uses the text color.

#### Content rules

- Labels are nouns or short phrases in sentence case ("Storage", "Importing orders").
- Put units and ratios in `meta`, in the formatted form of the active locale.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Progress value={62} label="Storage" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB" />
<Progress isIndeterminate label="Importing orders" />
<Meter value={82} tone="warning" label="Quota" showValue />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Spinner: Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.
- Instead, see Skeleton: Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.
- Used by: FileUpload

### ProportionBar

> A single bar split into the parts of a whole (payment methods, composition). It is an image
with a text summary ("Payment methods: Pix 47%, Cash 16%…"), and an optional legend with the
percentage and the value of each part.

Neutral by default: signal colors are not used for categories. Parts are separated by a
gap, and beyond four parts the ramp repeats with a hatch so they never look alike.

One bar split into the parts of a whole (payment methods, composition), with a text summary for assistive technology and an optional legend with the percentage and value of each part.

- Import: `import { ProportionBar } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/ProportionBar/ProportionBar.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/ProportionBar`): Default, WithLegend, EightParts, ExplicitColors, ZeroPart, AllZero, OneDecimalPercent, LongLabels, PortugueseBrazil

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `segments` | `readonly ProportionSegment[]` | yes |  | The parts of the whole, in display order. Without `color` they use a neutral ramp of four steps (`text`, `text-2`, `text-3`, `line-control`); from the fifth part on, the ramp repeats with a hatch pattern so no two parts look the same (up to eight; group the tail into "Other" or give explicit colors beyond that). The bar never sorts. |
| `label` | `string` |  |  | Name of the whole ("Payment methods"). It starts the summary read for the bar. |
| `legend` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Shows a list under the bar with swatch, label, percentage and formatted value for each part. |
| `format` | `(value: number) => ReactNode` |  |  | Formats each value in the legend. Default: `formatNumber` with the active locale. Use `formatCurrency` for money. |
| `percentDigits` | `number` |  | `0` | Decimals of the percentages in the summary and the legend. Default `0`. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ segment: (label: string, percent: string) => string; summary: (items: string, label?: string) => string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ ProportionBar: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `segment(label: string, percent: string)` | `{label} {percent}` | One segment in the summary read for the bar: "Cash 16%". Both arguments are already formatted. |
| `summary(items: string, label?: string)` | `{label?}: {items}` | The whole summary. `items` is the list of segments joined for the locale ("Cash 16%, Card 11% and Pix 73%"); `label` names the bar, if given. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-bg`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-line-subtle`, `--ds-proportion-bar-color`, `--ds-proportion-bar-hatch-size`, `--ds-proportion-bar-height`, `--ds-proportion-bar-percent-col-w`, `--ds-proportion-bar-segment-gap`, `--ds-proportion-bar-share`, `--ds-proportion-bar-swatch-size`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- Showing how a total divides into a few parts (2 to 8) at a glance.
- Next to or inside a `StatCard`.

#### When not to use

- Progress of a task: use `Progress`. A quantity within a range: use `Meter`.
- Comparing separate values or many categories: use `Chart` or `RankList`.
- Exact figures the user must read: show the legend (or a table).

#### Anatomy

```
div.root
  div[role=img][aria-label="Payment methods: Pix 53%, Cash 18%…"]   the track, 10px, pill radius
    div  one segment per non-zero part (flex share = its share of the whole, 2px gap)
  ul (legend, optional)
    li  swatch (aria-hidden) · label · percentage · value
```

#### Props (key ones)

| Prop            | Type                         | Default | Notes                                                                  |
| --------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `segments`      | `{ label, value, color? }[]` | -       | Display order; never sorted. Negative and non-finite values count as 0 |
| `label`         | `string`                     |         | Name of the whole; starts the summary                                  |
| `legend`        | `boolean`                    | `false` | List with swatch, label, percentage and formatted value                |
| `format`        | `(value) => ReactNode`       | `Intl`  | Formats legend values. Use `formatCurrency` for money                  |
| `percentDigits` | `number`                     | `0`     | Decimals of the percentages                                            |
| `messages`      | `Partial<messages>`          |         | `segment(label, percent)`, `summary(items, label?)`                    |

#### Distinguishing the parts

Neutral by default: signal colors are not used for categories.

- The ramp has four solid steps: `text`, `text-2`, `text-3`, `line-control`. All reach 3:1 against the track background.
- Neighbours are always separated by a 2px gap.
- From the fifth part on, the ramp **repeats with a diagonal hatch**, so up to eight parts look different. This is the only place a gradient is used, as a pattern, not as decoration.
- Beyond eight parts, group the smallest into "Other" or pass explicit `color`s. In development a warning appears when more than eight parts have no color.
- Even so, the legend and the summary carry the identity of every part; the fill only helps sighted users.

#### Accessibility

- The bar is `role="img"` with an `aria-label` that lists every part with its percentage: "Payment methods: Pix 53%, Cash 18%, Debit 17%, and Credit 11%". The list is joined with `Intl.ListFormat` for the locale; the per-part text comes from messages.
- The legend is a real list. It repeats the summary on purpose: it is the content sighted users read, and it stays available when you need more than the bar.
- Zero parts are listed in the legend (with 0%) but not drawn.
- Forced colors: segments use system colors (`CanvasText`, `GrayText`, `LinkText`, `Highlight`) and the track gets a border.

#### Content rules

- Part labels are short nouns ("Cash", "Pix"); the whole gets a label when the bar is not obvious from context.
- Percentages are rounded; they may not add up to exactly 100%. Use `percentDigits` if that matters.

#### Example

```tsx
<ProportionBar
  label="Payment methods"
  legend
  format={(value) => formatCurrency(value, 'USD', locale)}
  segments={[
    { label: 'Pix', value: 1693000 },
    { label: 'Cash', value: 573400 },
    { label: 'Debit', value: 538800 },
    { label: 'Credit', value: 359600 },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Progress: Progress of a task: use `Progress`. A quantity within a range: use `Meter`.
- Instead, see Meter: Progress of a task: use `Progress`. A quantity within a range: use `Meter`.
- Instead, see Chart: Comparing separate values or many categories: use `Chart` or `RankList`.
- Instead, see RankList: Comparing separate values or many categories: use `Chart` or `RankList`.

### Radio

> One option of a `RadioGroup`. `value` is required and identifies the option.

A labelled set of mutually exclusive options with native radio inputs. Built on React Aria `RadioGroup` + `RadioField` + `RadioButton` (the non-deprecated pair that supports a description per option). Shared field behavior is in [Field](../Field/Field.md).

- Import: `import { Radio } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/RadioGroup/RadioGroup.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/RadioGroup`): Default, WithSelection, Horizontal, WithDescriptions, Required, Invalid, Disabled, DisabledOption, ReadOnly, LongLabels

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Secondary text under the label. Linked with `aria-describedby`, not part of the name. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the option root. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the option root `<div>`. Use `inputRef` for the `<input>`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `PressEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onClick`, `onPress`, `onPressChange`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressStart`, `onPressUp`
- From `RadioFieldProps` (react-aria-components): `inputRef`
- From `RadioProps` (react-aria): `isDisabled`, `value`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-choice-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radio-dot-size`, `--ds-radio-size`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-5`, `--ds-target-min`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-3`

#### When to use

- Choose exactly one of 2 to 5 options that users want to compare.

#### When not to use

- Many options: `Select`.
- Independent choices: `Checkbox`.
- Immediate on/off: `Switch`.

#### Props (key ones)

`RadioGroup`:

| Prop                                                  | Notes                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                                               | Group name. Required: pass `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (type error otherwise; development warning too). |
| `description`, `errorMessage`                         | Linked to the group by `aria-describedby`.                                                                             |
| `orientation`                                         | `vertical` (default) or `horizontal`.                                                                                  |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`          | React Aria naming; `value` is a string.                                                                                |
| `name`                                                | Shared by every radio; the selected value is submitted.                                                                |
| `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly` | Standard states.                                                                                                       |

`Radio`: `value` (required), `label`, `description`, `isDisabled`, `className`, `inputRef`.

#### Look

- 18px circle (`--ds-radio-size`), `--ds-line-control` border at 3:1 or better in every state, accent border and a 9px accent dot when selected. Hover brightens the border.
- The option row is at least 24px tall and the whole row is clickable.
- A disabled group dims once; a single disabled option uses `--ds-opacity-disabled`.

#### Accessibility and keyboard

| Key                        | Behavior                                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                      | One tab stop: lands on the selected radio, or the first one when nothing is selected            |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowRight` | Next radio, selects it, wraps from the last to the first (directions follow the text direction) |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowLeft`    | Previous radio, selects it, wraps                                                               |
| `Space`                    | Selects the focused radio                                                                       |

Roving focus is handled by React Aria, so only one radio is in the tab order (the handoff made every radio tabbable). `role="radiogroup"` is named by the label; the description and error belong to the group; `aria-required` and `aria-invalid` are set.

#### Example

```tsx
<RadioGroup
  label="Region"
  name="region"
  defaultValue="eu"
  description="You cannot change this later."
>
  <Radio value="eu" label="EU: Frankfurt" />
  <Radio value="us" label="US: Virginia" description="Default for new workspaces." />
</RadioGroup>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Select: Many options: `Select`.
- Instead, see Checkbox: Independent choices: `Checkbox`.
- Instead, see Switch: Immediate on/off: `Switch`.
- Renders: Description, FieldMessages, Label

### RadioGroup

> A labelled `role="radiogroup"` of mutually exclusive options with native radio inputs.
The group is one tab stop; arrow keys move and select (roving focus is handled by React Aria).
`value`, `defaultValue` and `onChange(value)` follow React Aria; `name` is shared by every radio.
A group needs a name: pass `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

A labelled set of mutually exclusive options with native radio inputs. Built on React Aria `RadioGroup` + `RadioField` + `RadioButton` (the non-deprecated pair that supports a description per option). Shared field behavior is in [Field](../Field/Field.md).

- Import: `import { RadioGroup } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/RadioGroup/RadioGroup.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/RadioGroup`): Default, WithSelection, Horizontal, WithDescriptions, Required, Invalid, Disabled, DisabledOption, ReadOnly, LongLabels

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The `Radio` elements of the group. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Helper text under the label. Linked with `aria-describedby`. |
| `errorMessage` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  | Error text for the group, shown while it is invalid and the error is displayed (after a submit attempt with the default native validation, or at once with `isInvalid`). |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` |  | `'vertical'` | Layout of the options. Default `vertical`; arrow keys follow the reading direction either way. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the group root. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ requiredMark: string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`). |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the group root `<div>`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `AriaValidationProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-errormessage`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`

- From `ValueBase` (@react-types/shared): `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `value`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-choice-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radio-dot-size`, `--ds-radio-size`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-5`, `--ds-target-min`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-3`

#### When to use

- Choose exactly one of 2 to 5 options that users want to compare.

#### When not to use

- Many options: `Select`.
- Independent choices: `Checkbox`.
- Immediate on/off: `Switch`.

#### Props (key ones)

### RankList

> An ordered list of items with a value, a bar relative to the largest value and an optional
detail. Rows can be plain or buttons.

The list renders the items as given; pass `sort` and `limit` for a "top N". Put it in a
`Card` with `padding="none"`.

An ordered list of items with a value, a bar relative to the largest value and an optional detail. Rows can be plain or buttons. Meant to sit inside a `Card` without body padding.

- Import: `import { RankList } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/RankList/RankList.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/RankList`): Default, GivenOrder, SortedAndLimited, WithoutPositions, WithoutSwatchOrMeta, Actionable, Empty, LongLabels, BarsAlign, PortugueseBrazil

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly RankItem[]` | yes |  | The rows, rendered **in the order given** unless `sort` is set. This differs from the handoff, which always sorted descending and kept only six rows: sorting and truncating silently changes the data, so both are opt-in. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name of the list ("Top products"). Optional: a list inside a titled `Card` is already named by it. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the list. |
| `sort` | `'desc' \| 'asc'` |  |  | Sorts by `value` (`desc` largest first, `asc` smallest first) before `limit` is applied. Ties keep their input order. |
| `limit` | `number` |  |  | Shows only the first `limit` rows (after `sort`). Default: all rows. |
| `format` | `(value: number) => ReactNode` |  |  | Formats each value. Default: `formatNumber` with the active locale; use `formatCurrency` for money. |
| `showPosition` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Shows the position (1, 2, 3...) before each row. The list is ordered either way. Default `true`. |
| `emptyState` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Content when there are no rows. Default: the "No data for this period" message. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ empty: string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ RankList: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `empty` | `No data for this period` | Text shown when there are no items. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-meta`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-rank-list-bar-h`, `--ds-rank-list-padding-block`, `--ds-rank-list-padding-inline`, `--ds-rank-list-position-w`, `--ds-rank-list-share`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-6`, `--ds-surface-row-hover`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- "Top products", "best customers", "colors by sales": a short ranking with comparable values.

#### When not to use

- Several columns, sorting by the user, selection: use `DataTable`.
- Parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.
- A trend over time: use `Chart`.

#### Anatomy

```
div.root
  ol (role=list)
    li > div | button     grid, shared columns for all rows (subgrid)
      position            decorative number (aria-hidden); the ol already numbers the items
      label               optional swatch (aria-hidden) + text, truncated
      value               mono, formatted
      bar                 4px track + fill, relative to the largest value (aria-hidden)
      meta                mono detail, optional
```

#### Props (key ones)

| Prop           | Type                   | Default | Notes                                                                       |
| -------------- | ---------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`        | `RankItem[]`           | -       | `id`, `label`, `value`, `meta`, `swatch`, `onAction`. Rendered **as given** |
| `sort`         | `asc \| desc`          |         | Opt-in sort by value (stable ties)                                          |
| `limit`        | `number`               |         | Opt-in truncation, applied after `sort`                                     |
| `format`       | `(value) => ReactNode` | `Intl`  | Use `formatCurrency` for money                                              |
| `showPosition` | `boolean`              | `true`  | Numbers 1, 2, 3 of the rows shown                                           |
| `emptyState`   | `ReactNode`            |         | Default: "No data for this period" (messages)                               |
| `aria-label`   | `string`               |         | Optional name of the list                                                   |
| `messages`     | `Partial<messages>`    |         | `empty`                                                                     |

#### Accessibility

- A real ordered list (`ol`, explicit `role="list"` so Safari keeps the semantics with `list-style: none`).
- Rows with `onAction` are `<button>`s (React Aria `Button`): Tab, Enter, Space. Their name is the label followed by the value; position, bar and swatch are hidden from assistive technology.
- The bar and swatch are decorative: the value (and `meta`) carry the information as text.
- Bars of all rows share one grid, so their lengths are comparable.
- Text colors: label `text`, meta `text-2` (stays above 4.5:1 on hover); focus is an inset accent outline (system color in forced colors).

#### Content rules

- Labels are names, not sentences. Meta is short and mono: `12 units · 18%`.
- Use this for things (products, colors, customers). Give customers an `onAction` that opens the profile.

#### Example

```tsx
<Card padding="none" title="Top products">
  <RankList
    sort="desc"
    limit={6}
    format={(v) => formatCurrency(v, 'USD', locale)}
    items={products.map((f) => ({
      id: f.id,
      label: f.name,
      value: f.totalMinor,
      swatch: f.hex,
      meta: `${f.units} units · ${f.pct}`,
    }))}
  />
</Card>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see DataTable: Several columns, sorting by the user, selection: use `DataTable`.
- Instead, see ProportionBar: Parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.
- Instead, see Chart: A trend over time: use `Chart`.
- Renders: Swatch

### Rating

> A read-only star rating. It is a single image (`role="img"`) with a text alternative such
as "3.5 out of 5 stars"; the stars themselves are decorative. Half stars are supported.

It does not accept input. An interactive rating needs radio-group semantics and is not part
of the design system yet.

A read-only star rating, such as a review score. One image with a text alternative ("3.5 out of 5 stars"); half stars are supported.

- Handoff source: `components/display/Rating` (TODO `CMP-DSP-06`).

- Import: `import { Rating } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Rating/Rating.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Rating`): Default, HalfStar, Empty, Full, WithValue, Sizes, CustomScale, OutOfRange, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | yes |  | The rating to show, from 0 to `max`. Values are clamped and rounded to the nearest half star ("3.7" shows three and a half stars, and says "3.5 out of 5 stars"). |
| `max` | `number` |  | `5` | Number of stars. A whole number from 1. Default `5`. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | Star size token: `sm` 12px, `md` 14px (default), `lg` 18px. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Also shows the value as text ("3.5/5") after the stars. Hidden from assistive technology: the name already says it. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ label: (value: string, max: string, maxCount: number) => string; }>` |  |  | Override the built-in messages for this instance. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Rating: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label(value: string, max: string, maxCount: number)` | `{value} out of {max} stars` | Accessible name of the rating. Arguments are already formatted for the locale. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-rating-fill`, `--ds-rating-gap`, `--ds-rating-star-gap`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- Show a score someone else gave (a review, a quality grade).
- Next to the review text in lists and cards, optionally with the numeric value.

#### When not to use

- To collect a rating: it takes no input. An interactive rating needs radio-group semantics (one tab stop, arrows, `Space`) and is out of scope for now; use `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup` with labelled options meanwhile.
- For an average with a distribution or a trend: use `Chart` or `ProportionBar`.

#### Anatomy

```
span[role=img][aria-label="3.5 out of 5 stars"]
  stars (aria-hidden)
    star x max      empty glyph + clipped filled glyph (0, 50 or 100 %)
  value             optional "3.5/5" (aria-hidden)
```

#### Accessibility

- `role="img"` with an `aria-label` from messages; the glyphs and the visible value are `aria-hidden`, so the rating is announced once.
- The label is pluralized by the scale (`1 out of 1 star`, `3.5 out of 5 stars`) and numbers follow the locale (`3,5 de 5 estrelas` in pt-BR).
- The value is not carried by color alone: the label and the optional value text state the number. The empty star uses `--ds-line-control` (3:1 against the surfaces); filled uses `--ds-warning`.
- Forced colors: filled stars use `CanvasText`, empty ones `GrayText`.

#### Content rules

- Show the number next to the stars when the exact value matters; stars alone are fine in dense lists.
- Pair a rating with the review it belongs to; do not leave it alone in a row of badges.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Rating value={4} />
<Rating value={3.5} showValue size="lg" />
<Rating value={7} max={10} />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see SegmentedControl: To collect a rating: it takes no input. An interactive rating needs radio-group semantics (one tab stop, arrows, `Space`) and is out of scope for now; use `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup` with labelled options meanwhile.
- Instead, see RadioGroup: To collect a rating: it takes no input. An interactive rating needs radio-group semantics (one tab stop, arrows, `Space`) and is out of scope for now; use `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup` with labelled options meanwhile.
- Instead, see Chart: For an average with a distribution or a trend: use `Chart` or `ProportionBar`.
- Instead, see ProportionBar: For an average with a distribution or a trend: use `Chart` or `ProportionBar`.
- Renders: Icon
- Used by: ApprovalCard

### RequiredMark

> The visible marker of a required field, text from messages. Hidden from assistive technology:
the control announces "required" itself. Use it when a field cannot use `Label`
(for example inside a `Checkbox` label).

Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

- Import: `import { RequiredMark } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Field/Field.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Field`): Anatomy, ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt, RealtimeValidation

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ requiredMark: string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`). |

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Field: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `requiredMark` | `*` | Visible marker after the label of a required field. Hidden from assistive technology. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### Exports

| Export                                 | What it is                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Label`                                | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker.                                                         |
| `Description`                          | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`.                                                     |
| `FieldError`                           | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. |
| `FieldMessages`                        | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box.                                                                                  |
| `RequiredMark`                         | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`.                                                                                                       |
| `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel`      | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel<P>` helps type stories.                                       |
| `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result).                                                                               |

#### Anatomy and spacing

```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

#### One state model (ARCH-009)

| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

#### Required marker

`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

#### Validation behavior: native (default), and why

React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language. A static `errorMessage` replaces only that browser text: a message the app supplied (a `validate` rule or `validationErrors` on a `Form`) is shown instead (GAP-009).
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

#### Accessibility

- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

#### Related components

- Used by: Checkbox, Switch

### ResponseFeedback

> Feedback and follow-up actions under an assistant response: two toggle buttons (good and bad
response, `aria-pressed`), then optional Copy and Regenerate.

Choosing a rating is reversible, so nothing asks to confirm: pressing the active rating again
removes it. A polite live region says "Feedback sent" or "Feedback removed" after the change.
The first render never announces anything. The buttons show text only for now: thumbs, copy
and refresh icons are not part of the curated icon set yet.

Feedback and follow-up actions under an assistant response: good and bad response toggles, then optional Copy and Regenerate. Import it from `loui-ds/patterns`.

- Import: `import { ResponseFeedback } from 'loui-ds/patterns';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/patterns/ResponseFeedback/ResponseFeedback.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Patterns/ResponseFeedback`): Default, RatedBad, RatingOnly, Regenerating, Disabled, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `ResponseRating \| null` |  |  | Controlled rating. `null` means no rating. |
| `defaultValue` | `ResponseRating \| null` |  | `null` | Initial rating when uncontrolled. |
| `onChange` | `(value: ResponseRating \| null) => void` |  |  | Called with the new rating, or `null` when the person takes their rating back. |
| `onCopy` | `() => void` |  |  | Called when Copy is pressed. Without it there is no Copy button. Confirm with a toast ("Copied"). |
| `onRegenerate` | `() => void` |  |  | Called when Regenerate is pressed. Without it there is no Regenerate button. |
| `isRegenerating` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Disables Regenerate while a new response is being generated. |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Disables every button. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ groupLabel: string; positive: string; negative: string; copy: string; regenerate: string; sent: string; removed: string; }>` |  |  | Override the built-in messages for this instance. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ ResponseFeedback: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `groupLabel` | `Rate this response` | Accessible name of the group of rating buttons. |
| `positive` | `Good response` | Toggle buttons; pressed means the rating is set. |
| `negative` | `Bad response` |  |
| `copy` | `Copy response` | Action buttons (verb plus object). |
| `regenerate` | `Regenerate response` |  |
| `sent` | `Feedback sent` | Polite announcements after a rating changes. |
| `removed` | `Feedback removed` |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-line-subtle`, `--ds-response-feedback-divider-gap`, `--ds-response-feedback-gap`

#### When to use

- Under each assistant response in a `ChatPanel`, to learn which answers help.

#### When not to use

- Collecting a written review or a star rating: use `Rating` in a form.
- Anything that sends the rating somewhere the owner cannot see: say where it goes in your product.

#### Anatomy

```
div
  group "Rate this response"   toggle "Good response" · toggle "Bad response"   (aria-pressed)
  button "Copy response"       only with onCopy
  button "Regenerate response" only with onRegenerate
  status                       visually hidden live region
```

#### Accessibility

- The rating buttons are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) in a labelled group. Each is a tab stop; `Space` and `Enter` press.
- Rating is reversible, so nothing asks to confirm: pressing the active button again removes the rating.
- A polite live region says "Feedback sent" or "Feedback removed" after a change. It is silent on first render.
- Each control shows a decorative icon (`ThumbsUpIcon`, `ThumbsDownIcon`, `CopyIcon`, `RefreshIcon`) next to its visible text label; the text is the accessible name.

#### Content rules

- Buttons are verb plus object ("Copy response", "Regenerate response").
- Confirm Copy with a short past-tense toast ("Copied"), outside this pattern.
- Regenerate replaces content: offer Undo, as for any reversible action.

#### Example

```tsx
<ResponseFeedback
  onChange={(rating) => saveRating(message.id, rating)}
  onCopy={() => copyToClipboard(message.content)}
  onRegenerate={() => regenerate(message.id)}
  isRegenerating={busy}
/>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Rating: Collecting a written review or a star rating: use `Rating` in a form.
- Renders: Button, Icon, Toggle, VisuallyHidden

### ScrollArea

> A scrolling container with thin, themed scrollbars. It scrolls inside the space its parent
gives it: give it a height (or put it in a flex column and let it shrink).

While its content overflows it becomes a keyboard stop (`tabindex="0"`) and a labelled
`region`, so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys (WCAG 2.1.1). When nothing
overflows it is a plain container, with no tab stop and no landmark. A name is therefore
always required.

A scrolling container with thin, themed scrollbars that stays keyboard accessible.

- Import: `import { ScrollArea } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/ScrollArea/ScrollArea.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Layout/ScrollArea`): Default, NotScrollable, Horizontal, Both, LabelledBy, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `'both' \| 'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` |  | `'vertical'` | Which axes scroll. Default `vertical`. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name of the region ("Order history"). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the region. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-text-3`

#### When to use

- A bounded list, log or panel inside a page: a notification list, a long form step, a code output.
- A region that must scroll on its own while the page around it does not.

#### When not to use

- For the page itself: let the document scroll, or use `AppShell`'s `main`.
- For a table: `DataTable` has its own horizontal scroll and sticky parts.
- Inside a Dialog or Sheet body: those already scroll their body.

#### Anatomy

```
div (overflow auto, scrollbar-width: thin)
  div (content wrapper, observed for size changes)
    children
```

#### Accessibility

- A scroll container must be reachable by keyboard (WCAG 2.1.1). While the content overflows, the area gets `tabindex="0"` and `role="region"` with your label; with nothing to scroll it is a plain container (no tab stop, no landmark). A `ResizeObserver` keeps this in sync as content or size changes.
- Because focusability is dynamic, the type always requires a name, so a scrollable area is never unlabelled.
- Arrow keys, `PageUp`/`PageDown`, `Home`/`End` scroll it natively.
- The focus ring is drawn inside the box, so a clipping parent cannot hide it.
- Scrollbars are the browser's thin scrollbars colored with `--ds-line-control` (3:1 on the background); on hover they brighten to `--ds-text-3`.

#### Content rules

- Name it for what it holds: "Order history", "Activity", not "Scrollable area".

#### Examples

```tsx
<div style={{ blockSize: 240 }}>
  <ScrollArea aria-label="Activity">{events.map(renderEvent)}</ScrollArea>
</div>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see AppShell: For the page itself: let the document scroll, or use `AppShell`'s `main`.
- Instead, see DataTable: For a table: `DataTable` has its own horizontal scroll and sticky parts.

### SearchInput

> A search box: leading search icon, clear button (and `Escape` clears), optional decorative
shortcut hint, optional suggestions with accent-insensitive match highlighting. Built on React
Aria `SearchField` (plain) or `ComboBox` (with `suggestions`).

`onSubmit(text)` fires on `Enter` when no suggestion is highlighted.

A search box: leading search icon, clear button, optional decorative shortcut hint and optional suggestions with accent-insensitive match highlighting. Built on React Aria `SearchField` (plain) or `ComboBox` (with `suggestions`). Task: CMP-INP-06.

- Import: `import { SearchInput } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/SearchInput/SearchInput.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/SearchInput`): Default, ClearButton, WithShortcutHint, Landmark, WithSuggestions, AccentInsensitiveHighlight, NoSuggestions, Disabled, VisibleLabel, Sizes

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  |  | The text. Pair with `onChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  |  | The initial text when uncontrolled. |
| `onChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  |  | Called with the new text on every keystroke and when it is cleared. |
