| `empty` | `No data to show` | Text shown in place of the bars when there is no data. |
| `allHidden` | `All series are hidden. Show one in the legend.` | Text shown in place of the bars when every series is hidden through the legend. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-chart-series-1`, `--ds-chart-series-2`, `--ds-chart-series-3`, `--ds-chart-series-4`, `--ds-chart-series-hatch-size`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-stacked-bar-bar-thickness`, `--ds-stacked-bar-category-w`, `--ds-stacked-bar-color`, `--ds-stacked-bar-column-max-w`, `--ds-stacked-bar-extent`, `--ds-stacked-bar-height`, `--ds-stacked-bar-readout-min-h`, `--ds-stacked-bar-segment-gap`, `--ds-stacked-bar-share`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`

#### When to use

- Showing how each of a few categories (2 to about 12) divides into the same 2 to 8 parts: orders per channel per quarter, tasks per status per team.
- Comparing totals and composition together (default), or composition only (`normalize`).

#### When not to use

- One whole divided into parts: `ProportionBar`.
- One series over time or categories: `Chart`. Ranked values: `RankList`.
- Exact figures the reader must look up: give them a table; the hidden table is for assistive technology.
- More than eight series: group the tail into "Other".

#### Anatomy

```
div.root
  div[role=group][aria-label][aria-describedby]
    ul
      li  category (aria-hidden) · div.slot > div[role=img][tabindex][aria-label="Q1: Online 40…"] · total (aria-hidden)
  p[aria-hidden]  readout of the focused or hovered bar
  Legend           names the series (optionally toggles them)
  VisuallyHidden   instructions (aria-describedby) and a <table> with all values
```

Drawn with HTML and CSS: bars use one scale (the largest total is full length), parts are `flex` shares of their bar. There is no value axis; the total is printed with each bar and the legend shows the total of each series.

#### Props (key ones)

| Prop                   | Type                         | Default        | Notes                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `data`                 | `{ label, values }[]`        | -              | `values` is keyed by series `id`; missing or negative counts as 0     |
| `series`               | `{ id, label, color? }[]`    | -              | Part order: start to end (horizontal), bottom to top (vertical)       |
| `orientation`          | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` |                                                                       |
| `normalize`            | `boolean`                    | `false`        | Every bar at full length (100% stacked)                               |
| `format`               | `(value) => string`          | `Intl`         | Totals, legend, summaries, table. Use `formatCurrency` for money      |
| `legend`               | `boolean`                    | `true`         | The legend names the series; turn it off only if you name them nearby |
| `interactiveLegend`    | `boolean`                    | `false`        | Legend items hide and show series                                     |
| `hiddenSeries`         | `readonly string[]`          |                | Controlled hidden series                                              |
| `defaultHiddenSeries`  | `readonly string[]`          | `[]`           | Initial hidden series when uncontrolled                               |
| `onHiddenSeriesChange` | `(ids: string[]) => void`    |                |                                                                       |
| `height`               | `number \| string`           | 200px          | Vertical only (`--ds-stacked-bar-height`)                             |
| `description`          | `string`                     |                | Read after the name                                                   |
| `categoryLabel`        | `string`                     | "Category"     | Header of the first table column                                      |
| `messages`             | `Partial<messages>`          |                | Instructions, summaries, table headers, empty states                  |

`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is required.

#### Telling series apart without color

- A 2px gap (the track shows through) separates neighbouring parts.
- Series follow a neutral ramp of four steps that differ in lightness (`--ds-chart-series-1` to `-4`), so they also differ for readers with color vision deficiencies. From the fifth series the ramp repeats with a hatch pattern (up to eight). The series `color` prop is for when that is not enough; it is never hatched.
- The legend names every series and its swatch uses the same fill. A series keeps its fill when another is hidden.
- Each bar's summary and the data table list every series by name with its value.

The single-accent rule holds: the accent appears only in the focus ring. Signal colors appear only if you pass them as explicit series colors.

#### Accessibility

- A group named by `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`, described by the instructions and your `description`. Each bar is an image whose name is its summary: "Q1: Online 40, Store 30, and Phone 10. Total 80."
- Keyboard: one tab stop for all bars (roving). Arrow keys (and `Home`/`End`) move between bars, `Escape` dismisses the readout. The focused bar has a visible focus ring (system colors in forced colors).
- Why per-bar and not per-segment: a bar is a large target, the path through a chart stays short (one stop), and its single summary gives screen reader users the whole composition at once. The same text is printed in the readout line under the chart for keyboard and pointer users; the readout is `aria-hidden` because the focused bar is already announced.
- Hover shows the same readout. The line has reserved height, so nothing shifts.
- A visually hidden `<table>` (caption, category and one column per visible series, total) carries all values.
- Hidden series leave the bars, totals, summaries and table. If all are hidden, a message says so. An empty `data` shows "No data to show".
- Contrast: every ramp step keeps 3:1 against the track (`--ds-bg`); labels use `text-2`.
- Forced colors: segments use system colors; the track gets a border.
- Category labels are truncated in horizontal bars (96px column, `--ds-stacked-bar-category-w`); the summary and the table carry the full text. Keep labels short.

#### Content rules

- Bar labels: short ("Q1", "North"). Series labels: short nouns in sentence case.
- Name the chart for what it shows ("Orders per quarter, by channel").
- Formatted values come from `Intl`; pass `format` for currency.

#### Example

```tsx
<StackedBar
  aria-label="Orders per quarter, by channel"
  interactiveLegend
  series={[
    { id: 'online', label: 'Online' },
    { id: 'store', label: 'Store' },
    { id: 'phone', label: 'Phone' },
  ]}
  data={[
    { label: 'Q1', values: { online: 40, store: 30, phone: 10 } },
    { label: 'Q2', values: { online: 50, store: 20, phone: 30 } },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Not included

- Value axis and grid lines, negative values, grouped (side by side) bars, per-segment focus, zoom. Use `Chart` for a single series with an axis.
- Series order in vertical bars is fixed (first series at the bottom); the chart never sorts.

#### Related components

- Instead, see ProportionBar: One whole divided into parts: `ProportionBar`.
- Instead, see Chart: One series over time or categories: `Chart`. Ranked values: `RankList`.
- Instead, see RankList: One series over time or categories: `Chart`. Ranked values: `RankList`.
- Renders: Legend, VisuallyHidden

### StatCard

> An indicator card: a mono caption, a large mono number and a short note, optionally with a
trend and a small visual (such as a `ProportionBar`) in between.

It is a description list: the label is the term, the value and the note are its
descriptions, so a screen reader announces "Sold, $37,655.30, Up 12% vs previous 30 days".
A colored value is never the only signal: `tone` other than `neutral` requires a `note` or a
`trend`, and the trend is written as text ("Up 12%").

An indicator card for the top of a screen: a mono caption, a large mono number, an optional small visual and a short note or trend in words.

- Import: `import { StatCard } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/StatCard/StatCard.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/StatCard`): Default, Large, WithAside, WarningTone, DangerTone, SuccessTone, TrendUp, TrendUpIsBad, TrendDownAndFlat, WithProportionBar, LongText, Grid, PortugueseBrazil

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | What the number is, in a few words: "Sold", "Overdue". Shown as a mono caption (uppercase by CSS) and used as the term of the card. |
| `value` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The number or amount. Format it with `formatCurrency` or `formatNumber` for the active locale. |
| `size` | `'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | `md` (default, 24px) or `lg` (30px). |
| `aside` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Short mono text at the end of the label row: "42%". Read after the value. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Content between the value and the note, for example a 4px `ProportionBar`. |
| `noteTone` | `'neutral' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | `'neutral'` | Color of the note text. Default `neutral`. Only affects color: the note is text anyway. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ trendUp: (percent: string) => string; trendDown: (percent: string) => string; trendFlat: string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | `'neutral'` | Color of the value. Use `danger` or `warning` only when the number asks for action, `success` when everything is fine. Default `neutral`. A colored value must be backed by text: pass `note` or `trend` (type error otherwise). |
| `note` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Context or change in words: "3 sales · average ticket $120". |
| `trend` | `StatCardTrend` |  |  | A change versus a previous period, rendered as text through the messages. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `md`, `lg`
- `tone`: `neutral`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ StatCard: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trendUp(percent: string)` | `Up {percent}` | Text of an upward trend. `percent` is already formatted for the locale ("12%"). |
| `trendDown(percent: string)` | `Down {percent}` | Text of a downward trend. |
| `trendFlat` | `No change` | Text of a trend without change. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-danger`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-fs-num`, `--ds-fs-num-lg`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-meta`, `--ds-lh-num`, `--ds-lh-num-lg`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-stat-card-gap`, `--ds-stat-card-padding`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-tracking-caption`, `--ds-tracking-display`, `--ds-tracking-title`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-weight-medium`, `--ds-weight-regular`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- A handful of key numbers at the top of a page (Today, Purchases, Finance, Reports).
- A number with context: "3 sales · average ticket $120.00", or a change versus a previous period.

#### When not to use

- Many numbers that need comparing or sorting: use `DataTable`.
- A value the user edits: use a field.
- A status without a number: use `Badge`.

#### Anatomy

```
dl.root (surface, 1px line, radius lg, padding 20)
  dt   label        mono caption, uppercase by CSS
  dd   value        mono 24px (md) or 30px (lg); colored by tone
  dd   aside        short mono text at the end of the label row (optional)
  dd   children     small visual, e.g. a 4px ProportionBar (optional)
  dd   note         trend (arrow + "Up 12%" + comparison) and/or note text
```

#### Props (key ones)

| Prop       | Type                                        | Default   | Notes                                                                                   |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`    | `ReactNode`                                 | -         | A few words: "Sold", "Overdue"                                                          |
| `value`    | `ReactNode`                                 | -         | Format with `formatCurrency` / `formatNumber`                                           |
| `size`     | `md \| lg`                                  | `md`      | `--ds-fs-num` / `--ds-fs-num-lg`                                                        |
| `tone`     | `neutral \| success \| warning \| danger`   | `neutral` | Color of the value. Any other tone requires `note` or `trend` (type error, dev warning) |
| `note`     | `ReactNode`                                 |           | Context in words                                                                        |
| `noteTone` | `neutral \| success \| warning \| danger`   | `neutral` | Color of the note text                                                                  |
| `trend`    | `{ direction, value?, tone?, comparedTo? }` |           | Change as text: "Up 12%", "Down 4.5%", "No change". `value` is a ratio (`0.12`)         |
| `aside`    | `ReactNode`                                 |           | "42%"                                                                                   |
| `children` | `ReactNode`                                 |           | Between the value and the note                                                          |
| `messages` | `Partial<messages>`                         |           | `trendUp(percent)`, `trendDown(percent)`, `trendFlat`                                   |

#### Accessibility

- It is a description list: the label is the term (`dt`), the value and the note are its descriptions (`dd`). A screen reader announces "Sold, $37,655.30, Up 12% vs previous 30 days".
- Color is never the only signal. A non-neutral `tone` must come with a `note` or a `trend` (enforced by types, with a one-time development warning for untyped callers). The trend direction is written as text and the arrow icon is decorative.
- Contrast: the signal colors on `surface` pass 4.5:1; notes use `text-2`; the caption uses `text-3` (do not put the card on a raised or hover surface).
- No interaction. If the card should open something, wrap the label in a link or add a button in the note area.

#### Content rules

- Tone only changes when there is something to do: `danger`/`warning` for numbers that ask for action, `success` for "all done". Do not decorate.
- At most four cards per row; use a grid with `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(240px, 1fr))` so large numbers are not cut.
- Trends say what changed and compared to what ("Up 12% vs previous 30 days"). When up is bad (costs, returns) set `trend.tone: 'danger'`.

#### Example

```tsx
<StatCard
  label="Sold"
  value={formatCurrency(3765530, 'USD', locale)}
  trend={{ direction: 'up', value: 0.12, comparedTo: 'vs previous 30 days' }}
/>
<StatCard label="Overdue" value="$96.40" tone="danger" note="Water bill since Oct 28" />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see DataTable: Many numbers that need comparing or sorting: use `DataTable`.
- Instead, see Badge: A status without a number: use `Badge`.
- Renders: Icon

### StatusSteps

> A horizontal indicator of progress through a linear status flow (Draft, Packed, Shipped).
It is an ordered list; every step states its progress as text read by assistive technology
("Completed", "Current", "Not started", from messages), and the current step has
`aria-current="step"`. The marker (number or check) and the connector lines are decorative.

With `onSelect` each step becomes a real button, so the status can be changed from here.

A horizontal indicator of progress through a linear status flow (Draft, Packed, Shipped, Delivered). It is an ordered list; each step states its progress as text for assistive technology, and the steps can optionally be buttons to change the status.

- Handoff source: `components/erp/StatusSteps.jsx` (TODO `CMP-PAT-05`).

- Import: `import { StatusSteps } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/StatusSteps/StatusSteps.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/StatusSteps`): Default, FirstStep, Complete, ManySteps, LongLabels, Interactive, Controlled, Portuguese, RightToLeft, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `readonly StatusStep[]` | yes |  | The steps, in order. |
| `current` | `number` | yes |  | Index of the current step (0-based). Steps before it are complete. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name of the list ("Order status"). Required: name this or use `aria-labelledby`. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the list. |
| `complete` | `boolean` |  | `false` | When `true`, the current step is complete too (the whole flow is done). |
| `onSelect` | `(index: number, step: StatusStep) => void` |  |  | Makes every step a button. Called with the index and the step; the consumer decides whether going back or skipping ahead is allowed. Reversible changes need no confirmation (offer Undo). |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ complete: string; current: string; upcoming: string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ StatusSteps: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `complete` | `Completed` | Read after the label of a step that is done. |
| `current` | `Current` | Read after the label of the step in progress. |
| `upcoming` | `Not started` | Read after the label of a step that has not started. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-lh-meta`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-primary-bg`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-status-steps-connector-thickness`, `--ds-status-steps-content-z-index`, `--ds-status-steps-gap`, `--ds-status-steps-marker-border-width`, `--ds-status-steps-marker-hover-border`, `--ds-status-steps-marker-size`, `--ds-status-steps-padding-block`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-inverse`, `--ds-weight-medium`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- Show where a record is in a fixed, ordered flow, optionally letting people move it.
- A flow of 3 to 6 short steps.

#### When not to use

- A multi-page form with validation and Back/Next: build it with `Tabs` or your router.
- Non-linear or parallel states: use `Badge`.
- A percentage of something: use `Progress`.

#### Anatomy

```
ol aria-label="Order status"
  li[data-state=complete|current|upcoming]
    span | button            (button only with onSelect; aria-current="step" on the current one)
      marker                 (number or check, aria-hidden)
      label
      visually hidden state  ("Completed", "Current", "Not started")
  connector lines            (CSS pseudo-elements, decorative)
```

#### Accessibility

- `ol` / `li` semantics; the position is implied by the list ("2 of 4").
- Every step's state is real text read after its label (`Completed`, `Current`, `Not started`, from messages). The number or check is `aria-hidden`; color and the check are not the only signal.
- The current step has `aria-current="step"`.
- With `onSelect`, steps are native buttons: Tab / Shift+Tab move, Enter and Space select, focus has the accent ring. There is no roving focus because this is a list of buttons, not a composite widget.
- Contrast: upcoming labels use `--ds-text-2` and the upcoming marker border `--ds-line-control` (3:1).
- Forced colors: current and complete markers use `Highlight`; connectors use `ButtonText`.

#### Content rules

- Labels are nouns or past participles in sentence case ("Packed", "In production").
- Moving a status is reversible: do not confirm; offer Undo in a toast.

#### Examples

```tsx
<StatusSteps
  aria-label="Order status"
  steps={[
    { id: 'draft', label: 'Draft' },
    { id: 'packed', label: 'Packed' },
    { id: 'shipped', label: 'Shipped' },
  ]}
  current={1}
  onSelect={(index) => setStatus(index)}
/>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Tabs: A multi-page form with validation and Back/Next: build it with `Tabs` or your router.
- Instead, see Badge: Non-linear or parallel states: use `Badge`.
- Instead, see Progress: A percentage of something: use `Progress`.
- Renders: Icon, VisuallyHidden

### Stepper

> Progress through a multi-step flow such as a setup assistant. It is an ordered list; every
step states its progress as text for assistive technology ("Completed", "Current", "Not
started") and the current step has `aria-current="step"`. Markers and connectors are
decorative. Completed steps can be buttons with `onStepPress`.

In narrow containers the horizontal orientation shows only the markers and a visible summary
("Step 3 of 9"), so nine steps fit in 320 px.

Progress through a multi-step flow, such as a 9-step setup assistant. It is an ordered list; each step states its progress as text for assistive technology, and completed steps can optionally be buttons to go back.

- Import: `import { Stepper } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Stepper/Stepper.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Stepper`): Default, FirstStep, AllComplete, Vertical, NineStepsNarrow, NineStepsWide, LongLabels, GoBackToCompletedSteps, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `readonly StepperStep[]` | yes |  | The steps, in order. |
| `current` | `number` | yes |  | Index of the current step (0-based). Steps before it are completed. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name of the list ("New agent steps"). Required: name this or use `aria-labelledby`. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the list. |
| `complete` | `boolean` |  | `false` | When `true`, the current step is completed too (the whole flow is done). |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` |  | `'horizontal'` | `horizontal` (default) or `vertical`. Horizontal collapses to markers and "Step 3 of 9" in narrow containers. |
| `onStepPress` | `(index: number, step: StepperStep) => void` |  |  | Makes every completed step a button that calls this with its index and the step, so people can go back. The current and upcoming steps are never buttons: the flow itself (Next) moves forward. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ complete: string; current: string; upcoming: string; summary: (current: string, total: string) => string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Stepper: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `complete` | `Completed` | Read after the label of a step that is done. |
| `current` | `Current` | Read after the label of the step in progress. |
| `upcoming` | `Not started` | Read after the label of a step that has not started. |
| `summary(current: string, total: string)` | `Step {current} of {total}` | Visible summary of the progress when the labels do not fit; `current` and `total` are formatted numbers. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-meta`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-primary-bg`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-stepper-connector-thickness`, `--ds-stepper-content-z-index`, `--ds-stepper-gap`, `--ds-stepper-marker-border-width`, `--ds-stepper-marker-size`, `--ds-stepper-padding-block`, `--ds-stepper-step-gap`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-inverse`, `--ds-weight-medium`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- A guided flow with several steps shown one at a time (assistant, onboarding, checkout), where people need to know where they are and how much is left.
- Flows of 3 to 10 steps. In narrow containers it collapses to markers plus "Step 3 of 9".

#### When not to use

- The status of a record in a fixed flow (Draft, Packed, Shipped): use `StatusSteps`.
- A percentage of something: use `Progress`.
- Switching between views of the same content: use `Tabs`.

##### Stepper and StatusSteps

|                    | Stepper                                        | StatusSteps                              |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Describes          | Your progress through a flow you are doing now | The state a record is in                 |
| Typical length     | 3 to 10 steps                                  | 3 to 6 steps                             |
| Interaction        | Only completed steps can be pressed (go back)  | Every step can be pressed (change state) |
| Orientation        | Horizontal or vertical                         | Horizontal                               |
| Narrow containers  | Markers plus "Step 3 of 9"                     | Same layout                              |
| Per-step help text | `description` (vertical)                       | None                                     |

#### Anatomy

```
div[data-orientation]
  p (aria-hidden)           "Step 3 of 9: Label", visible only in narrow containers
  ol aria-label="Setup progress"
    li[data-state=complete|current|upcoming]
      span | button         (button only for completed steps with onStepPress; aria-current="step" on the current one)
        marker              (number or check, aria-hidden)
        label + visually hidden state ("Completed", "Current", "Not started")
        description         (vertical only)
  connector lines           (CSS pseudo-elements, decorative)
```

#### Accessibility

- A real ordered list named by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The current step has `aria-current="step"` (on the button when it is one).
- Progress is text, not only color or a check: every step ends with a visually hidden "Completed", "Current" or "Not started" (messages).
- Markers, connectors and the "Step 3 of 9" summary are decorative duplicates (`aria-hidden`); the list conveys the same information.
- Keyboard: completed step buttons are in the Tab order and activate with `Enter` or `Space`. Upcoming steps are not focusable, so people cannot skip ahead; move forward with the flow's own Next button.
- Target size: the marker is 24 px, so step buttons meet WCAG 2.5.8 even at 320 px with 9 steps.
- Reflow: in containers up to 480 px wide the horizontal labels are visually hidden (still read by screen readers) and a visible "Step N of M: label" line appears. The vertical orientation needs no collapse.
- Forced colors: markers and connectors use system colors; the state text still names every step.

#### Content rules

- Labels: a few words, sentence case, nouns ("Source", "Review"), not sentences.
- The description says what the step is for, in one line ("Name and purpose").
- Name the list for what it is: "New agent steps", not "Steps".

#### Examples

```tsx
<Stepper aria-label="Setup progress" steps={steps} current={step} />

<Stepper
  aria-label="Setup progress"
  orientation="vertical"
  steps={steps}
  current={step}
  onStepPress={(index) => setStep(index)}
/>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see StatusSteps: The status of a record in a fixed flow (Draft, Packed, Shipped): use `StatusSteps`.
- Instead, see Progress: A percentage of something: use `Progress`.
- Instead, see Tabs: Switching between views of the same content: use `Tabs`.
- Renders: Icon, VisuallyHidden

### SubMenu

> An item that opens a nested menu. Arrow Right (Arrow Left in right-to-left) opens it and
Arrow Left closes it; Escape closes the submenu first, then the menu.

A menu of commands that opens from a trigger. Built on React Aria `MenuTrigger`, `Popover` and `Menu`. Exports `Menu`, `MenuItem`, `MenuSection`, `MenuSeparator`, `SubMenu` and `MoreActionsMenu`.

- Handoff source: `components/navigation/Menu` (CMP-NAV-02).

- Import: `import { SubMenu } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Menu/Menu.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Menu`): Default, EscapeRestoresFocus, TypeaheadAndHomeEnd, Open, CheckboxItems, RadioItems, WithSections, WithSubmenu, LongLabels, MoreActions

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Label of the item that opens the submenu; end it with an ellipsis when it opens more choices ("Move to…"). |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | `MenuItem`, `MenuSection` and `MenuSeparator` elements of the submenu. |
| `textValue` | `string` |  |  | Used for typeahead and as the item's name when `label` is not a string. |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean` |  |  | Disables the item: it cannot be opened or focused by typeahead. |
| `delay` | `number` |  |  | Milliseconds the pointer must rest on the item before the submenu opens. Default 200. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the submenu list. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-danger-soft-hover`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-item-h`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-menu-indicator-size`, `--ds-menu-max-width`, `--ds-menu-min-width`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-select-popover-max-height`, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-tracking-caption`

#### When to use

- Row, card or toolbar actions that do not deserve their own button.
- View options with check or radio items (columns shown, sort order, density).

#### When not to use

- Choosing a value for a field: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
- Content the user types into or operates (filters, forms): use `Popover`.
- Navigation between pages: use `Tabs`, `Sidebar` or `Breadcrumb`.
- The only way to reach an important action: keep primary actions visible.

#### Anatomy

```
MenuTrigger
  trigger            Button | IconButton    aria-haspopup=true, aria-expanded
  Popover            raised surface, radius lg, overlay shadow, z popover
    Menu             role=menu, named by the trigger (aria-labelledby)
      MenuItem       role=menuitem | menuitemcheckbox | menuitemradio, height --ds-item-h
        indicator    check / dot (selectable menus)
        label
        shortcut     mono hint, optional
        chevron      when it opens a SubMenu
      MenuSection    role=group, caption optional (mono uppercase)
      MenuSeparator  1px line
```

#### Accessibility

Keyboard contract (AGENTS.md section 8):

| Key                                     | Behavior                                                        |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter`, `Space`, `ArrowDown` (trigger) | Opens the menu and focuses the first item                       |
| `ArrowUp` (trigger)                     | Opens the menu and focuses the last item                        |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown`                 | Move between items; disabled items are skipped                  |
| `Home` / `End`                          | First / last item                                               |
| Typing                                  | Typeahead: focus moves to the item whose label starts with it   |
| `Enter` / `Space`                       | Activates the item (checkbox and radio items toggle) and closes |
| `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft`              | Open / close a submenu (mirrored in right-to-left)              |
| `Escape`                                | Closes one level; focus returns to the trigger                  |

- Items are real `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` or `menuitemradio` elements with `aria-checked`; the handoff used `tabIndex=0` divs with no keyboard activation.
- Danger is red text plus the item's own label ("Delete order"); the colour is never the only signal. `tone="danger"` does not confirm: open a `ConfirmDialog` from `onAction`.
- The shortcut hint is visual; bind the key yourself. It uses `--ds-text-2` so the hint stays legible next to the label.
- Focus is shown with the accent ring; forced colors use a `Highlight` outline.
- Layer: `--ds-z-popover` (see Dialog doc, "Layers", for menus opened inside a Dialog or Sheet).
- The `MoreActionsMenu` trigger has a tooltip that repeats its name.

#### Content rules

- Items are a verb plus object in sentence case ("Duplicate order"). End with an ellipsis only when the item opens something that needs more input ("Move to…").
- Order: most common first, destructive last, separated by a `MenuSeparator`.

#### Examples

```tsx
<MoreActionsMenu onAction={(key) => run(String(key))}>
  <MenuItem id="edit" shortcut="Ctrl+E">Edit order</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem id="duplicate">Duplicate order</MenuItem>
  <MenuSeparator />
  <MenuItem id="delete" tone="danger">Delete order</MenuItem>
</MoreActionsMenu>

<Menu trigger={<Button>View</Button>} selectionMode="multiple" defaultSelectedKeys={['id']}>
  <MenuItem id="id">Show ID</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem id="status">Show status</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Select: Choosing a value for a field: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
- Instead, see Combobox: Choosing a value for a field: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
- Instead, see Popover: Content the user types into or operates (filters, forms): use `Popover`.
- Instead, see Tabs: Navigation between pages: use `Tabs`, `Sidebar` or `Breadcrumb`.
- Instead, see Sidebar: Navigation between pages: use `Tabs`, `Sidebar` or `Breadcrumb`.
- Instead, see Breadcrumb: Navigation between pages: use `Tabs`, `Sidebar` or `Breadcrumb`.
- Renders: Icon, IconButton

### SuggestionChip

> A dashed chip that proposes a piece of text. Pressing it **inserts** that text into a
nearby field (for example a message composer); it never submits or navigates.

The dashed border and the leading plus tell sighted users that it adds something. The plus
is decorative: screen readers hear the label, so word the label as the text itself and put
the chips in a labelled group ("Suggested replies") so the purpose is announced once.

A dashed chip that proposes a piece of text. Pressing it **inserts** that text into a nearby field (a message composer, a note, a search box). Built on React Aria `Button`.

- Handoff source: `components/forms/SuggestionChip.jsx` (TODO `CMP-FRM-10`).

- Import: `import { SuggestionChip } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/SuggestionChip/SuggestionChip.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/SuggestionChip`): Default, Disabled, LongText, InsertsText, RightToLeft, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The suggested text. The chip is named by it and, when pressed, the consumer inserts exactly this text (or the text it stands for) into the field it belongs to. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` |  |  | Ref to the underlying `<button>` element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaBaseButtonProps` (react-aria): `aria-controls`, `aria-current`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-pressed`, `form`, `formAction`, `formEncType`, `formMethod`, `formNoValidate`, `formTarget`, `name`, `preventFocusOnPress`, `type`, `value`
- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`
- From `ButtonProps` (react-aria): `isDisabled`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `FocusableDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `excludeFromTabOrder`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `HoverEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onHoverChange`, `onHoverEnd`, `onHoverStart`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `PressEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onClick`, `onPress`, `onPressChange`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressStart`, `onPressUp`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- Suggested replies, snippets, prompts or tags that save typing.
- The result of pressing is always "this text appears in the field"; the user still reviews and sends it.

#### When not to use

- To run an action (save, send, delete): use `Button`.
- To filter or toggle a state: use `Tag` in a `TagGroup` with selection, or `SegmentedControl`.
- To navigate: use `Link`.

#### Behavior

`SuggestionChip` does not know about the field. `onPress` is where the consumer inserts the text (append at the caret, replace the selection, or set the value) and, usually, returns focus to the field. The chip never submits a form and never sends anything.

#### Accessibility

- A real `<button type="button">`: `Enter` and `Space` press it.
- The leading plus is decorative (`aria-hidden`) and the dashed border is visual. Neither is the only cue: the chip sits in a group whose label says what the chips are, so give the container a name (`role="group"` with `aria-label="Suggested replies"`).
- Word the label as the text itself ("Your order has shipped."), not as an instruction. Screen reader users then hear exactly what will be inserted.
- Long text wraps inside the available width; the chip keeps a 32px minimum height.
- Disabled: reduced opacity and no hover. The handoff's .45 and .35 values are unified into one token.
- Focus: accent border and ring.

#### Content rules

- The label is the text to insert, in sentence case, in the voice of the product (see AGENTS.md section 6).
- Keep it to one sentence; very long snippets belong in a template picker.

#### Examples

```tsx
<div role="group" aria-label="Suggested replies">
  {replies.map((reply) => (
    <SuggestionChip key={reply} onPress={() => insert(reply)}>
      {reply}
    </SuggestionChip>
  ))}
</div>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Button: To run an action (save, send, delete): use `Button`.
- Instead, see Tag: To filter or toggle a state: use `Tag` in a `TagGroup` with selection, or `SegmentedControl`.
- Instead, see TagGroup: To filter or toggle a state: use `Tag` in a `TagGroup` with selection, or `SegmentedControl`.
- Instead, see SegmentedControl: To filter or toggle a state: use `Tag` in a `TagGroup` with selection, or `SegmentedControl`.
- Instead, see Link: To navigate: use `Link`.
- Renders: Icon

### Swatch

> A small circle filled with a color, with a subtle inset ring so dark colors stay visible on
dark surfaces. It needs either a `label` (the color's name) or `decorative`, so the color is
never the only carrier of meaning.

Built as a plain element rather than React Aria `ColorSwatch`: that one paints an inline
`background` and names itself with a generated description ("vibrant blue"), while this one
sets only the `--ds-swatch-color` custom property and uses the name you give it.

A small circle filled with a color, with a subtle inset ring so dark colors stay visible on dark surfaces. It shows a color; it never names it, so every swatch is either labelled or explicitly decorative.

- Handoff source: `components/erp/Swatch.jsx` (TODO `CMP-PAT-03`).

- Import: `import { Swatch } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Swatch/Swatch.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Swatch`): Default, Sizes, ExtremeColors, Decorative, ShortHex

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | `string` | yes |  | The color to show, as `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`. Anything else throws in development and renders an empty circle in production. |
| `label` | `string` |  |  | Name of the color ("Navy"). Required whenever the swatch is the only thing that identifies the color: a color on its own says nothing to a screen reader or to a color-blind user. |
| `decorative` | `true` |  |  | Hides the swatch from assistive technology. Use it only when the color is also named by adjacent text (a table cell, an option label). |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | Diameter token: `sm` 16px, `md` 20px (default), `lg` 32px. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-line-control`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-swatch-color`, `--ds-swatch-ring`, `--ds-swatch-size-lg`, `--ds-swatch-size-md`, `--ds-swatch-size-sm`

#### When to use

- Next to the name of a color, tag or category (a legend, a table cell, an option).
- On its own, with a `label`, when the color is the whole content (a color chip in a toolbar).

#### When not to use

- To carry a status: use `Badge` (text plus tone).
- To pick a color: use `ColorOption` from `loui-ds/patterns`.
- For arbitrary CSS colors (`rgb()`, names): only `#rgb` and `#rrggbb` are accepted.

#### Anatomy

```
span[role=img] aria-label="Navy"        (labelled)
span[aria-hidden]                        (decorative)
  background: var(--ds-swatch-color)
  inset ring: var(--ds-swatch-ring)
```

#### Accessibility

- A color on its own is not information: it is invisible to screen readers and ambiguous for color-blind users, hence the required `label` or `decorative`.
- Labelled swatches are `role="img"`. Decorative ones are `aria-hidden`.
- The inset ring uses `--ds-swatch-ring`, a low-contrast outline that keeps near-black swatches visible. It is not a boundary meant to reach 3:1: the name next to or on the swatch is what identifies it.
- Forced colors: `forced-color-adjust: none` keeps the fill, and a `ButtonText` border is added.

#### Content rules

- Labels are plain color names in sentence case ("Navy", "Brick red"), not hex codes.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Swatch color="#1f3a93" label="Navy" />

<span>
  <Swatch color="#c0392b" decorative size="sm" /> Brick red
</span>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Badge: To carry a status: use `Badge` (text plus tone).
- Instead, see ColorOption: To pick a color: use `ColorOption` from `loui-ds/patterns`.
- Used by: ApprovalCard, ColorOption, MatrixGrid, RankList

### Switch

> An on/off setting that applies immediately. Renders a native checkbox with `role="switch"`
(so `name` / `value` take part in form submission), a 36x20 track and a 16px knob.

State props follow React Aria: `isSelected`, `defaultSelected` and `onChange(isSelected)`.
For a choice that is confirmed later with a Save button, prefer `Checkbox`.

An on/off setting that takes effect immediately. A native checkbox with `role="switch"`, a 36x20 track and a 16px knob. Built on React Aria `SwitchField` + `SwitchButton` (the non-deprecated pair that supports a description and an error outside the label). Shared field behavior is in [Field](../Field/Field.md).

- Import: `import { Switch } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Switch/Switch.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Switch`): Default, On, WithDescription, LabelAtEnd, Disabled, ReadOnly, Required, Invalid, LongLabel, WithoutVisibleLabel

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Secondary text under the label. Linked with `aria-describedby`, not part of the name. |
| `errorMessage` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  | Error text, shown while the switch is invalid and the error is displayed. |
| `labelPlacement` | `'start' \| 'end'` |  | `'start'` | Where the label sits relative to the track. `start` (default): text on the leading side, track on the trailing side, spread across the row, the settings-list layout. `end`: track first. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the field root. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ requiredMark: string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`). |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the field root `<div>`. Use `inputRef` for the `<input>`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `AriaSwitchProps` (react-aria): `aria-controls`
- From `AriaValidationProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-errormessage`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `FocusableDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `excludeFromTabOrder`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `InputBase` (@react-types/shared): `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`
- From `InputDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `form`, `name`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `PressEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onClick`, `onPress`, `onPressChange`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressStart`, `onPressUp`
- From `RACValidation` (react-aria-components): `validationBehavior`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- From `SwitchFieldProps` (react-aria-components): `inputRef`
- From `ToggleProps` (react-stately): `value`
- From `ToggleStateOptions` (react-stately): `defaultSelected`, `isSelected`, `onChange`
- From `Validation` (@react-types/shared): `isInvalid`, `isRequired`, `validate`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-switch-knob-offset`, `--ds-switch-knob-size`, `--ds-switch-track-height`, `--ds-switch-track-width`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-3`

#### When to use

- Settings that apply as soon as they change ("Email notifications"), with the state obvious from the label.

#### When not to use

- Choices confirmed later with a Save button or submitted as an agreement: `Checkbox`.
- One of several options: `RadioGroup`.

#### Props (key ones)

| Prop                                                                  | Notes                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                                                               | Visible label. Without it pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (renders only the track).                          |
| `description`                                                         | Secondary text under the label, linked by `aria-describedby`, not part of the name.                                 |
| `labelPlacement`                                                      | `start` (default): text on the leading side, track on the trailing side, spread across the row. `end`: track first. |
| `isSelected` / `defaultSelected` / `onChange(isSelected)`             | React Aria naming.                                                                                                  |
| `name`, `value`                                                       | Submitted with the form while on (`value` defaults to `on`).                                                        |
| `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `errorMessage` | Standard states.                                                                                                    |
| `inputRef` / `ref`                                                    | `inputRef` is the `<input>`, `ref` the field root.                                                                  |

#### Look

- Off: track in `--ds-line-control` (3:1 or better against the page, also on hover); on: `--ds-accent`. The knob uses `--ds-text` and moves with `inset-inline-start`, so it mirrors in right-to-left.
- Sizes come from component tokens: `--ds-switch-track-width`, `--ds-switch-track-height`, `--ds-switch-knob-size`, `--ds-switch-knob-offset`.
- The row is at least as tall as the track and the whole row is the click target, with one toggle per click.
- Reduced motion: transitions are removed by the base layer.
- Forced colors: the track gets a system border and a `Highlight` fill when on; the knob uses `CanvasText`.

#### Accessibility

- `Space` toggles the focused switch. `Enter` does not toggle (it submits the form, as for any native checkbox).
- Announced as "switch, on/off", named by the label only; the description is `aria-describedby`.
- State is conveyed by position and by color, and by the announced state.

#### Example

```tsx
<Switch label="Email notifications" description="A summary every morning." defaultSelected />
<Switch label="Dark mode" labelPlacement="end" name="theme" value="dark" />
<Switch aria-label="Enable sync" />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Checkbox: Choices confirmed later with a Save button or submitted as an agreement: `Checkbox`.
- Instead, see RadioGroup: One of several options: `RadioGroup`.
- Renders: FieldMessages, RequiredMark

### Tab

> One tab of a `TabList`, with an optional count and shortcut hint.

Tabs switch between panels of related content on the same page. Built on React Aria `Tabs`, `TabList`, `Tab` and `TabPanel`: one tab stop, arrow keys between tabs, panels linked to their tabs.

- Handoff source: `components/navigation/Tabs.jsx` (TODO `CMP-NAV-01`).

- Import: `import { Tab } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Tabs/Tabs.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Tabs`): Default, ArrowKeys, FocusMovesIntoPanel, ManualActivation, Counts, ShortcutHints, DisabledTab, Controlled, LongLabels, RightToLeft, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Tab label: a noun in sentence case ("Orders"). |
| `count` | `string \| number` |  |  | A count shown after the label. Numbers are formatted for the active locale. The count is part of the tab's accessible name, so pair it with `countLabel` when the bare number is ambiguous. |
| `countLabel` | `string` |  |  | Accessible text for the count ("3 pending"). When set, it replaces the visible count in the accessible name. Recommended whenever `countTone` is not `neutral`. |
| `countTone` | `'neutral' \| 'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | `'neutral'` | Tone of the count. `neutral` (default) is plain mono text; the other tones draw a soft pill. Color never carries the meaning alone: use `countLabel` to say what the count means. |
| `shortcut` | `readonly string[]` |  |  | Keys of a shortcut hint shown after the label, as for `Kbd` (`['1']`, `['Mod', 'K']`). Decorative: hidden from assistive technology, and it registers nothing. Register the shortcut itself with `useHotkey`. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the tab element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `HoverEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onHoverChange`, `onHoverEnd`, `onHoverStart`
- From `LinkDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `download`, `href`, `hrefLang`, `ping`, `referrerPolicy`, `rel`, `routerOptions`, `target`
- From `PressEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onClick`, `onPress`, `onPressChange`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressStart`, `onPressUp`
- From `TabProps` (react-aria-components): `id`, `isDisabled`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-accent-soft`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-danger-soft`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-success-soft`, `--ds-tabs-count-padding-inline`, `--ds-tabs-count-size`, `--ds-tabs-gap`, `--ds-tabs-indicator-height`, `--ds-target-min`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-warning-soft`, `--ds-weight-medium`, `--ds-weight-regular`

#### When to use

- Several views of the same object (Details, Items, History) where only one is shown at a time.
- Filtering a list into a few named groups that each have their own panel.

#### When not to use

- To pick a value without panels (a view mode, a unit): use `SegmentedControl`.
- To move between pages or routes: use `NavItem` in a navigation list, or `Link`s. (`Tab` does accept `href`, but a primary navigation is not a tab list.)
- For more than about seven tabs, or for steps of a process.

#### Anatomy

```
Tabs                         (root, flex column)
  TabList  aria-label        (role=tablist, 1px bottom line)
    Tab id                   (role=tab; 2px ink underline when selected)
      label
      count                  (optional; neutral text or a toned pill)
      shortcut hint          (optional Kbd, aria-hidden)
  TabPanel id                (role=tabpanel, labelled by its tab)
```

#### Accessibility

- Roles: `tablist` > `tab` (with `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`) and `tabpanel` (`aria-labelledby` the tab).
- Keyboard: `Tab` enters the list once (roving tab stop) and the next `Tab` goes to the panel; `←` / `→` move (and wrap), `Home` / `End` jump. In right-to-left locales the arrows swap. Disabled tabs are skipped.
- Activation: automatic by default. Use `keyboardActivation="manual"` when showing a panel is slow or has side effects, so arrowing across tabs does not trigger work.
- Count: the visible count is part of the tab name ("Orders 12"). With `countLabel` the visible number is hidden from assistive technology and the label is read instead ("Pending 3 pending"). Color never carries the meaning, so a toned count always needs words.
- Shortcut hint: decorative; it does not change the name. Tell users about the shortcut elsewhere (help, tooltip) if it matters.
- Contrast: inactive tab text is `--ds-text-3` on `--ds-bg` (passes). Do not place tabs on a raised or hover surface without checking.
- Focus: accent ring on the tab and on a focused panel. Forced colors: the selected underline uses `Highlight`.
- Reduced motion: only a color transition, neutralized by the base styles.

#### Content rules

- Labels are nouns in sentence case ("Order items"), one or two words.
- Do not repeat the count in the label. `countLabel` says what the number counts ("3 pending").

#### Examples

```tsx
<Tabs defaultSelectedKey="items">
  <TabList aria-label="Order sections">
    <Tab id="details">Details</Tab>
    <Tab id="items" count={12} countTone="warning" countLabel="12 pending">
      Items
    </Tab>
    <Tab id="history" shortcut={['3']}>
      History
    </Tab>
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel id="details">…</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel id="items">…</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel id="history">…</TabPanel>
</Tabs>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see SegmentedControl: To pick a value without panels (a view mode, a unit): use `SegmentedControl`.
- Instead, see NavItem: To move between pages or routes: use `NavItem` in a navigation list, or `Link`s. (`Tab` does accept `href`, but a primary navigation is not a tab list.)
- Instead, see Link: To move between pages or routes: use `NavItem` in a navigation list, or `Link`s. (`Tab` does accept `href`, but a primary navigation is not a tab list.)
- Renders: Kbd, VisuallyHidden

### TabList

> The row of tabs. Name it with `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) so screen readers can
tell several tab lists apart.

Tabs switch between panels of related content on the same page. Built on React Aria `Tabs`, `TabList`, `Tab` and `TabPanel`: one tab stop, arrow keys between tabs, panels linked to their tabs.


#### Related components

- Instead, see SegmentedControl: To pick a value without panels (a view mode, a unit): use `SegmentedControl`.
- Instead, see NavItem: To move between pages or routes: use `NavItem` in a navigation list, or `Link`s. (`Tab` does accept `href`, but a primary navigation is not a tab list.)
- Instead, see Link: To move between pages or routes: use `NavItem` in a navigation list, or `Link`s. (`Tab` does accept `href`, but a primary navigation is not a tab list.)
- Instead, see Tab: To move between pages or routes: use `NavItem` in a navigation list, or `Link`s. (`Tab` does accept `href`, but a primary navigation is not a tab list.)
- Renders: Kbd, VisuallyHidden

### TabPanel

> The content of one tab. `id` must equal the `id` of its `Tab`; the panel is then labelled by
the tab and the tab points to the panel (`aria-controls`). The panel is focusable when it
has no focusable content, so keyboard users can reach it.

Tabs switch between panels of related content on the same page. Built on React Aria `Tabs`, `TabList`, `Tab` and `TabPanel`: one tab stop, arrow keys between tabs, panels linked to their tabs.

- Handoff source: `components/navigation/Tabs.jsx` (TODO `CMP-NAV-01`).

- Import: `import { TabPanel } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Tabs/Tabs.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Tabs`): Default, ArrowKeys, FocusMovesIntoPanel, ManualActivation, Counts, ShortcutHints, DisabledTab, Controlled, LongLabels, RightToLeft, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Panel content. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the `tabpanel` element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`
- From `AriaTabPanelProps` (react-aria): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `TabPanelProps` (react-aria-components): `shouldForceMount`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-accent-soft`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-danger-soft`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-success-soft`, `--ds-tabs-count-padding-inline`, `--ds-tabs-count-size`, `--ds-tabs-gap`, `--ds-tabs-indicator-height`, `--ds-target-min`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-warning-soft`, `--ds-weight-medium`, `--ds-weight-regular`

#### When to use

- Several views of the same object (Details, Items, History) where only one is shown at a time.
- Filtering a list into a few named groups that each have their own panel.

#### When not to use

- To pick a value without panels (a view mode, a unit): use `SegmentedControl`.
- To move between pages or routes: use `NavItem` in a navigation list, or `Link`s. (`Tab` does accept `href`, but a primary navigation is not a tab list.)
- For more than about seven tabs, or for steps of a process.

#### Anatomy

```
Tabs                         (root, flex column)
  TabList  aria-label        (role=tablist, 1px bottom line)
    Tab id                   (role=tab; 2px ink underline when selected)
      label
      count                  (optional; neutral text or a toned pill)
      shortcut hint          (optional Kbd, aria-hidden)
  TabPanel id                (role=tabpanel, labelled by its tab)
```

#### Accessibility

- Roles: `tablist` > `tab` (with `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`) and `tabpanel` (`aria-labelledby` the tab).
- Keyboard: `Tab` enters the list once (roving tab stop) and the next `Tab` goes to the panel; `←` / `→` move (and wrap), `Home` / `End` jump. In right-to-left locales the arrows swap. Disabled tabs are skipped.
- Activation: automatic by default. Use `keyboardActivation="manual"` when showing a panel is slow or has side effects, so arrowing across tabs does not trigger work.
- Count: the visible count is part of the tab name ("Orders 12"). With `countLabel` the visible number is hidden from assistive technology and the label is read instead ("Pending 3 pending"). Color never carries the meaning, so a toned count always needs words.
- Shortcut hint: decorative; it does not change the name. Tell users about the shortcut elsewhere (help, tooltip) if it matters.
- Contrast: inactive tab text is `--ds-text-3` on `--ds-bg` (passes). Do not place tabs on a raised or hover surface without checking.
- Focus: accent ring on the tab and on a focused panel. Forced colors: the selected underline uses `Highlight`.
- Reduced motion: only a color transition, neutralized by the base styles.

#### Content rules

- Labels are nouns in sentence case ("Order items"), one or two words.
- Do not repeat the count in the label. `countLabel` says what the number counts ("3 pending").

#### Examples

```tsx
<Tabs defaultSelectedKey="items">
  <TabList aria-label="Order sections">
    <Tab id="details">Details</Tab>
    <Tab id="items" count={12} countTone="warning" countLabel="12 pending">
      Items
    </Tab>
    <Tab id="history" shortcut={['3']}>
      History
    </Tab>
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel id="details">…</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel id="items">…</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel id="history">…</TabPanel>
</Tabs>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see SegmentedControl: To pick a value without panels (a view mode, a unit): use `SegmentedControl`.
- Instead, see NavItem: To move between pages or routes: use `NavItem` in a navigation list, or `Link`s. (`Tab` does accept `href`, but a primary navigation is not a tab list.)
- Instead, see Link: To move between pages or routes: use `NavItem` in a navigation list, or `Link`s. (`Tab` does accept `href`, but a primary navigation is not a tab list.)
- Instead, see Tab: To move between pages or routes: use `NavItem` in a navigation list, or `Link`s. (`Tab` does accept `href`, but a primary navigation is not a tab list.)
- Renders: Kbd, VisuallyHidden

### Tabs

> Tabs switch between panels of related content. Built on React Aria `Tabs`: one tab stop,
`Left` / `Right` / `Home` / `End` move between tabs, `Tab` moves into the panel.

Selection follows RAC: `selectedKey` / `defaultSelectedKey` / `onSelectionChange`.
`keyboardActivation="manual"` makes the arrow keys only move focus; `Enter` or `Space`
then activates the tab (use it when showing a panel is slow or has side effects).

### Tag

> A mono outlined label for versions, SKUs and filters. Standalone it is static text (with an
optional remove button); inside a `TagGroup` it is a keyboard-navigable item that can be
removed with Backspace or Delete.

A mono outlined label for versions, SKUs and filters. `Tag` is static text on its own (with an optional remove button); inside a `TagGroup` it is an item with keyboard navigation, selection and removal. `TagGroup` is built on React Aria `TagGroup`, `TagList` and `Tag`.

- Import: `import { Tag } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Tag/Tag.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Tag`): Default, Removable, Disabled, LongText, RightToLeft, RemovableGroupStory, GroupStatic, GroupSelectable, GroupWithDisabledTag, GroupEmpty

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The text of the tag. Plain text, or any node together with `textValue`. |
| `textValue` | `string` |  |  | Plain-text version of the tag. Required when `children` is not a string: it names the tag for screen readers and is used in the name of the remove button ("Remove {textValue}"). |
| `id` | `Key` |  |  | Inside a `TagGroup`: the key of the tag (used by `onRemove`, selection and `disabledKeys`). Outside a group: the DOM `id`. |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean` |  |  | Disables the tag (inside a group: keyboard removal and selection too). |
| `onRemove` | `() => void` |  |  | Standalone tag only: shows a remove button that calls this. Inside a `TagGroup` use the group's `onRemove` instead (it also enables Backspace and Delete on the focused tag). |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ remove: (label: string) => string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Tag: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remove(label: string)` | `Remove {label}` | Name of the remove button of a tag: it includes the text of the tag. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-accent-soft`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-tag-height`, `--ds-tag-padding-inline`, `--ds-tag-remove-size`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- Show an attribute or identifier: `v2.4.0`, `ORD-1048`, `notebook`.
- Show applied filters that the user can remove (`TagGroup` with `onRemove`).
- Let the user toggle filters (`TagGroup` with `selectionMode`).

#### When not to use

- For a status (Shipped, Failed): use `Badge`.
- For a command: use `Button`.
- For choosing one option from a list: use `Select` or `RadioGroup`.

#### Anatomy

```
TagGroup           (grid; optional visible label)
  Label
  TagList          (flex wrap)
    Tag            (row)
      text
      remove button  only when the group has onRemove (24x24 target)
```

#### Accessibility

- A group is a `grid` with one `row` per tag. Arrow keys move between tags (roving focus); the focused tag is the only one in the tab order.
- **Backspace and Delete remove the focused tag** (or all selected tags) when the group has `onRemove`. Keyboard users are told so by a description that React Aria adds to the focused tag.
- **The remove button is named "Remove {text}"** from the message catalog (pt-BR: "Remover {text}"), not just "Remove". The button is also a tab stop after its tag, and is a 24 by 24 pixel target (WCAG 2.5.8).
- After a removal, focus moves to a neighbouring tag (React Aria); handle the empty state with `renderEmptyState` and move focus to something sensible yourself if the whole group disappears.
- Selection is exposed as `aria-selected`, and shown with the accent border and tint (a permitted use of the accent). Selection is never signalled by color alone: the state is announced.
- A standalone `Tag` is plain text. With `onRemove` it contains a real `<button>` (Enter or Space); Backspace and Delete do nothing there because the tag itself is not focusable. Use a `TagGroup` when keyboard removal matters.
- Text is `--ds-text-2` on the page surface; disabled tags are exempt from contrast and carry `aria-disabled`.

#### Content rules

- Short, lowercase or code-like values are fine (`v2.4.0`, `ORD-1048`); filters use the user's own words.
- Write a `textValue` that reads well after "Remove": "Remove notebook".

#### Examples

```tsx
<Tag>v2.4.0</Tag>

<TagGroup label="Product" onRemove={(keys) => setTags((t) => t.filter((x) => !keys.has(x)))}>
  {tags.map((tag) => <Tag key={tag} id={tag}>{tag}</Tag>)}
</TagGroup>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Badge: For a status (Shipped, Failed): use `Badge`.
- Instead, see Button: For a command: use `Button`.
- Instead, see Select: For choosing one option from a list: use `Select` or `RadioGroup`.
- Instead, see RadioGroup: For choosing one option from a list: use `Select` or `RadioGroup`.
- Renders: Icon
- Used by: TagInput

### TagGroup

> A group of tags with one tab stop and arrow-key navigation. With `onRemove`, Backspace and
Delete remove the focused tag (or the selected tags) and every tag gets a remove button.
Built on React Aria `TagGroup`.

A mono outlined label for versions, SKUs and filters. `Tag` is static text on its own (with an optional remove button); inside a `TagGroup` it is an item with keyboard navigation, selection and removal. `TagGroup` is built on React Aria `TagGroup`, `TagList` and `Tag`.

- Import: `import { TagGroup } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Tag/Tag.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Tag`): Default, Removable, Disabled, LongText, RightToLeft, RemovableGroupStory, GroupStatic, GroupSelectable, GroupWithDisabledTag, GroupEmpty

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| ((item: T) => ReactNode)` | yes |  | Static `Tag` children, or a render function when `items` is given. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label of the group. Without it, give the group an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. |
| `onRemove` | `(keys: Set<Key>) => void` |  |  | Called with the keys of the tags to remove (Backspace, Delete or the remove button). Makes the tags removable. |
| `items` | `Iterable<T>` |  |  | Data for the render function. Each item needs an `id` (or pass `id` to the rendered `Tag`). |
| `renderEmptyState` | `() => ReactNode` |  |  | Content shown when there are no tags (for example "No filters applied"). |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |

- From `MultipleSelection` (@react-types/shared): `defaultSelectedKeys`, `disallowEmptySelection`, `onSelectionChange`, `selectedKeys`, `selectionMode`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-accent-soft`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-tag-height`, `--ds-tag-padding-inline`, `--ds-tag-remove-size`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`

### TagInput

> A text field that turns what you type into removable tags: `Enter` or a comma adds the
tag, pasting `a, b, c` adds three, `Backspace` on the empty input removes the last one.
Duplicates are ignored with a polite message; `maxTags` and `validateTag` reject with an
error that is read aloud.

Built from `TagGroup` / `Tag` and React Aria `TextField`. The tags are a keyboard-navigable
list (one tab stop; `Shift+Tab` from the input reaches it, `Backspace` or `Delete` on a tag
removes it), the input is a normal text box. The value is the list of tags; with `name` each
tag is submitted as a hidden field.

For choosing from known options use `Combobox`; for filters that are always visible use
`ToggleGroup`.

A text field that turns what you type into removable tags: `Enter` or a comma adds a tag, pasting `a, b, c` adds three, `Backspace` on the empty input removes the last one. Built from `TagGroup` / `Tag` and React Aria `TextField`. The value is the list of tags; with `name` each tag is submitted as a hidden form field.

- TODO `GAP-005`.

- Import: `import { TagInput } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/TagInput/TagInput.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/TagInput`): Default, AddWithKeyboard, WithTags, BackspaceRemovesLast, RemoveWithKeyboard, Duplicate, MaxTags, Validation, Invalid, Required, Disabled, ReadOnly, Small, Large, ManyTagsWrap, LongTag, SemicolonDelimiter, Controlled, InForm, Portuguese, RightToLeft, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `readonly string[]` |  |  | The tags (controlled). Pair with `onChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `readonly string[]` |  |  | The initial tags (uncontrolled). |
| `onChange` | `((tags: string[]) => void)` |  |  | Called with the full list of tags whenever a tag is added or removed. |
| `name` | `string` |  |  | Name used to submit the tags with a form. Each tag is submitted as its own hidden field with this name (read them with `formData.getAll(name)`). The text being typed is never submitted. |
| `form` | `string` |  |  | The `id` of the `<form>` the hidden fields belong to, when the field is outside it. |
| `inputValue` | `string` |  |  | The text in the input, not yet a tag (controlled). Pair with `onInputChange`. |
| `defaultInputValue` | `string` |  |  | The initial text in the input (uncontrolled). |
| `onInputChange` | `((text: string) => void)` |  |  | Called with the text of the input as the user types. |
| `delimiters` | `readonly string[]` |  | `[',']` | Characters that end a tag while typing and split pasted text. `Enter` always adds the tag, and line breaks always split pasted text. Default `[',']`. Pass `[]` to use only `Enter`. |
| `maxTags` | `number` |  |  | Maximum number of tags. Trying to add another shows an error and keeps the text. |
| `validateTag` | `((tag: string) => string \| null)` |  |  | Decides whether a tag may be added. Return a message to reject it ("Use letters and digits only."); return nothing to accept it. The message is shown as the field error and read aloud. It receives the trimmed text. |
| `caseSensitive` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Treat "Notebook" and "notebook" as different tags. Default: they are the same, and the second is ignored. |
| `addOnBlur` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Turns the text left in the input into a tag when the input loses focus. Default `true`. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Helper text under the control. Linked with `aria-describedby`. |
| `errorMessage` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  | Error text from your own validation, shown while the field is invalid (`isInvalid`). The messages of `validateTag` and `maxTags` take its place while they apply. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  | Text shown while the field has no tags and no text. Never a substitute for the label. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | Control height: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px. The box grows when tags wrap. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the field root. |
| `inputClassName` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the text `<input>`. |
| `inputRef` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` |  |  | Ref to the text `<input>`. The `ref` prop points at the field root. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ tagsLabel: (fieldLabel?: string) => string; added: (tag: string) => string; addedMany: (count: number) => string; removed: (tag: string) => string; duplicate: (tag: string) => string; duplicates: (count: number) => string; maxReached: (max: number) => string; } & { ...; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance: `tagsLabel`, `added`, `addedMany`, `removed`, `duplicate`, `duplicates`, `maxReached`, `requiredMark`. The remove button of a tag uses the `Tag` messages. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the field root `<div>`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `AriaTextFieldProps` (react-aria): `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-autocomplete`, `aria-controls`, `aria-haspopup`, `enterKeyHint`
- From `AriaValidationProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-errormessage`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `FocusableDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `excludeFromTabOrder`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `InputBase` (@react-types/shared): `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `RACValidation` (react-aria-components): `validationBehavior`
- From `TextFieldProps` (react-aria-components): `isInvalid`
