- From `TextInputDOMEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBeforeInput`, `onCompositionEnd`, `onCompositionStart`, `onCompositionUpdate`, `onCopy`, `onCut`, `onInput`, `onPaste`, `onSelect`
- From `TextInputDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoComplete`, `autoCorrect`, `spellCheck`
- From `Validation` (@react-types/shared): `isRequired`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ TagInput: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tagsLabel(fieldLabel?: string)` | `{fieldLabel?}, added tags` | Name of the list of added tags. `fieldLabel` is the text label of the field, when it has one. |
| `added(tag: string)` | `Added “{tag}”.` | Announced (polite) after one tag is added. |
| `addedMany(count: number)` | `Added 2 tags.` | Announced (polite) after several tags are added at once (paste). |
| `removed(tag: string)` | `Removed “{tag}”.` | Announced (polite) after a tag is removed with Backspace on the empty input. |
| `duplicate(tag: string)` | `“{tag}” is already added.` | Shown and announced (polite) when a typed tag is already in the list and was ignored. |
| `duplicates(count: number)` | `2 duplicate tags were skipped.` | Shown and announced (polite) when several pasted tags were ignored as duplicates. |
| `maxReached(max: number)` | `You can add up to 2 tags.` | Error shown when the user tries to add a tag beyond the maximum. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-tag-height`, `--ds-tag-input-gap`, `--ds-tag-input-input-min-width`, `--ds-tag-input-padding-block`, `--ds-tag-input-padding-inline`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`

#### When to use

- Free-form lists the user types: keywords, e-mail recipients, labels, SKUs.
- When the list can grow beyond what you want to show as checkboxes.

#### When not to use

- Choosing from known options: use `Combobox` (or `Select`).
- A fixed set of filters that are always visible: use `ToggleGroup`.
- Showing tags the user cannot edit: use `TagGroup`.

#### Anatomy

```
div (field root)
  Label
  div.control                     (the bordered box, wraps over several rows)
    TagGroup[role=grid] aria-label    (only while there are tags; one row per tag)
      Tag > text + remove button (24x24)
    input[type=text]              (the textbox; named by the Label)
  Description
  FieldError                      (role=alert: validation and maximum)
  div[role=status]                (polite: added, removed, duplicate; visible for a duplicate)
  input[type=hidden] x N          (only with `name`)
```

#### Behavior

| Input                                        | Result                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter` with text                            | Adds the tag (trimmed), clears the input. Does not submit the form. `Enter` on an empty input submits as usual. |
| A delimiter key (`,`)                        | Same as `Enter`; the character is never typed.                                                                  |
| Paste with delimiters or line breaks         | Adds every piece. Duplicates are skipped; a message counts them. A paste without delimiters is a normal paste.  |
| `Backspace` on an empty input                | Removes the last tag (announced: "Removed “headphones”.").                                                      |
| Duplicate                                    | Ignored, input cleared, polite message "“notebook” is already added." Not an error.                             |
| Beyond `maxTags` / rejected by `validateTag` | Error (`role="alert"`, field invalid), nothing is added, the text stays so it can be fixed.                     |
| Blur with text                               | Adds it (`addOnBlur`).                                                                                          |

#### Accessibility

- The input is a normal `textbox` named by the label. The tags are a `grid` named "Products, added tags" with one `row` per tag (React Aria `TagGroup`): `Shift+Tab` from the input reaches the tags; a row, then its remove button, are tab stops; `←` / `→` move between tags; `Backspace` or `Delete` on a focused tag removes it. After the last tag is removed focus returns to the input.
- Remove buttons are 24x24 and named "Remove notebook" (message `Tag.remove`).
- Additions, removals and duplicates are announced in one polite `role="status"` region; errors are in the field's `role="alert"` message, linked with `aria-describedby`. Only duplicates are also shown as text below the box, so the notice is not color-only; the error is text and the box border turns danger.
- The click target of the whole box focuses the input.
- Contrast: the box border is `--ds-line-control` (3:1) in every state, as in the other fields.

#### Content rules

- Label as a noun phrase ("Products", "Recipients"). Placeholder: an example or an action ("Add a product"), never the label.
- `validateTag` messages say how to fix it: "Enter a complete email address."
- Tags are shown as typed (trimmed); sorting is up to you.

#### Messages (`messages` prop, or `DSProvider messages={{ TagInput: … }}`)

`tagsLabel(fieldLabel?)`, `added(tag)`, `addedMany(count)`, `removed(tag)`, `duplicate(tag)`, `duplicates(count)`, `maxReached(max)`, `requiredMark`. English and `pt-BR` ship with the library. The remove button uses the `Tag` messages.

#### Examples

```tsx
<TagInput label="Products" name="products" value={products} onChange={setProducts} maxTags={10} />

<TagInput
  label="Recipients"
  delimiters={[',', ';']}
  validateTag={(tag) => (tag.includes('@') ? undefined : 'Enter a complete email address.')}
/>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Combobox: Choosing from known options: use `Combobox` (or `Select`).
- Instead, see Select: Choosing from known options: use `Combobox` (or `Select`).
- Instead, see ToggleGroup: A fixed set of filters that are always visible: use `ToggleGroup`.
- Instead, see TagGroup: Showing tags the user cannot edit: use `TagGroup`.
- Renders: FieldMessages, Label, Tag, TagGroup

### Text

> Body text on the type scale. It sets size, line height, color tone and an optional mono
face; the element (`as`) carries the meaning. Use `Heading` for headings and `Code` for code.

Body text on the type scale, with a tone, an optional mono face and truncation.

- Import: `import { Text } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Text/Text.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Typography/Text`): Default, Small, Label, Meta_, Caption, Secondary, Tertiary, Mono, AsParagraph, Truncated, LongText, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `'body' \| 'caption' \| 'label' \| 'meta' \| 'small'` |  | `'body'` | Type scale step: `body` 15px, `small` 14px, `label` 13px, `meta` 12px, or `caption` 11.5px. `caption` is always Geist Mono, uppercase by CSS, with extra tracking: write the source text in sentence case. Default `body`. |
| `tone` | `'default' \| 'secondary' \| 'tertiary'` |  | `'default'` | Text color: `default` (`--ds-text`), `secondary` (`--ds-text-2`, supporting text) or `tertiary` (`--ds-text-3`, hints). Tertiary passes 4.5:1 on every surface, but signals the lowest importance: use it for meta and hints, never for primary content. Default `default`. |
| `mono` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Geist Mono with tabular figures, for codes, identifiers, amounts and shortcuts. |
| `truncate` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Keeps the text on one line and cuts it with an ellipsis. Put the full text in `title` or nearby for sighted users. |
| `as` | `'span' \| 'dd' \| 'div' \| 'dt' \| 'em' \| 'figcaption' \| 'label' \| 'legend' \| 'li' \| 'p' \| 'small' \| 'strong'` |  | `'span'` | Element to render. Default `span`, which is safe inside any inline context; use `p` for a paragraph. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `body`, `caption`, `label`, `meta`, `small`
- `tone`: `default`, `secondary`, `tertiary`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-body`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-body`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-meta`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-tracking-caption`, `--ds-weight-medium`, `--ds-weight-regular`

#### When to use

- Paragraphs, supporting lines, labels, counts, metadata and small captions.
- Anywhere a size from the type scale or a secondary tone is needed on plain text.

#### When not to use

- Headings: use `Heading`.
- Code: use `Code`.
- Links: use `Link`. Field labels: use the `Label` of the field.

#### Anatomy

```
span (or the element in `as`)
```

#### Accessibility

- `tertiary` passes 4.5:1 on every surface (TOK-004), but it carries the lowest importance: use it for hints and meta, never for primary content.
- Truncated text hides content visually: show the full value elsewhere (a `title`, a tooltip, a detail view) when it matters.
- The caption's uppercase is CSS only, so screen readers read the sentence-case source.
- Long unbroken values wrap (`overflow-wrap: break-word`).

#### Content rules

- Sentence case. Numbers, codes and amounts go in `mono`, formatted with `Intl` (see `utils`).

#### Examples

```tsx
<Text as="p">Your order has shipped.</Text>
<Text size="small" tone="secondary">Updated 2 minutes ago</Text>
<Text size="caption" tone="secondary">Shipping</Text>
<Text mono>ORD-1048</Text>
<Text truncate>{longFileName}</Text>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Heading: Headings: use `Heading`.
- Instead, see Code: Code: use `Code`.
- Instead, see Link: Links: use `Link`. Field labels: use the `Label` of the field.
- Instead, see Label: Links: use `Link`. Field labels: use the `Label` of the field.

### Textarea

> Multi-line text field built on React Aria `TextField` + `TextArea`. Same contract as `Input`.

Multi-line text field. Same contract as [Input](../Input/Input.md) (label, description, error, states, validation timing from [Field](../Field/Field.md)), plus an aside, auto-growing height and a character count. Built on React Aria `TextField` + `TextArea`.

- Import: `import { Textarea } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Textarea/Textarea.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Textarea`): Default, WithDescription, WithAside, Required, Invalid, Disabled, ReadOnly, AutoGrow, WithCharacterCount, NoResize, LongLabel, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Helper text under the control. Linked with `aria-describedby`. |
| `errorMessage` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  | Error text, shown while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. See `Input`. |
| `aside` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Text on the label line, aligned to the end (for example "Optional" or "Markdown supported"). It is part of the field's description for assistive technology, not of its name. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  | Text shown while the field is empty. Never a substitute for the label. |
| `rows` | `number` |  | `3` | Visible lines before the user types. Default 3. |
| `resize` | `'none' \| 'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both'` |  | `'vertical'` | Whether the user can drag the corner to resize. Default `vertical`. Ignored with `autoGrow`. |
| `autoGrow` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Grows with its content instead of scrolling. |
| `showCount` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Shows "used / max" on the label line and announces the remaining characters politely once typing pauses. Needs `maxLength`. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the field root. |
| `textareaClassName` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the `<textarea>` element. |
| `textareaRef` | `Ref<HTMLTextAreaElement>` |  |  | Ref to the `<textarea>` element. The `ref` prop points at the field root. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ count: (used: string, max: string) => string; remaining: (n: number) => string; over: (n: number) => string; } & { requiredMark: string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance: `count`, `remaining`, `over`, `requiredMark`. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the field root `<div>`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `AriaTextFieldProps` (react-aria): `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-autocomplete`, `aria-controls`, `aria-haspopup`, `enterKeyHint`
- From `AriaValidationProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-errormessage`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `FocusableDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `excludeFromTabOrder`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `InputBase` (@react-types/shared): `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`
- From `InputDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `form`, `name`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `RACValidation` (react-aria-components): `validationBehavior`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- From `TextFieldProps` (react-aria-components): `isInvalid`
- From `TextInputDOMEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBeforeInput`, `onCompositionEnd`, `onCompositionStart`, `onCompositionUpdate`, `onCopy`, `onCut`, `onInput`, `onPaste`, `onSelect`
- From `TextInputDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoComplete`, `autoCorrect`, `maxLength`, `minLength`, `pattern`, `spellCheck`
- From `Validation` (@react-types/shared): `isRequired`, `validate`
- From `ValueBase` (@react-types/shared): `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `value`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Textarea: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count(used: string, max: string)` | `{used} / {max}` | Visible counter next to the label, for example "12 / 200". Arguments are already formatted. |
| `remaining(n: number)` | `2 characters remaining` | Polite announcement, made once typing pauses. |
| `over(n: number)` | `2 characters over the limit` | Announcement when a controlled value exceeds `maxLength`. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-danger`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-lh-meta`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-textarea-padding-block`, `--ds-textarea-padding-inline`

#### When to use

- Notes, comments, descriptions, messages longer than a line.

#### When not to use

- One line of text: `Input`.
- Rich text or Markdown editing: a dedicated editor.

#### Props (key ones)

| Prop                                         | Notes                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label`, `description`, `errorMessage`       | As in `Input`.                                                                                                           |
| `aside`                                      | Text on the label line, aligned to the end ("Optional", "Markdown supported"). Part of the description, not of the name. |
| `rows`                                       | Visible lines. Default 3.                                                                                                |
| `resize`                                     | `none`, `vertical` (default), `horizontal`, `both`.                                                                      |
| `autoGrow`                                   | Grows with its content; the manual resize handle is off.                                                                 |
| `maxLength` + `showCount`                    | Shows "used / max" on the label line and announces the remaining characters politely.                                    |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)` | React Aria naming; `onChange` receives the string.                                                                       |
| `textareaRef` / `ref`                        | `textareaRef` is the `<textarea>`, `ref` the field root.                                                                 |
| `messages`                                   | `count`, `remaining`, `over`, `requiredMark`.                                                                            |

#### Character count

- The visible counter ("12 / 200", formatted for the locale) is `aria-hidden`: announcing it on every keystroke would drown the user.
- A separate visually hidden `role="status"` (polite) region announces "N characters remaining" once typing has paused for one second. It stays silent until the value changes, and says "N characters over the limit" when a controlled value exceeds `maxLength`.
- Plural forms and the pt-BR text come from `Textarea.messages.ts`. Override `count`, `remaining` and `over` per instance or via `DSProvider messages={{ Textarea: { ... } }}`.
- `showCount` has no effect without `maxLength`. The native `maxLength` stops typing at the limit.

#### Accessibility

- Native `<textarea>` named by its label; `aside` and `description` are in `aria-describedby` (description first, then aside).
- Keyboard: standard text editing; `Enter` inserts a newline; `Tab` leaves the field.
- Auto-grow keeps all content visible (no inner scrollbar), which helps zoom and reflow.

#### Example

```tsx
<Textarea label="Notes" aside="Optional" description="Plain text only." maxLength={500} showCount />
<Textarea label="Message" autoGrow rows={2} isRequired errorMessage="Write a message." />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Input: One line of text: `Input`.
- Renders: FieldMessages, Label, VisuallyHidden
- Used by: ApprovalCard, ChatPanel

### Timeline

> A chronological list of events. It is an ordered list; each event has a `<time>`, a title, an
optional description, an optional actor and an optional tone marker. The marker and the line
are decorative: a tone is also stated as hidden text before the title.
Newest events come first by default, the order for dated records.

A chronological list of events: when it happened, what happened, who did it, and an optional detail and tone marker. It is a semantic ordered list, newest event first by default.

- Import: `import { Timeline } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Timeline/Timeline.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Timeline`): Default, OldestFirst, Tones, DateOnly, LongText, SingleEvent, Empty, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly TimelineItem[]` | yes |  | The events. |
| `order` | `'newest-first' \| 'oldest-first' \| 'as-given'` |  | `'newest-first'` | Order of the list: `newest-first` (default, for dated records), `oldest-first`, or `as-given` to keep the order of `items`. |
| `timeZone` | `string` |  |  | IANA time zone used to show date-times ("America/Sao_Paulo"). Defaults to the viewer's zone. |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Rendered instead of the list when `items` is empty (for example an `EmptyState`). |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ accent: string; success: string; warning: string; danger: string; actor: (actor: string) => string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Timeline: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accent` | `Highlighted` | Visually hidden prefix read before the title of an event with a tone; color and icon alone cannot carry it. |
| `success` | `Success` |  |
| `warning` | `Warning` |  |
| `danger` | `Error` |  |
| `actor(actor: string)` | `By {actor}` | Visible label before the person or system that caused the event. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-meta`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-timeline-connector-thickness`, `--ds-timeline-dot-size`, `--ds-timeline-item-gap`, `--ds-timeline-marker-gap`, `--ds-timeline-marker-size`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- The history of a record or a process: status changes, comments, deliveries, audit entries.
- Events that have a time and read as a story, a few lines each.

#### When not to use

- Tabular data that people sort and compare: use `DataTable`.
- The steps of a flow someone is going through now: use `Stepper`.
- The state of a record in a fixed flow: use `StatusSteps`.
- Totals and amounts per line: use `LedgerList`.

#### Anatomy

```
ol[aria-label]
  li[data-tone]
    marker (aria-hidden)         dot (neutral) | icon: accent info, success check, warning triangle, danger circle
    div
      title                      VisuallyHidden tone text ("Success") + title
      meta                       "By <actor>" · <time dateTime>
      description                optional
  connector line                 (CSS pseudo-element, decorative)
```

#### Accessibility

- A real ordered list; each time is a `<time dateTime>` with a machine-readable value, and its text comes from `Intl` for the active locale (never hand-built).
- The tone is not only color and icon: a visually hidden prefix ("Success", "Warning", "Error", "Highlighted", from messages) comes before the title. The marker and the line are `aria-hidden`.
- The list is not interactive, so it has no keyboard behavior of its own; put links or buttons in the `title` or `description` when an event needs an action.
- Text uses `text` and `text-2` (4.5:1 on the page surface). Forced colors: markers and line use system colors.
- Reflow: text wraps (long words break) and the layout is a single column, so it works at 320 px.

#### Content rules

- Title: what happened, past tense, sentence case, no exclamation marks ("Order shipped", "Request approved").
- Description: one short sentence of detail, only when it adds something.
- Actor: a person or system name. The component adds "By".
- Do not repeat the time in the title.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Timeline
  aria-label="Request history"
  items={[
    { id: 'a', time: '2026-10-28T09:15:00Z', title: 'Request created', actor: 'Ana Costa' },
    { id: 'b', time: '2026-10-31T16:05:00Z', title: 'Request approved', tone: 'success' },
  ]}
/>

<Timeline aria-label="Audit log" items={events} order="oldest-first" timeZone="UTC" />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see DataTable: Tabular data that people sort and compare: use `DataTable`.
- Instead, see Stepper: The steps of a flow someone is going through now: use `Stepper`.
- Instead, see StatusSteps: The state of a record in a fixed flow: use `StatusSteps`.
- Instead, see LedgerList: Totals and amounts per line: use `LedgerList`.
- Renders: Icon, VisuallyHidden

### ToastRegion

> Renders the toasts of a queue. Mount **one** near the app root, inside `DSProvider`, and call
`toast()` from anywhere. Built on React Aria's toast region (isolated in `toast.rac.ts`).

The region is a landmark named "Toast notifications" that `F6` moves into; the timer of every toast
pauses while the pointer is over the region or focus is inside it (WCAG 2.2.1). Toasts stack
at the bottom center of the viewport, clear of side panels, above dialogs and below tooltips.

A short, temporary message about something that just happened, with an optional action (usually Undo). Mount one `ToastRegion` and call `toast()` from anywhere. Built on React Aria's toast region and queue.

- Handoff source: `components/feedback/Toast` (CMP-FBK-02). Undo recipe: GAP-008 groundwork.

- Import: `import { ToastRegion } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Toast/Toast.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Toast`): AllTones, WithAction, LongMessage, UndoPattern, PausesOnHoverAndFocus, KeyboardRegion

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `queue` | `ToastQueue` |  | `createToastQueue()` | The queue to show. Defaults to the one `toast()` writes to. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ region: string; dismiss: string; info: string; success: string; warning: string; danger: string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the region. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the region element. |

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Toast: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `region` | `Toast notifications` | Accessible name of the region that holds the toasts (a landmark reachable with F6). |
| `dismiss` | `Dismiss notification` | Name of the dismiss button of a toast. |
| `info` | `Information` | Visually hidden prefix that tells screen reader users the kind of toast; the dot alone cannot. |
| `success` | `Success` |  |
| `warning` | `Warning` |  |
| `danger` | `Error` |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-toast-dot-size`, `--ds-toast-max-width`, `--ds-toast-min-height`, `--ds-toast-offset`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-z-toast`

#### When to use

- Feedback for an action that finished: "Order #1051 created", "3 items archived".
- Reversible actions, with **Undo**.

#### When not to use

- A state that stays on the page ("Scheduled maintenance"): use `Alert`.
- A field error: use the field's error message.
- Anything the user must read to proceed: use `Dialog` or `Alert`. A toast disappears.
- The only place an essential result is shown: toasts can be missed.

#### Anatomy

```
ToastRegion          role=region, aria-label "Toast notifications", landmark (F6); fixed, bottom center; z toast
  Toast              role=alertdialog (React Aria), raised surface, strong line, radius lg, overlay shadow
    dot              decorative, colored by tone
    message          "Success: " (visually hidden) + text
    Button           optional action ("Undo")
    IconButton       "Dismiss notification"
```

#### API

```tsx
// once, near the root, inside DSProvider
<ToastRegion />;

// anywhere
import { toast } from 'loui-ds';
toast('Draft saved'); // info
toast.success('Order #1051 created');
toast.warning('Stock is low for 2 items');
toast.danger('Payment failed', { timeout: null }); // stays until dismissed
toast.success('3 items archived', { action: { label: 'Undo', onPress: restore } });
```

| Option    | Type                                   | Default | Notes                                                   |
| --------- | -------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tone`    | `info \| success \| warning \| danger` | `info`  | Feedback components use `info`, not `neutral`/`accent`. |
| `action`  | `{ label, onPress }`                   |         | One action. The toast closes after `onPress`.           |
| `timeout` | `number \| null`                       | `5000`  | Milliseconds. `null` = until dismissed.                 |
| `onClose` | `() => void`                           |         | Timeout, dismiss or action.                             |

`toast(...)` returns a key; `toast.close(key)` and `toast.clear()` remove toasts. `useToast()` returns the same stable object. `createToastQueue()` / `createToastApi(queue)` and `<ToastRegion queue>` give an isolated queue (tests, a second region). `ToastRegion` also takes `messages` and `className`. At most four toasts show at once; the rest wait.

#### Default timeout: 5000 ms

The handoff closed toasts after 3.6 s, which is too short to read a sentence and reach Undo (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable). The default is 5 s **and** the timer pauses while the pointer is over the toast region or focus is inside it, so a keyboard or slow reader can always finish. Use `timeout: null` for failures the user has to act on.

#### Accessibility

- The region is a landmark named "Toast notifications". **F6** moves focus into it (and back), so Undo is keyboard reachable. React Aria registers a region as a landmark only if it is mounted with its first toast, so `ToastRegion` renders nothing while the queue is empty and mounts the region when a toast arrives.
- Each toast is announced by React Aria's toast semantics. The tone is spoken as a prefix ("Success: ...", "Error: ...") from messages; the colored dot is decorative and `aria-hidden`.
- Pause on hover and on focus within the region; the timer resumes on leave or blur.
- Dismiss button named from messages ("Dismiss notification"); action is a real `Button`.
- Layer `--ds-z-toast` (58): above dialogs, below tooltips. Bottom center keeps it clear of side panels (Sheet, Sidebar).
- Reduced motion: the 150 ms fade-in is removed. Forced colors: border and dot use `CanvasText`.
- `UNSTABLE_*` isolation: all React Aria `UNSTABLE_Toast*` imports live in `toast.rac.ts`. Renaming or stabilizing them is a one-file change.

#### Content rules

- Past tense, short, no exclamation marks: "Order #1051 created", "3 items archived".
- Action: a verb ("Undo"). No "Close" button text; the dismiss control is an icon.
- Do not repeat what is already visible on the page.

#### The undo pattern (recipe)

"Reversible actions never ask; they offer Undo" (AGENTS.md section 5). Do the action immediately, then toast with an Undo that reverses it:

```tsx
function archiveOrder(order: Order) {
  const previous = order.status;
  setStatus(order.id, 'archived'); // 1. do it now
  toast.success(`Order #${order.number} archived`, {
    // 2. say so, past tense
    action: {
      label: 'Undo',
      onPress: () => setStatus(order.id, previous), // 3. reverse it from the saved state
    },
  });
}
```

Rules:

1. Save what you need to reverse **before** acting; Undo must not depend on state that has moved on.
2. If the change was already sent to a server, Undo sends the inverse change; do not delay the real action to "wait for Undo".
3. For deletes, soft-delete or keep the record for the Undo window plus a margin, and keep the confirmation dialog (`ConfirmDialog`), then show the toast. For example: confirm, delete, toast "Order #1048 deleted" with Undo.
4. Irreversible actions get a `ConfirmDialog`, not a toast.
5. A hook (`useUndoable`) that wraps steps 1 to 3 is tracked as GAP-008.

#### Related components

- Instead, see Alert: A state that stays on the page ("Scheduled maintenance"): use `Alert`.
- Instead, see Dialog: Anything the user must read to proceed: use `Dialog` or `Alert`. A toast disappears.
- Renders: Button, IconButton, VisuallyHidden

### Toggle

> A button that stays pressed: it switches one setting on or off (bold text, a filter, "show
archived"). Built on React Aria `ToggleButton`: a native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`,
toggled by `Enter` and `Space`.

Use it for an independent on/off choice that applies at once. For a setting inside a form
use `Switch` or `Checkbox`; for several related toggles use `ToggleGroup`; for one value out
of a few use `SegmentedControl`.

A button that stays pressed: it switches one setting on or off (bold text, a filter, "show archived") and applies it at once. A native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`, built on React Aria `ToggleButton`. Looks like `Button` (`secondary` and `ghost`), with a clear pressed state.

- TODO `GAP-005`.

- Import: `import { Toggle } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Toggle/Toggle.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Toggle`): Default, Pressed, Ghost, GhostPressed, Small, Large, WithLeadingIcon, IconOnly, IconOnlyWithTooltip, Disabled, DisabledPressed, KeyboardToggle, Controlled, LongLabel, RightToLeft, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Label: a short noun or verb in sentence case ("Bold", "Show archived"). |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Node before the label, usually `<Icon size="sm" />`. Decorative; the label names the toggle. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Replaces the accessible name when the visible label is not enough. Rarely needed. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the toggle. |
| `icon` | `LucideIcon` |  |  | The icon to draw: one of the curated set (for example `StarIcon`). Decorative inside the button. |
| `label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name of an icon-only toggle, required. Name what the toggle controls, not what it looks like and not its state ("Bold", "Show archived"): the pressed state is announced separately. |
| `tooltip` | `boolean \| ToggleTooltipOptions` |  |  | Shows `label` in a `Tooltip` on hover and keyboard focus. Pass `true`, or an object to add a shortcut or change the side. The `label` stays the accessible name. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  | Inside a `ToggleGroup`: the value of this toggle in the group's `value` (required there, unique in the group). Standalone: the DOM id. |
| `variant` | `'secondary' \| 'ghost'` |  |  | Visual style, as for `Button`. `secondary` (default) has a border; `ghost` has none at rest. Inside a `ToggleGroup` it defaults to the group's `variant`. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  |  | Height token: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px. Inside a `ToggleGroup` it defaults to the group's `size`. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` |  |  | Ref to the underlying `<button>` element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaBaseButtonProps` (react-aria): `aria-controls`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-pressed`, `preventFocusOnPress`
- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `ButtonProps` (react-aria): `isDisabled`
- From `FocusableDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `excludeFromTabOrder`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `HoverEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onHoverChange`, `onHoverEnd`, `onHoverStart`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `PressEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onClick`, `onPress`, `onPressChange`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressStart`, `onPressUp`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- From `ToggleButtonProps` (react-aria): `defaultSelected`, `isSelected`, `onChange`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `variant`: `secondary`, `ghost`
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-body`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-body`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-space-5`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- One independent on/off choice in a toolbar or filter bar: Bold, Show archived, Only mine.
- An icon-only on/off control (Favorite, Pin) with a required `label`.

#### When not to use

- A setting that is saved with a form: use `Switch` or `Checkbox`.
- Several related toggles that share a value: use `ToggleGroup`.
- One value out of a few options (View: List, Board): use `SegmentedControl`.
- An action that does something once: use `Button`.

#### Anatomy

```
button[aria-pressed]
  leading   (optional, decorative)
  label     (or a single icon when icon-only)
```

#### Accessibility

- Semantics: `<button aria-pressed="true|false">`. Inside a single-selection `ToggleGroup` it is a `radio` with `aria-checked`.
- Keyboard: `Tab` focuses; `Space` and `Enter` toggle.
- The pressed state is shown by a brighter border, a raised fill and ink text, never by color alone. Focus is the accent border and ring.
- Icon-only toggles need a `label` that names what the toggle controls, not its state: the pressed state is announced by the browser. The icon is decorative.
- Targets are at least 32px (`sm`). Forced colors: the pressed toggle gets a `Highlight` border and an underline.

#### Content rules

- Label with a short noun or verb phrase in sentence case: "Bold", "Show archived". Do not change the label when the state changes ("Hide archived" would be read as the opposite of the state).

#### Examples

```tsx
<Toggle isSelected={showArchived} onChange={setShowArchived}>
  Show archived
</Toggle>

<Toggle icon={StarIcon} label="Favorite" tooltip variant="ghost" />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Switch: A setting that is saved with a form: use `Switch` or `Checkbox`.
- Instead, see Checkbox: A setting that is saved with a form: use `Switch` or `Checkbox`.
- Instead, see ToggleGroup: Several related toggles that share a value: use `ToggleGroup`.
- Instead, see SegmentedControl: One value out of a few options (View: List, Board): use `SegmentedControl`.
- Instead, see Button: An action that does something once: use `Button`.
- Renders: Icon, Tooltip
- Used by: ResponseFeedback

### ToggleGroup

> A row (or column) of related `Toggle`s that share one value: the list of pressed `id`s.

With the default `multiple` selection the toggles are independent (bold, italic, underline;
or a set of filters) and the group is a `toolbar`. With `single` selection it behaves like
a radio group that can also be empty.

`ToggleGroup` vs `SegmentedControl`: a `SegmentedControl` is one value of one setting (View:
List, Board), exactly one option is always selected. A `ToggleGroup` is a set of on/off
choices where none, one or several are on.

Built on React Aria `ToggleButtonGroup`: one tab stop, arrow keys move between toggles (they
stop at the ends), `Space` and `Enter` toggle the focused one.

A row (or column) of related `Toggle`s that share one value: the list of pressed `id`s. With the default `multiple` selection the toggles are independent (bold, italic, underline; a set of filters). With `single` selection at most one is pressed. Built on React Aria `ToggleButtonGroup`.

- TODO `GAP-005`.

- Import: `import { ToggleGroup } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/ToggleGroup/ToggleGroup.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/ToggleGroup`): Default, Preselected, Ghost, Small, Large, Vertical, IconOnly, SingleSelection, DisabledToggle, DisabledGroup, KeyboardSelection, Controlled, Wrapping, RightToLeft, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The `Toggle` children. Each needs an `id` that is unique in the group. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name of the group ("Text formatting"). Required: name this or use `aria-labelledby`. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the group. |
| `selectionMode` | `'single' \| 'multiple'` |  | `'multiple'` | `multiple` (default): any number of toggles can be pressed, independently (text formatting, filters); the group is a toolbar. `single`: at most one is pressed; the group is a radio group. To pick exactly one value of a setting prefer `SegmentedControl`. |
| `value` | `readonly string[]` |  |  | The `id`s of the pressed toggles (controlled). Pair with `onChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `readonly string[]` |  |  | The `id`s of the toggles that start pressed (uncontrolled). |
| `onChange` | `(value: string[]) => void` |  |  | Called with the `id`s of all pressed toggles after the user presses or releases one. |
| `disallowEmptySelection` | `boolean` |  |  | Keeps at least one toggle pressed. Pointless in `multiple` mode unless you want that rule. |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` |  | `'horizontal'` | Layout and arrow keys: `horizontal` (default, `←` `→`) or `vertical` (`↑` `↓`). |
| `variant` | `'secondary' \| 'ghost'` |  |  | Visual style handed down to every `Toggle` that does not set its own. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  |  | Size handed down to every `Toggle` that does not set its own. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the group element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `ToggleGroupProps` (react-stately): `isDisabled`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `variant`: `secondary`, `ghost`
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-space-2`

#### ToggleGroup or SegmentedControl

|           | `SegmentedControl`                           | `ToggleGroup`                                                    |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Meaning   | One value of one setting (View: List, Board) | Independent on/off choices (Bold, Italic; filters)               |
| Selection | Exactly one option, always                   | None, one or several (`multiple`), or none/one                   |
| Role      | `radiogroup` of `radio`                      | `toolbar` of `button[aria-pressed]` (`radiogroup` when `single`) |
| Value     | `string`                                     | `string[]`                                                       |
| Content   | `options` array with optional counts         | `Toggle` children, text or icon-only                             |

Rule of thumb: if choosing one option makes the others "not selected" and one must always be on, use `SegmentedControl`. If each choice can stand alone, use `ToggleGroup`. Use `single` here only when "nothing selected" is meaningful (for example an optional filter).

#### When to use

- Text formatting (Bold, Italic), list markers, or a small set of filters that combine.

#### When not to use

- A single on/off choice: use `Toggle`.
- Choosing one value of a setting: use `SegmentedControl`.
- A long list of filters: use `CheckboxGroup` or a `Select`/`Combobox` with multiple selection.

#### Anatomy

```
div[role=toolbar] aria-label       (or role=radiogroup when single)
  button[aria-pressed]             (one `Toggle` per choice, each with an id)
```

#### Accessibility

- Semantics: `multiple` is a `toolbar` (a group of buttons with `aria-pressed`); `single` is a `radiogroup` of `radio` buttons. The group needs an accessible name (enforced by the types).
- Keyboard: one tab stop; `←` / `→` (`↑` / `↓` when vertical) move focus and stop at the ends (React Aria does not wrap); `Space` and `Enter` press the focused toggle. Disabled toggles are skipped.
- Pressed state is shown by border, fill and ink text, not by color alone.
- Icon-only toggles need a `label`.

#### Content rules

- Group name: a noun phrase ("Text formatting", "Filters"). Toggle labels: one word or a short phrase in sentence case.

#### Examples

```tsx
<ToggleGroup aria-label="Text formatting" value={marks} onChange={setMarks}>
  <Toggle id="fav" icon={StarIcon} label="Favorite" />
  <Toggle id="pin" icon={StarIcon} label="Pinned" />
</ToggleGroup>

<ToggleGroup aria-label="Order filters" defaultValue={['mine']}>
  <Toggle id="mine">Only mine</Toggle>
  <Toggle id="late">Late</Toggle>
</ToggleGroup>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Toggle: A single on/off choice: use `Toggle`.
- Instead, see SegmentedControl: Choosing one value of a setting: use `SegmentedControl`.
- Instead, see CheckboxGroup: A long list of filters: use `CheckboxGroup` or a `Select`/`Combobox` with multiple selection.
- Instead, see Select: A long list of filters: use `CheckboxGroup` or a `Select`/`Combobox` with multiple selection.
- Instead, see Combobox: A long list of filters: use `CheckboxGroup` or a `Select`/`Combobox` with multiple selection.

### ToolCallList

> The steps of a multi-step agent run as an ordered list of `ToolCallStep`. Use it under the
message the run belongs to; each step opens its own details.

One step of an agent run: the tool it called, whether it is running, succeeded or failed, how long it took and, on request, what went in and out. `ToolCallList` shows a multi-step run. Import both from `loui-ds/patterns`.

- Import: `import { ToolCallList } from 'loui-ds/patterns';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/patterns/ToolCallStep/ToolCallList.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Patterns/ToolCallStep`): Default, Running, Failed, Expanded, WithoutDetails, LongName, RightToLeft, MultiStepRun

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `readonly ToolCallListStep[]` | yes |  | The steps of the run, in the order they happened. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name of the list. Defaults to "Steps"; say which run it is ("Steps of the order check"). |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ running: string; succeeded: string; failed: string; input: string; output: string; error: string; finishedSucceeded: (name: string) => string; finishedFailed: (name: string) => string; listLabel: string; }>` |  |  | Override the built-in messages for this instance (also applied to every step). |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ ToolCallStep: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `running` | `Running` | Visible status text of a step. |
| `succeeded` | `Succeeded` |  |
| `failed` | `Failed` |  |
| `input` | `Input` | Labels of the detail blocks, and the accessible names of their code blocks. |
| `output` | `Output` |  |
| `error` | `Error` | Label of the output block when the step failed. |
| `finishedSucceeded(name: string)` | `{name} succeeded` | Polite announcement when a running step finishes. |
| `finishedFailed(name: string)` | `{name} failed` |  |
| `listLabel` | `Steps` | Accessible name of a ToolCallList. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-danger-line`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-surface-row-hover`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-tool-call-step-gap`, `--ds-tool-call-step-list-gap`, `--ds-tool-call-step-padding-block`, `--ds-tool-call-step-padding-inline`, `--ds-tracking-caption`

#### When to use

- Under an assistant message, to show what the agent did before it answered ("search_orders", "draft_reply").
- A run log where the owner wants to check why the agent answered as it did.

#### When not to use

- Progress of a long job with a known number of steps: use `StatusSteps` or `Progress`.
- Something the owner has to approve: use `ApprovalCard`.

#### Anatomy

```
div (ToolCallStep)
  h{headingLevel} > button   chevron · status icon + text · name (mono) · duration (mono)
  details (when open)        "Input" label + code block · "Output" or "Error" label + code block
  status                     visually hidden live region
ol (ToolCallList)            one li per step
```

Without `input` and `output` the header is plain text and there is nothing to open.

#### Accessibility

- The header is a button inside a heading (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`); `Enter` and `Space` toggle it.
- Color never carries the status: the text "Running", "Succeeded" or "Failed" is always visible, with an icon.
- When a running step finishes, a polite live region says "search_orders succeeded" or "search_orders failed" once. A step that is already finished on first render is silent.
- Code blocks that overflow become labelled, keyboard-scrollable regions ("Input", "Output", "Error").
- Reduced motion and forced colors are handled.

#### Content rules

- Tool names are identifiers: show them as the agent calls them, in mono.
- Put the error text in `output` when a step fails, and say how to fix it when you can.
- Do not put secrets, tokens or customer data in `input` or `output`.

#### Example

```tsx
<ToolCallList
  aria-label="Steps of the order check"
  steps={[
    {
      stepId: 's1',
      name: 'search_orders',
      status: 'succeeded',
      durationMs: 1240,
      input: '{ "customer": "C-204" }',
      output: '{ "count": 3 }',
    },
    { stepId: 's2', name: 'draft_reply', status: 'running' },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see StatusSteps: Progress of a long job with a known number of steps: use `StatusSteps` or `Progress`.
- Instead, see Progress: Progress of a long job with a known number of steps: use `StatusSteps` or `Progress`.
- Instead, see ApprovalCard: Something the owner has to approve: use `ApprovalCard`.

### ToolCallStep

> One step of an agent run: the tool it called, whether it is running, succeeded or failed, how
long it took and, on request, what went in and out.

With `input` or `output` the header is a button that opens the details (`aria-expanded`,
`aria-controls`), inside a heading so the steps appear in the outline. Without them it is
plain text. The status is text plus an icon, never color alone. When a running step finishes,
a polite live region says so once; a step that is already finished on first render is silent.

One step of an agent run: the tool it called, whether it is running, succeeded or failed, how long it took and, on request, what went in and out. `ToolCallList` shows a multi-step run. Import both from `loui-ds/patterns`.

- Import: `import { ToolCallStep } from 'loui-ds/patterns';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/patterns/ToolCallStep/ToolCallStep.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Patterns/ToolCallStep`): Default, Running, Failed, Expanded, WithoutDetails, LongName, RightToLeft, MultiStepRun

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | Name of the tool or step ("search_orders"). Shown in mono; it is the name of the details button. |
| `status` | `'running' \| 'succeeded' \| 'failed'` | yes |  | `running` (spinner), `succeeded` or `failed`. The status is always shown as text next to its icon. |
| `durationMs` | `number` |  |  | How long the step took, in milliseconds. Omit while it is running. |
| `input` | `ReactNode` |  |  | What the tool was called with. A string is shown in a code block; pass nodes for anything richer. With `input` or `output` the step gets a details button. |
| `output` | `ReactNode` |  |  | What the tool returned, or the error text when `status` is `failed`. Same rules as `input`. |
| `isExpanded` | `boolean` |  |  | Controlled state of the details. |
| `defaultExpanded` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Initial state of the details when uncontrolled. Default closed. |
| `onExpandedChange` | `(isExpanded: boolean) => void` |  |  | Called when the details open or close. |
| `headingLevel` | `'1' \| '2' \| '3' \| '4' \| '5' \| '6'` |  | `'4'` | Heading level of the step header (`h1` to `h6`). Default `4`. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ running: string; succeeded: string; failed: string; input: string; output: string; error: string; finishedSucceeded: (name: string) => string; finishedFailed: (name: string) => string; listLabel: string; }>` |  |  | Override the built-in messages for this instance. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ ToolCallStep: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `running` | `Running` | Visible status text of a step. |
| `succeeded` | `Succeeded` |  |
| `failed` | `Failed` |  |
| `input` | `Input` | Labels of the detail blocks, and the accessible names of their code blocks. |
| `output` | `Output` |  |
| `error` | `Error` | Label of the output block when the step failed. |
| `finishedSucceeded(name: string)` | `{name} succeeded` | Polite announcement when a running step finishes. |
| `finishedFailed(name: string)` | `{name} failed` |  |
| `listLabel` | `Steps` | Accessible name of a ToolCallList. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-danger-line`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-surface-row-hover`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-tool-call-step-gap`, `--ds-tool-call-step-list-gap`, `--ds-tool-call-step-padding-block`, `--ds-tool-call-step-padding-inline`, `--ds-tracking-caption`

#### When to use

- Under an assistant message, to show what the agent did before it answered ("search_orders", "draft_reply").
- A run log where the owner wants to check why the agent answered as it did.

#### When not to use

- Progress of a long job with a known number of steps: use `StatusSteps` or `Progress`.
- Something the owner has to approve: use `ApprovalCard`.

#### Anatomy

```
div (ToolCallStep)
  h{headingLevel} > button   chevron · status icon + text · name (mono) · duration (mono)
  details (when open)        "Input" label + code block · "Output" or "Error" label + code block
  status                     visually hidden live region
ol (ToolCallList)            one li per step
```

Without `input` and `output` the header is plain text and there is nothing to open.

#### Accessibility

- The header is a button inside a heading (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`); `Enter` and `Space` toggle it.
- Color never carries the status: the text "Running", "Succeeded" or "Failed" is always visible, with an icon.
- When a running step finishes, a polite live region says "search_orders succeeded" or "search_orders failed" once. A step that is already finished on first render is silent.
- Code blocks that overflow become labelled, keyboard-scrollable regions ("Input", "Output", "Error").
- Reduced motion and forced colors are handled.

#### Content rules

- Tool names are identifiers: show them as the agent calls them, in mono.
- Put the error text in `output` when a step fails, and say how to fix it when you can.
- Do not put secrets, tokens or customer data in `input` or `output`.

#### Example

```tsx
<ToolCallList
  aria-label="Steps of the order check"
  steps={[
    {
      stepId: 's1',
      name: 'search_orders',
      status: 'succeeded',
      durationMs: 1240,
      input: '{ "customer": "C-204" }',
      output: '{ "count": 3 }',
    },
    { stepId: 's2', name: 'draft_reply', status: 'running' },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see StatusSteps: Progress of a long job with a known number of steps: use `StatusSteps` or `Progress`.
- Instead, see Progress: Progress of a long job with a known number of steps: use `StatusSteps` or `Progress`.
- Instead, see ApprovalCard: Something the owner has to approve: use `ApprovalCard`.
- Renders: Code, Icon, Spinner, VisuallyHidden

### Tooltip

> An ink-style hint for a control, built on React Aria `TooltipTrigger` and `Tooltip`.

It opens on hover (after a delay) and on keyboard focus, closes with `Escape` (WCAG 1.4.13),
stays open while the pointer is over it, and describes the trigger through `aria-describedby`.
A tooltip is a supplement: the trigger must already have its own accessible name.

A short, ink-style hint for a control. Built on React Aria `TooltipTrigger` and `Tooltip`.

- Handoff source: `components/feedback/Tooltip` (CMP-FBK-04).

- Import: `import { Tooltip } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Tooltip/Tooltip.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Tooltip`): Default, Open, WithShortcut, Bottom, Start, End, LongText, OnIconButton, Disabled

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` | yes |  | The element the tooltip describes. It must be focusable and built on React Aria, such as `Button`, `IconButton` or `Link`, so the tooltip opens on keyboard focus as well as hover. |
| `content` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Short text, a few words. It is linked to the trigger with `aria-describedby`, so it must add detail only: never put the only copy of essential information in a tooltip, because touch users cannot hover and the text is not shown until the trigger is focused. |
| `shortcut` | `string` |  |  | Keyboard shortcut shown after the text in mono type ("⌘K"). Pair it with `aria-keyshortcuts` on the trigger. |
| `placement` | `'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'start' \| 'end'` |  | `'top'` | Side of the trigger, `top` by default. `start` and `end` follow the writing direction. |
| `delay` | `number` |  | `500` | Milliseconds before opening on hover. Default 500. Focus opens it immediately. |
| `closeDelay` | `number` |  | `0` | Milliseconds before closing after the pointer leaves. Default 0. |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean` |  |  | Never opens when `true`, for example while the trigger is disabled. |
| `isOpen` | `boolean` |  |  | Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  |  | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(isOpen: boolean) => void` |  |  | Called when the tooltip opens or closes. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the tooltip bubble. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the tooltip bubble. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-primary-bg`, `--ds-primary-fg`, `--ds-primary-fg-muted`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-tooltip-max-width`, `--ds-weight-medium`, `--ds-weight-regular`

#### When to use

- Name or add a shortcut to an icon-only control ("Add order", with `N`).
- Explain a truncated label, in a few words.

#### When not to use

- Essential information (an error, a requirement, a price). **A tooltip is never the only source of essential information**: touch users cannot hover, and the text is not shown until the trigger is focused or hovered.
- Interactive content (links, buttons, forms): use `Popover`.
- A long explanation: put it in the page, or use a `Popover`.

#### Anatomy

```
TooltipTrigger
  trigger            Button | IconButton | Link   (focusable, React Aria based)
  Tooltip            role=tooltip, primary background, label type, radius sm
    content          text
    shortcut         optional, mono caption, --ds-primary-fg-muted
```

#### Accessibility

- Role `tooltip`, linked to the trigger with `aria-describedby` while open. The trigger keeps its own accessible name.
- Opens on **keyboard focus and hover**, closes on blur, pointer leave or `Escape` (WCAG 1.4.13: dismissible). The pointer can move onto the tooltip without closing it (hoverable), and it stays until dismissed (persistent).
- Placement is collision-aware.
- Contrast: `--ds-primary-fg` on `--ds-primary-bg`; the shortcut uses `--ds-primary-fg-muted` (at least 4.5:1 on the ink surface).
- Reduced motion: the 150 ms fade is disabled. Forced colors: a `CanvasText` border is drawn.
- Layer: `--ds-z-tooltip`, the top of the stack.

#### Content rules

- Sentence case, no final period for a fragment, no exclamation marks.
- Do not repeat a visible label; add the shortcut or the missing detail.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Add order" shortcut="N">
  <IconButton label="Add order" icon={PlusIcon} />
</Tooltip>
```

`IconButton` also takes a `tooltip` prop that does this for you.

#### Related components

- Instead, see Popover: Interactive content (links, buttons, forms): use `Popover`.
- Used by: IconButton, Toggle

### TopBar

> The page header: a title with an optional subtitle, or a breadcrumb trail, and an actions
slot. It is a `header` element, `--ds-topbar-h` (64px) high, with a bottom divider. It does
not stick by itself; position it in your layout.

The page header: a title with an optional subtitle, or a breadcrumb trail, and a slot for actions. A `header` element, 64px high (`--ds-topbar-h`), with a bottom divider.

- Handoff source: `components/layout/TopBar.jsx` (TODO `CMP-LAY-02`).

- Import: `import { TopBar } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/TopBar/TopBar.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/TopBar`): Default, WithSubtitle, WithPrimaryAction, WithContent, WithBreadcrumb, HeadingLevel2, LongTitle, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  |  | The title of the page or section. Rendered as a heading (see `headingLevel`). Ignored when `breadcrumb` is set: the trail then names the page and the page supplies its own `h1`. |
| `subtitle` | `ReactNode` |  |  | One short line under the title (a count, a date, an environment). Not used with `breadcrumb`. |
| `headingLevel` | `'1' \| '2' \| '3' \| '4' \| '5' \| '6'` |  | `'1'` | Heading level of the title, `1` by default (one `h1` per page). |
| `breadcrumb` | `readonly BreadcrumbItem[]` |  |  | A breadcrumb trail shown instead of the title. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Free content next to the title, for example a `Badge` or a `SegmentedControl`. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Actions at the end of the bar. Put the single primary action of the screen last, as a `Button variant="primary"` with its shortcut as a `Kbd` in `trailing`. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-bg`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-heading`, `--ds-fs-meta`, `--ds-lh-heading`, `--ds-lh-meta`, `--ds-line-subtle`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-top-bar-padding-inline`, `--ds-topbar-h`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- At the top of the content area of an app shell, next to the `Sidebar`.
- To hold the single primary action of the screen, at the top right, with its keyboard shortcut.

#### When not to use

- For the heading of a card or section: use `Card` or a heading.
- For a floating or sticky toolbar: position this component in your layout instead.

#### Accessibility

- A `header` that is not inside `main`, `section` or `article` is the page's banner landmark. Use at most one banner per page; inside a section it is a plain group.
- The title is a real heading. A breadcrumb replaces it, so keep a page-level `h1` elsewhere in that case.
- The title wins the space: content next to it (`children`, such as badges) wraps to a second line before the title truncates, and the bar grows taller. A title truncates with an ellipsis only when it alone is wider than the bar. The actions never shrink or move out of the bar; on narrow screens keep the primary action and put the others in a `Menu`.
- The primary action is a `Button variant="primary"` with its shortcut as a `Kbd` in `trailing`. Register the shortcut with `useHotkey`; `Kbd` only displays it.
- Height is a minimum, so a 200% text zoom grows the bar instead of clipping it.

#### Content rules

- Titles are nouns in sentence case ("Orders"). Subtitles give context: a count, a date, an environment.
- One primary action per screen, a verb plus object: "Create order".

#### Examples

```tsx
<TopBar
  title="Orders"
  subtitle="1,248 orders"
  actions={
    <Button variant="primary" trailing={<Kbd keys={['N']} />}>
      Create order
    </Button>
  }
/>

<TopBar breadcrumb={[{ label: 'Orders', href: '/orders' }, { label: 'ORD-1048' }]} />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Card: For the heading of a card or section: use `Card` or a heading.
- Renders: Breadcrumb

### Tour

> A step-by-step onboarding tour. Each step is a non-modal popover (React Aria `Popover` with
`isNonModal`) anchored to an element, with a title, a short text, a "Step 2 of 5" counter and
Skip, Back and Next or Done buttons. The page stays interactive; there is no scrim.

Focus moves into each step as it appears (the step is a named dialog, so a screen reader
announces its title). `Escape` skips the tour. When the tour ends, focus returns to the element
that had it before the tour opened, normally the button that started it.

Use a `Tooltip` for a hint on one control, and a `Popover` for interactive content. A tour is
for a few steps shown once; do not use it to hold documentation.

Step-by-step onboarding hints anchored to elements of the page. Each step is a non-modal popover (React Aria `Popover` with `isNonModal`) with a title, a short text, a "Step 2 of 5" counter and Skip, Back and Next or Done buttons. Generic: it lives in the core entry point.

- Import: `import { Tour } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Tour/Tour.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Tour`): Default, FirstStep, MiddleStep, LastStep, AboveTarget, KeyboardOnly

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `readonly TourStep[]` | yes |  | The steps, in order. Each points at one element through `target`. |
| `step` | `number` |  |  | Zero-based index of the current step (controlled). Pair with `onStepChange`. |
| `defaultStep` | `number` |  | `0` | Initial step when uncontrolled. Default `0`. |
| `onStepChange` | `(step: number) => void` |  |  | Called when the user moves to another step. |
| `isOpen` | `boolean` |  |  | Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(isOpen: boolean) => void` |  |  | Called with `false` when the tour is finished or skipped. |
| `onComplete` | `() => void` |  |  | Called when the user presses Done on the last step. `onOpenChange(false)` follows. |
| `onSkip` | `() => void` |  |  | Called when the user skips the tour, with `Skip tour` or `Escape`. `onOpenChange(false)` follows. |
| `placement` | `'bottom' \| 'bottom left' \| 'bottom right' \| 'bottom start' \| 'bottom end' \| 'top' \| 'top left' \| 'top right' \| 'top start' \| 'top end' \| 'left' \| 'left top' \| 'left bottom' \| 'start' \| 'start top' \| 'start bottom' \| 'right' \| 'right top' \| 'right bottom' \| 'end' \| 'end top' \| 'end bottom'` |  | `'bottom start'` | Side and alignment relative to the target. Default `bottom start`. Flips on collision. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ progress: (current: number, total: number) => string; back: string; next: string; done: string; skip: string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the step surface. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  | Ref to the step surface. |

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Tour: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `progress(current: number, total: number)` | `Step 2 of 2` | Progress text of a step, such as "Step 2 of 5". |
| `back` | `Back` | Goes to the previous step. |
| `next` | `Next` | Goes to the next step. |
| `done` | `Done` | Finishes the tour on the last step. |
| `skip` | `Skip tour` | Ends the tour before the last step. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-heading`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-heading`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-tour-arrow-size`, `--ds-tour-padding`, `--ds-tour-width`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- Guiding new users through the interface with a few onboarding hints (three to six steps) that introduce a screen.
- Pointing at controls that are not obvious from their label.

#### When not to use

- A hint on one control: `Tooltip`.
- Interactive content anchored to a button (filters, a small form): `Popover`.
- Documentation or long explanations: link to help instead.
- A task the user must finish before going on: `Dialog` or `Sheet`.

#### Anatomy

```
Popover (non-modal, anchored to step.target, z popover, overlay shadow)
  OverlayArrow
  Dialog (role=dialog, named by the title)
    Heading        step title
    content        step text (--ds-text-2)
    footer         "Step 2 of 5" (mono) ... Skip tour (ghost) · Back · Next | Done (primary)
```

The primary button is Next, or Done on the last step. Skip is hidden on the last step, Back on the first.

#### Accessibility

- Each step is a `dialog` named by its title. It is non-modal: the page is not inert, there is no scrim, nothing is hidden from assistive technology.
- Focus moves into each step as it appears (the dialog itself, so a screen reader reads its title; the next `Tab` reaches Skip, Back and Next). Pressing Next or Back mounts the next step and moves focus to it, so focus never lands on a removed button.
- While a step is open, `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` cycle through the step's buttons (React Aria contains focus in the dialog); `Escape` skips the tour and is the keyboard way out. A pointer press elsewhere on the page does not end it, and the page stays visible and readable (no scrim, not inert).
- When the tour ends, focus returns to the element that had focus when the tour opened (normally the button that started it); for a tour that is open on first render, to the target of the current step if it is focusable. If the consumer closes a controlled tour from outside, focus is left where the user put it.
- The target is scrolled into view (`block: nearest`) when its step appears. The step is positioned against the target and flips when it does not fit; the arrow points at the target.
- The fade-in is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Visuals are calm: raised surface, strong line and the overlay shadow only; accent is used only for focus rings.
- Because the step is rendered in a portal, it comes last in the Tab order of the page: the user reaches it by the focus that moves into it, not by tabbing from the target.

#### Content rules

- Title: the name of the thing, in sentence case ("Filters"). Text: one or two sentences saying what it does, with no exclamation marks or emoji.
- Button labels come from the message catalog: Back, Next, Done, Skip tour.

#### Examples

```tsx
const search = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
const filters = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<>
  <Button onPress={() => setOpen(true)}>Start tour</Button>
  <Button ref={search}>Search</Button>
  <Button ref={filters}>Filters</Button>
  <Tour
    isOpen={open}
    onOpenChange={setOpen}
    steps={[
      { target: search, title: 'Search', content: 'Find any item by name or code.' },
      { target: filters, title: 'Filters', content: 'Narrow the list by status or date.' },
    ]}
  />
</>;
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Tooltip: A hint on one control: `Tooltip`.
- Instead, see Popover: Interactive content anchored to a button (filters, a small form): `Popover`.
- Instead, see Dialog: A task the user must finish before going on: `Dialog` or `Sheet`.
- Instead, see Sheet: A task the user must finish before going on: `Dialog` or `Sheet`.
- Renders: Button

### VisuallyHidden

> Hides content visually while keeping it available to assistive technology.
Use it for text alternatives that sighted users do not need.

Hides content visually while keeping it in the accessibility tree. It renders a `span` (or the element given by `as`) with the standard "screen reader only" clipping, so the text is read aloud and found by assistive technology but takes no space on screen.

- Import: `import { VisuallyHidden } from 'loui-ds';`
- Status: stable
- Source: `src/components/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Primitives/VisuallyHidden`): Default, AsHeading

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `ElementType` |  | `span` | Element to render. Defaults to `span`. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### When to use

- A text alternative for an icon-only control when a `label` prop is not available (for example the name of a custom control).
- A heading or landmark label that sighted users do not need because the layout already implies it.
- Extra context for a repeated link or button ("Edit" followed by a hidden "order ORD-1048").

#### When not to use

- To hide content from everyone: use the `hidden` attribute or conditional rendering.
- To hide content from assistive technology only: use `aria-hidden="true"`.
- For a skip link that appears on focus: use `SkipLink`.
- For text that sighted keyboard users need to see: render it visibly.

#### Anatomy

```
span.root   (or as="h2", "div", ...)
  clip: rect(0 0 0 0); position: absolute; 1px box; overflow: hidden
```

#### Accessibility

- The content stays in the accessibility tree and in the reading order; place it where it should be read.
- Do not put interactive elements inside: a focusable element that cannot be seen is a focus-visibility failure (WCAG 2.4.7).
- Write the text as you would write visible copy: sentence case, no emoji, no decorative punctuation.

#### Content rules

- Keep it short and specific ("Close dialog", not "Click here to close the dialog window").
- Do not repeat what the visible label already says.

#### Examples

```tsx
<button type="button">
  <span aria-hidden="true">x</span>
  <VisuallyHidden>Close dialog</VisuallyHidden>
</button>

<VisuallyHidden as="h2">Order summary</VisuallyHidden>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see SkipLink: For a skip link that appears on focus: use `SkipLink`.
- Used by: Alert, ApprovalCard, Banner, Chart, ChatPanel, CommandPalette, DataTable, FileUpload, Kbd, Legend, Link, MatrixGrid, NavItem, ResponseFeedback, SegmentedControl, ShortcutsHelp, StackedBar, StatusSteps, Stepper, Tab, TabList, TabPanel, Tabs, Textarea, Timeline, ToastRegion, ToolCallStep

---

## Hooks and utilities

> Hooks, locale-aware utilities and message helpers exported from `loui-ds`. Money is an integer in minor units with an ISO 4217 code (ADR-0006).

### Hooks

#### useControllableState

Controlled/uncontrolled state for the `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange`
convention (AGENTS.md section 9). Thin wrapper over react-stately's `useControlledState`,
which also warns in development when a component switches between modes.

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useControllableState({ value: props.value, defaultValue: props.defaultValue ?? '', onChange: props.onValueChange });
```

```ts
useControllableState<T>({ value, defaultValue, onChange, }: UseControllableStateOptions<T>): [T, (value: T) => void]
```

#### useDSLocale

Returns the active locale (BCP 47 tag) set by `DSProvider`; `en-US` without a provider.

```ts
useDSLocale(): string
```

#### useHotkey

Runs `handler` when a single key combo is pressed.

- `combo`: modifiers joined with `+` and one key, e.g. `Mod+K`, `Shift+/`, `Alt+N`, `Escape`.
  `Mod` is Command on macOS and Control elsewhere.
- Ignores events from editable fields (unless `allowInEditable`), IME composition,
  key auto-repeat (unless `allowRepeat`) and events another handler already prevented.

This is deliberately small. A shortcut registry with conflict detection and a help
overlay is a separate task (GAP-004).

```ts
useHotkey(combo: string, handler: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void, { enabled, scope, allowInEditable, allowRepeat, preventDefault, platform, }?: UseHotkeyOptions): void
```

#### useHotkeys

Registers keyboard shortcuts in the registry (see `HotkeyProvider`) for as long as the
component is mounted.

- `keys`: `Mod+K`, `F2`, `N`, `1`, `Shift+/`, `Escape`. `Mod` is Command on macOS and Control
  elsewhere.
- Ignores editable fields (`allowInEditable`), IME composition, auto-repeat (`allowRepeat`),
  events another handler already prevented and, for page-level shortcuts, focus inside an open
  dialog or menu (`allowInOverlay`).
- Only one named scope is active at a time (`useHotkeyScope`); shortcuts of other scopes wait.
- In development, registering the same combo twice in one scope logs a warning; the most
  recent registration wins.
- `description` and `group` make a shortcut appear in `useRegisteredHotkeys`, the
  command palette and `ShortcutsHelp`.

Handlers may close over props and state: the latest handler always runs. The array can be
created inline on each render.

```ts
useHotkeys(definitions: readonly HotkeyDefinition[]): void
```

#### useHotkeyScope

Makes `name` the active scope while the component is mounted (and `isActive`): shortcuts
registered with `scope: name` fire and `global` ones stop, until the component unmounts.
